author: mongrelion
body:
Problem triggered by configuring `type: openai` with a custom base URL for an API (e.g. OpenCode Go) that does not expose an OpenAI-compatible `/models` endpoint.

GoModel received HTML instead of JSON on discovery, failed to parse it, marked the provider "unhealthy", and discarded the explicitly configured model list entirely — even though those models work perfectly fine for chat completions. Oracle already had this fallback (PR #246), but every other OpenAI-compatible provider silently dropped configured models on discovery failure. This change makes them behave consistently with Oracle and respects the user's explicit model configuration as a reliability guarantee.

Value: providers that users have explicitly configured with a known list of working models no longer go "unhealthy" just because their upstream doesn't support the /models endpoint or returns an unexpected response shape. The fallback preserves any metadata returned by upstream when it is available, and degrades gracefully to bare model IDs otherwise. 

---

* refactor(openai-compatible): extract doListModels from ListModels so the new fallback logic reuses the same upstream call path; add a helper that deduplicates and trims configured model names for correctness.

* fix(openai-compatible): make CompatibleProvider.ListModels fall back to explicitly configured models when the upstream /models endpoint returns an error (including non-JSON responses such as HTML pages), so providers with pre-defined model lists stay usable even when discovery fails.

* fix(openai, openrouter, vllm): pass opts.Models through to CompatibleProviderConfig so these provider types benefit from the new fallback logic; Azure gets its own fallback in its custom ListModels method since it calls a different endpoint (/openai/models).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed model listing failures across Azure, OpenAI, OpenRouter, and vLLM providers. When the upstream model endpoint is unavailable or returns an error, the system now gracefully falls back to your configured models instead of failing completely. Non-critical issues are logged as warnings.

body:
## Summary

This PR improves one-click deployment robustness on cloud hosts where the primary NIC is not `eth0`, and makes CubeProxy certificate generation deterministic across restarts.

## Motivation

In AWS and other environments, the primary interface is often `ens5`/`enp*` instead of `eth0`.
The current one-click flow may assume `eth0`, which can lead to incorrect node networking config.

Also, CubeProxy cert generation relied on implicit mkcert CA location. Setting a stable `CAROOT` makes behavior more predictable in automated deployments.

## Changes

1. Add primary NIC detection in `deploy/one-click/lib/common.sh`
   - New `detect_primary_interface()`:
      - Prefer `CUBE_SANDBOX_ETH_NAME` when explicitly provided
      - Otherwise use default route interface
      - Fallback to first non-loopback up interface
   - Update `detect_node_ip()` to detect IPv4 from the detected primary NIC first, then fallback to first global IPv4.

2. Wire NIC detection into install flow in `deploy/one-click/install.sh`
   - Detect/export `CUBE_SANDBOX_ETH_NAME`
   - Persist it into one-click runtime env file
   - Patch `Cubelet/config/config.toml` (`eth_name = ...`) during install when value is available

3. Stabilize mkcert CA root in `deploy/one-click/scripts/one-click/up-cube-proxy.sh`
   - Set/export `CAROOT` default to `${TOOLBOX_ROOT}/cubeproxy/caroot`
   - Ensure `CAROOT` directory exists before cert generation

## Validation

- `bash -n` passed for all modified scripts
- Function smoke test:
   - `detect_primary_interface` returns host primary NIC
   - `detect_node_ip` returns expected IPv4

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible for environments already using `eth0`
- Users can still override NIC explicitly via `CUBE_SANDBOX_ETH_NAME`

author: theetaz
body:
> **Stacked on #23** (11-PR stack).

## Summary

Hardens the corpus CI gate. JSON Schema catches shape violations; this PR adds a second layer that catches **semantic** problems — cross-field invariants, authority-appropriate content, cross-record foreign keys, honest confidence scoring for analogy chunks. Also adds a non-fatal trilingual coverage report so CI visibly tracks translation progress.

## What the new gates catch

### Cultivation-plan gates
- ≥ 1 activity per plan (zero activities = not a plan)
- ≥ 1 pest_risk for any \`in_review\` / \`published\` plan (draft exempt)
- \`authority\` required
- \`source_document_url\` must be paired with \`source_document_title\` (otherwise UI renders "[unnamed source]")

### Knowledge-chunk gates
- \`source_slug\` must resolve to a committed \`knowledge_source\` fixture (cross-record FK — schema can't express this)
- \`body\` ≥ 50 characters
- Published \`doa_official\` / \`peer_reviewed\` chunks **require** a verbatim \`quote\` (traceability for claims that drive farmer recommendations)
- \`inferred_by_analogy\` chunks:
  - must declare \`confidence\` explicitly
  - **cap at 0.85** — no "near-certain" cross-regional claims
  - must carry a \`caveat\` in \`field_provenance\` (the whole point of the authority label)

## Trilingual coverage report

```
i18n coverage — cultivation_plans titles/summaries (12 plans):  en=12  si=12  ta=12
i18n coverage — knowledge_chunks body_translated (21 chunks):  en=6  si=6  ta=6
```

Non-fatal. Tells reviewers + PR authors exactly how far translation is from complete, without failing builds on partial coverage.

## Exit codes

- \`0\` — schema + quality gates pass (happy path)
- \`1\` — schema failures (unchanged behaviour)
- \`2\` — schema clean but quality-gate failures (**new**); makes CI log distinguish "data shape broken" from "data content shallow"

## Current state

\`python3 scripts/validate_corpus.py\` → \`✓ 292 records valid (schema + quality gates)\`

Every record already in the corpus passes. This PR is pure tightening; it doesn't break any existing fixture.

## Changement

Refactor du workflow unique en 4 jobs sequentiels, inspire de [remidesjardins/TP1_DevOps](https://github.com/remidesjardins/TP1_DevOps/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml).

## Structure

```
CI-1 Build --> CI-2 Tests --> CI-3 Qualite --> CI-4 Docker
                    |
                    v
            build/ en artifact (reutilise en CI-3)
```

- **CI-1 · Build** : `./gradlew clean assemble -x test` — fail fast si le code ne compile pas
- **CI-2 · Tests** : `./gradlew test jacocoTestReport` + upload de `build/` en artifact
- **CI-3 · Qualite** : download de `build/`, lance `./gradlew sonar -x test -x jacocoTestReport` (pas de re-execution des tests) + Codecov
- **CI-4 · Image Docker** : build final

## Bonus

- `concurrency` : annule les runs obsoletes sur la meme branche
- Retention des artifacts `build/` reduite a 1 jour (volumineux)

## Hors perimetre

- Pas de workflow `analyse-main.yml` separe (overkill pour un TP)
- Dockerfile inchange (tests toujours sur le host)

# fix(inpi): force role entrepreneur pour les EI [PLA-4455]

## ✅ Type of PR

- [x] Bug Fix

## 🗒️ Description

L'INPI expose parfois un champ `role` dans `entrepreneur.descriptionPersonne`
(ex `"99"`) qui **masquait** le rôle `ROLE_ENTREPRENEUR` (`"101"`) attendu
côté API pour les Entrepreneurs Individuels. Le mapping `CompanyMapper`
écrasait déjà ce rôle ; `InpiDataOutput` restait incohérent et renvoyait
la valeur brute de l'INPI.

Ce fix aligne `InpiDataOutput::processEntrepreneurForEI()` sur le
comportement déjà en place dans `CompanyMapper` : le rôle est forcé à
`ROLE_ENTREPRENEUR` avant construction du mandataire.

## 🚶‍➡️ Behavior

- Pour une EI, le mandataire exposé côté API porte **toujours** `role = "101"`, que l'INPI fournisse un `role` ou non dans `descriptionPersonne`.
- Aucun impact sur les formes juridiques non-EI (SARL, SAS, etc.) : leur rôle continue de provenir de `roleEntreprise`.
- Aucun changement de signature publique ni de schéma.

## 🧪 Steps to test

- [ ] Lancer la suite PHPUnit ciblée : `castor quality:phpunit --filter testItForcesEntrepreneurRoleForEIEvenWhenInpiProvidesOne`
- [ ] Sur un payload INPI réel — SIREN `431817741` — vérifier que le mandataire retourné a `role = "101"` (et non `"99"`)
- [ ] Vérifier qu'un appel INPI sur une SARL/SAS renvoie toujours le bon `roleEntreprise` (non-régression)

author: jfmeyers
body:
## Summary

Completes the wiring between the backend \`LookupDescriptor\` emitted on
\`FilterableField.lookup\` (granit-dotnet #1127 / PR 2) and the headless
\`useSmartFilter\` state machine. When a filterable field declares a lookup
source, the UI layer can now render \`<LookupPicker>\` (from #205 / PR 4)
instead of inline enum/boolean suggestions — no change required to the
caller other than the metadata itself.

Refs ADR-023. PR **5 of 7**.

## Changes

### \`@granit/query-engine\`

- \`FilterableField\` gains \`readonly lookup?: LookupDescriptor\`. Mirrors the
  .NET contract merged as granit-dotnet #1127 verbatim.
- New \`peerDependency\` on \`@granit/data-lookup\` (types only, zero runtime cost).

### \`@granit/react-query-engine\`

- \`useSmartFilter\` exposes \`selectedFieldLookup: LookupDescriptor | undefined\`
  in \`UseSmartFilterReturn\`. The consumer reads this to branch between the
  default suggestion list and \`<LookupPicker>\`.
- \`buildValueSuggestions\` short-circuits to \`[]\` when the selected field
  declares a lookup — the suggestion dropdown stays empty and the caller
  wires the picker directly.
- New \`peerDependency\` on \`@granit/data-lookup\`.

## Usage

Consumer (e.g., SmartFilterBar component in showcase-admin-react):

\`\`\`tsx
const {
  phase, selectedField, selectedFieldLookup, selectedOperator, confirmValue,
} = useSmartFilter({ metadata });

if (phase === 'enterValue' && selectedFieldLookup) {
  return (
    <LookupPicker
      descriptor={selectedFieldLookup}
      multi={selectedOperator === 'In'}
      onChange={(v) => confirmValue(String(v))}
      scope={formWatchedValues}
      client={axios}
      culture={i18n.resolvedLanguage}
      render={/* consumer UI */}
    />
  );
}
\`\`\`

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm -F @granit/query-engine exec tsc --noEmit\` + \`pnpm -F @granit/react-query-engine exec tsc --noEmit\` clean.
- [x] \`pnpm lint\` clean.
- [x] \`pnpm test --run packages/@granit/react-query-engine\` → **91 tests** (86 existing + **5 new**).
- [x] Zero regression across \`@granit/query-engine\`, \`@granit/data-lookup\`, \`@granit/react-data-lookup\` (98 tests total green).
- [x] \`pnpm -F @granit/query-engine build\` + \`pnpm -F @granit/react-query-engine build\` produce valid bundles.
- [ ] CI green.

## Dependencies

- **Depends on #205 (PR 4)** — base branch is \`feature/data-lookup-frontend-sdk\`
  so GitHub shows the incremental diff. Once #205 merges into \`develop\`, the
  base will auto-retarget to \`develop\`.
- Consumes \`LookupDescriptor\` types from \`@granit/data-lookup\` (PR 4).
- Consumes backend \`FilterableField.lookup\` from granit-dotnet #1127 (merged).

## Scope discipline

| ✅ In this PR | ❌ Deferred |
| --- | --- |
| \`FilterableField.lookup\` type + \`selectedFieldLookup\` hook surface | Showcase SmartFilterBar component wiring — out of this monorepo |
| 5 new unit tests | First backend adopters (Tenant/User/Meter \`.AsLookup\`) — PR 6 |
| Bypass of inline enum/boolean suggestions for lookup fields | \`<LookupSelect>\` migration in showcase edit forms — PR 7 |

author: megglos
body:
Closes #5.

## What lands here

Structural foundation for the library. No business logic yet — just the Maven layout, the hexagonal boundary enforcement, and the build infrastructure that every subsequent feature PR will land into.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `camunda-security-library` parent pom exists with `core`, `api`, `adapters` submodules
- [x] `./mvnw clean install` from repo root succeeds
- [x] ArchUnit test in `core` passes, and fails if `core` is made to import from `api` or `adapters` (fail case verified locally against a throwaway violating class before final commit)
- [x] No production Java classes exist in any submodule — only the ArchUnit test in `core/src/test/java`
- [x] JUnit 5, AssertJ, Mockito, ArchUnit are managed/available as test dependencies in every submodule

## Beyond the literal issue text

Additions discussed and agreed during planning / review:

1. **Automatic license header population.** Mirrors the camunda/camunda setup: full license at `licenses/CAMUNDA-LICENSE-1.0.txt` + root `LICENSE` for GitHub detection + `COPYING-HEADER.txt` template, applied automatically by `com.mycila:license-maven-plugin` bound to `process-sources`. The Camunda License 1.0 itself is declared in the parent POM's `<licenses>` block.
2. **CI workflow** (`.github/workflows/build.yml`). Runs `./mvnw --batch-mode --no-transfer-progress -T 1C clean verify` on push to `main` and on PRs. `-T 1C` runs one Maven thread per CPU core; every plugin we use (compiler, surefire, license, enforcer) is thread-safe. `verify` will pick up integration tests (failsafe) automatically when they land — no workflow change required.
3. **Dependency convergence enforcement** via `maven-enforcer-plugin` with the `dependencyConvergence` rule. Runs on every submodule during `validate`; catches transitive-version drift the moment it appears.
4. **Maven distribution hash pinning.** `.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties` declares `distributionSha256Sum` for `apache-maven-3.9.9-bin.zip`, so the wrapper refuses to launch if the fetched distribution doesn't match.

## Design notes

- **Parent POM at repo root**, no container directory. Matches the updated issue scope and the `./mvnw` convention.
- **Spring Boot 4.0.5** imported as a BOM (`<scope>import</scope>`), *not* inherited via `spring-boot-starter-parent`. This is a library, not an app — avoiding the parent keeps our `<build>` configuration ours.
- **Java 21 baseline.** Bounded by downstream consumers (Hub, OC).
- **Maven wrapper pinned to 3.9.9** via `.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties` + SHA-256 (see point 4 above).
- **Plugin activation pattern.** Both `license-maven-plugin` and `maven-enforcer-plugin` are fully configured once in the parent's `<pluginManagement>` (including their `<executions>`), then opted in by each submodule via a bare `<plugin>` reference. The aggregator POM itself never runs these plugins — only the three submodules do — which eliminates the concurrent-write race that would otherwise exist under `-T 1C` and avoids each source file being processed twice.
- **Consumer-facing single-artifact story** is deliberately deferred. A future `camunda-security-library-spring-boot-starter` module (already aspirational in `.claude/docs/architecture.md`) will be the "one dep, pulls everything" artifact for downstream consumers. Out of scope here.
- `DomainArchTest` uses `allowEmptyShould(true)` because ArchUnit's default fail-on-empty-match would trip while `core/src/main/java` is still empty. The rule starts biting the moment any production class lands.

## What's next

- #6 — inbound port interfaces
- #7 — outbound port interfaces
- #8 — deployment-strategy config + `@ConditionalOnProperty` wiring
- Later: `-spring-boot-starter` module for the consumer aggregation

## Summary
- The `helm-schema` pre-commit hook from `losisin/helm-values-schema-json@v2.3.1` now strictly requires the tool to be installed as a helm plugin and exits `1` otherwise. The shared `giantswarm/github` CI workflow installs it as a standalone `helm-schema` binary on PATH rather than as a helm plugin, so every pre-commit run on `main` and all open PRs has been failing.

author: quynhanh1706vp-byte
body:
TokenFromQuery was designed to let SSE/WS clients send the JWT via
?token= query param, with fallback to Authorization header and
X-API-Key. After PR #69 (client), PR #72 (WS dead fallback), and
PR #74 (netcap/stream + p4), no caller reaches it:

    $ grep -rn TokenFromQuery --include='*.go' .
    internal/auth/middleware.go:...  func TokenFromQuery(...)

Single match — the definition itself. Safe to delete.

Dead code of this shape is dangerous: it documents an insecure
pattern (query-string tokens), and a future refactor could wire it
back in without realizing the cost. Removing it closes that risk.

body:
Upstream changes into production branch

## Summary by Sourcery

Improve robustness and performance of Sekoia.io alert events threshold trigger and state management, and bump integration version.

Bug Fixes:
- Correct cleanup of never-triggered alerts so recent alerts are not removed prematurely.
- Ensure time-threshold triggers use fresh alert state and are skipped when alert info is missing or invalid.
- Fix retry and polling logic for Sekoia.io events search jobs so HTTP errors propagate correctly and timeouts are handled deterministically.
- Prevent unbounded growth and leakage of per-alert locks by using an LRU-bounded cache and purging locks for removed alerts.
- Ensure alerts without notification event counts are handled safely by defaulting to zero and deferring to time-threshold processing.
- Include custom_status and verdict fields in alert threshold events to avoid downstream KeyErrors.

Enhancements:
- Reduce S3 state reloads and logging noise in AlertStateManager and threshold trigger paths to improve performance.
- Refine alert threshold evaluation to rely primarily on notification metadata and simplify no-threshold-met handling.
- Tighten typing, method signatures, and internal helpers for alert threshold trigger and state manager.
- Adjust time-threshold background processing to always run state cleanup and to avoid duplicate thread creation.

Documentation:
- Update changelog with details of alert threshold robustness fixes and release Sekoia.io version 2.71.3.

Tests:
- Expand and adjust unit tests for alert threshold trigger, state manager cleanup, search job error handling, and lock behavior, including regression coverage for time and cleanup bugs.

author: vantatechca
body:
## Summary
Two root causes of false `OK` heartbeats:

1. **Screenshot taken while the page was still loading.** `domcontentloaded` + a flat 5s sleep isn't enough — the payment section is an iframe that hydrates late, and Shopify's Checkout Extensibility lazy-renders sections as you scroll.
2. **Claude Vision had no reference for what "healthy" or "broken" actually looks like** — just a bullet list of bad text patterns. It had no region-by-region checklist and no concrete examples, so it gave the page the benefit of the doubt when the payment area was still a skeleton.

## Changes

### `screenshot.js` — wait for the real checkout, not just the DOM
Replaces the 5s blind sleep with a proper multi-step wait:

1. `domcontentloaded`
2. Wait for **any** checkout-shell selector to appear (`form[action*="checkouts"]`, `#checkout-main`, `.step__sections`, `[data-checkout-rendered]`, etc.)
3. **Scroll through the whole page** in 400px increments to force lazy-rendered iframes and summary sections to hydrate, then scroll back to the top
4. Wait for a **payment-section selector** (`data-payment-section`, card-field iframe, Spreedly iframe, `#payment-method`, etc.)
5. Wait for a **pay-now button selector**
6. `waitForLoadState("networkidle")` — iframes finish their network work
7. Final 2.5s buffer for paint

If any individual wait times out, the run continues — we still take a screenshot — so this is fail-open, not fail-closed.

### `analyze.js` — give Claude a checklist and concrete examples
Rewrote the system prompt around three blocks:

1. **What a HEALTHY checkout looks like**, broken down by region (left column top→bottom: contact → delivery → shipping → **payment** → pay button; right column: order summary with currency)
2. **What a BROKEN checkout looks like — 7 concrete examples** with the exact short PROBLEM reply to return, including "payment section empty, only a spinner visible bottom left" and "no payment gateway available"
3. **How to inspect step-by-step**: region by region, asking (a) present? (b) fully rendered? (c) any error text? — with explicit instruction to spend extra attention on the payment section because that's where real failures show up and it's usually bottom-left

Bias toward reporting: "if in doubt, flag PROBLEM. A false alarm is cheap; a missed outage is expensive."

Kept the IGNORE list from PR #5 so draft-order noise doesn't come back. Bumped `max_tokens` to 120.

## Test plan

body:
## Summary

- New persistent `-o, --output` root flag (`text` default, `json`); rejects any other value before subcommand RunE fires
- JSON mode emits a single versioned envelope on stdout per invocation (`upgrade --all` emits NDJSON, one envelope per repo) with stable top-level keys: `schema_version`, `command`, `repo`, `apply`, `result`, `warnings`, `hints`
- Warnings (missing-secret, drift) and hints from the existing diagnostics layer dual-emit: structured entries in the envelope on stdout, zerolog events on stderr — humans tailing the run still see them live
- `template fetch`, `add`, and `status` reject `-o json` with a clear error rather than silently falling back to text
- Text mode (default) is byte-identical to pre-feature behavior; the only diff in `deploy`/`sync`/`upgrade` baselines is the random `/tmp/gh-aw-fleet-*` clone path, which was already non-deterministic
- Zero new dependencies — verified by `go mod graph` diff

## Test plan

- [x] `make ci` passes (fmt-check, vet, golangci-lint, full test suite)
- [x] 35+ new tests across `cmd/output_test.go`, `internal/fleet/diagnostics_test.go`, `internal/fleet/list_result_test.go`
- [x] Live verification on real fleet: `go run . list -o json | jq -e .schema_version` returns `1`; `go run . deploy rshade/gh-aw-fleet -o json` emits envelope with `missing_secret` warning; `go run . upgrade rshade/gh-aw-fleet -o json` emits envelope with `audit_json: null` and populated `changed_files`
- [x] `go mod graph` diff before/after is empty
- [x] Text-mode `list` output byte-identical to pre-feature baseline
- [x] Top-level envelope keys pinned by `TestEnvelope_TopLevelKeysPinned`
- [x] Empty slices marshal as `[]` for every result type via reflection-based regression test
- [ ] Live `--apply` against a real fleet repo with `-o json` — to be validated by the operator during a real deploy cycle

## Changes

### New files

- `cmd/output.go` — `Envelope`, `Diagnostic` constants, `writeEnvelope` / `writeEnvelopeTo`, `outputMode`, `validateOutputMode`, `rejectJSONMode`, `preResultFailureEnvelope`, `initSlices` reflection walker
- `cmd/output_test.go` — envelope shape, schema-version pin, flag validator, empty-array invariant, NDJSON line semantics, audit_json nesting, no-null-slices regression for all result types
- `internal/fleet/list_result.go` — `ListResult`, `ListRow`, `BuildListResult`
- `internal/fleet/list_result_test.go` — shape, empty config, engine-empty-not-dash
- `internal/fleet/diagnostics_test.go` — Diagnostic JSON shape, Hint codes snake_case, `CollectHintDiagnostics` dedup and non-nil-empty semantics
- `specs/003-cli-output-json/` — spec artifacts (plan, research, data model, quickstart, contracts, tasks, checklists)

### Modified files

- `cmd/root.go` — registers `--output` persistent flag; chains `validateOutputMode` into `PersistentPreRunE` after log-flag validation
- `cmd/list.go` — branches on `outputMode`; routes breadcrumb through `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` so JSON mode keeps stdout pure
- `cmd/deploy.go` — JSON branch; `emitDeployEnvelope` dual-emits warnings via factored `buildMissingSecretMessage` so envelope and zerolog text stay in sync
- `cmd/sync.go` — JSON branch; `emitSyncEnvelope` for drift and preflight diagnostics; preserves text-mode hint surface (DeployPreflight only)
- `cmd/upgrade.go` — JSON branch on single-repo path; `runUpgradeAllJSON` emits NDJSON streaming per-repo for `--all`; extracted `validateUpgradeArgs` / `runUpgradeAll` / `runUpgradeSingle` helpers to keep `RunE` readable
- `cmd/template.go`, `cmd/add.go`, `cmd/stubs.go` — reject `-o json` at top of RunE (FR-013)
- `internal/fleet/deploy.go` — JSON tags on `DeployResult` and `WorkflowOutcome`
- `internal/fleet/sync.go` — JSON tags on `SyncResult`
- `internal/fleet/upgrade.go` — JSON tags on `UpgradeResult`; `audit_json` is a `json.RawMessage` that nests as a native object (not a quoted string)
- `internal/fleet/diagnostics.go` — `Diagnostic` struct, stable code constants, `Code` field on `Hint`, parallel `CollectHintDiagnostics`
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased Added entry plus `### JSON envelope schema` section documenting the schema_version 1 contract
- `skills/fleet-deploy/SKILL.md`, `skills/fleet-eval-templates/SKILL.md`, `skills/fleet-upgrade-review/SKILL.md`, `skills/fleet-onboard-repo/SKILL.md` — one-line note that `-o json` is available; three-turn pattern unchanged

### Bug fixes surfaced during implementation

- `initSlices` was converting nil `json.RawMessage` (which is `[]byte`) to empty `[]byte{}`, causing `MarshalJSON` to fail with "unexpected end of JSON input" on every `upgrade -o json` invocation; fixed by skipping `[]byte` element kinds in the reflection walker
- `cmd/list.go` used `cmd.OutOrStderr()` for the breadcrumb, which despite the name returns the OUT writer (cobra naming quirk); switched to `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` so JSON-mode tests with `SetOut` don't leak the breadcrumb into the stdout buffer (production behavior unchanged)

Closes #25

Closes #58.

Part 4 of the \`refactor/april-2026\` course. Targets the intermediate branch; maintainer merges \`refactor/april-2026\` → \`main\` at the end.

## Change

Adds \`src/commands/commandHelpers.ts\` (15 LOC) with:

\`\`\`ts
export function commandRegistrar(context: vscode.ExtensionContext) {
  return (id: string, handler: CommandHandler) => {
    context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand(id, handler));
  };
}
\`\`\`

Each \`*Commands\` class now opens its registration method with:

\`\`\`ts
const register = commandRegistrar(this.context);
register('computor.x.y', handler);
register('computor.x.z', handler);
\`\`\`

Instead of 3-line wrappers per registration.

## Application

| File | Registrations |
|---|---|
| LecturerCommands | 41 |
| LecturerExampleCommands | 40 |
| TutorCommands | 16 |
| StudentCommands | 13 |
| StudentOfflineCommands | 7 |
| UserManagerCommands | 4 |
| LogoutCommands | 2 |
| LecturerFsCommands | 2 |
| SettingsCommands | 1 |
| SignUpCommands | 1 |
| UserPasswordCommands | 1 |
| **Total** | **128** |

The bulk was applied by a one-off Python script (not committed) that matched the exact \`this.context.subscriptions.push(\\n  vscode.commands.registerCommand(...)\\n);\` pattern and dedented bodies by the detected inner-indent width. Short-form and \`private registerCommands()\` edge cases were cleaned up by hand.

## Result

- Net ~−205 LOC (after helper)
- \`tsc --noEmit\`: clean
- \`npm run compile\` (webpack): clean
- \`npm run lint\`: no new warnings (eqeqeq / semi warnings present are all pre-existing in their respective lines)
- Zero behavior changes

## Deliberately out of scope

- No error-handling wrapper. Different commands have intentionally-different user-facing error messages; a one-size-fits-all wrapper would change UX. That's a separate discussion / branch.
- \`extension.ts\`'s standalone \`context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand(...))\` calls are left alone on this branch — they live outside a class method and would benefit from a slightly different helper shape. Candidate for a follow-up once auth-session + view-init branches are merged.
- \`src/types/generated/*\` untouched.

author: missingroberto
body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/1103
Fixes the flake in `TestIntegrationV1Beta1APIAvailable` and `TestIntegrationV1Beta1OpenAPISchema` reported in https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/1103.

## Root cause

`TestIntegrationV1Beta1RepositoryCRUD` creates a repo with `sync.enabled: true` and `sync.target: "folder"`. The background sync calls `EnsureFolderExists` (`pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/jobs/sync/full.go:53`) for the repository root folder with `Path: ""`. `SetSourceProperties` (`pkg/apimachinery/utils/meta.go:787`) *deletes* the `AnnoKeySourcePath` annotation when the path is empty — so the root folder ends up with a manager annotation but no source path.

There's then a race between the sync creating/indexing the root folder and the repo's `remove-orphan-resources` finalizer listing managed resources to delete. If the folder isn't yet visible to the lister, the finalizer misses it and the folder is leaked past repo deletion.

The next test runs `CleanupAllResources` as admin. Admin isn't the provisioning identity, so the folder delete routes through `handleManagedResourceRouting` (`pkg/storage/unified/apistore/managed.go:244`) which requires a non-empty source path — hence:

```
CleanupAllResources(folders): deleteAndWait: timed out with 1 items remaining
(first delete error: deleteAndWait: delete "test-v1beta1-repo":
managed resource is missing source path annotation)
```

## Fix

The test only exercises v1beta1 API CRUD serialization; it does not need sync. Disable sync to match the pattern used in `pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/apiversion/version_test.go:38`. No sync -> no root folder -> no race.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

The underlying issue — orphaned root folders (with empty source paths) being un-deletable by admin — still affects any repo using `sync.target: folder`. Worth a separate investigation.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on `pkg/tests/apis/provisioning/v1beta1/...` passes
- [ ] Flake no longer reproduces on the affected test matrix

body:
## Summary
Fixes the SystemSwitcher contrast + Carbon styling issues flagged in the screenshot this morning. The switcher uses Carbon's per-DS button classes (\`cb-btn-ghost\` / \`cb-btn-primary\`) which reference theme-scoped tokens (\`var(--cds-button-primary)\`, \`var(--cds-link-primary)\`) that Carbon's \`buildCSS\` emits under \`.cds--<themeKey>\` selectors. Without a matching ancestor class on the chrome, only the :root fallback fired — producing mismatched / muted colors.

## Fix
Conditionally apply \`className={\\\`cds--\${carbonThemeKey}\\\`}\` on the \`<header>\` element in \`DesignHubApp\` when \`isCarbon\` is true. The Carbon theme-scoped rules now resolve correctly for everything inside the header (SystemSwitcher, ThemeControls, future chrome icons).

Other DSs (Salt / M3 / Fluent / ausos) use \`:root\`-scoped tokens that \`<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML>\` already injects globally — no wrapper needed for those.

## Files changed
- \`src/components/DesignHubApp.tsx\` — 1 conditional className prop + a paragraph-long doc comment explaining why.

No store / registry / CSS changes. No new tokens.

## Gate checks
- \`npm run typecheck\` ✓ clean
- \`npm run test\` ⚠ local worker-pool timeout (laptop resource exhaustion during session); deferring to CI — my change is a single JSX prop addition, zero risk
- \`npm run tokens:audit\` ✓ 0-delta

## Manual verification (what you'll see when it's deployed)
- Active DS = Carbon: \`<header>\` has \`class=\"cds--g100\"\` (or whichever Carbon theme key). Inactive label colors use Carbon g100 link blue (\`#78a9ff\`, ~8.5:1 contrast), Carbon active button uses g100's \`--cds-button-primary\` (\`#4589ff\`), flat border-radius: 0 per Carbon spec.
- Switch to Salt / M3 / Fluent / ausos: header has no \`cds--*\` class, renders per its DS's :root-scoped tokens (unchanged behavior).

This pull request implements full backend integration for task completion and uncompletion in the projects feature. It introduces new use cases and repository methods for marking tasks as complete or incomplete, updates the UI for accessibility, and ensures error handling for network failures. **Backend integration for task completion/uncompletion:**

- Introduced new use cases: `CompleteTaskUseCase` and `UncompleteTaskUseCase`, which interact with the repository and handle errors, returning a `Result` type.

**Toggle task completion logic:**

- Refactored `ToggleTaskCompletionUseCase` to use the new repository methods, handle network errors, and return a `Result` type. Updated tests to verify backend calls and error handling.

**UI and accessibility improvements:**

- Updated the task completion checkbox in `task.component.html` and `task.component.css` to be more accessible, including visually hidden labels for screen readers and improved focus styles. The completion control now uses the `change` event for toggling.

- Updated the corresponding test to trigger the new event and verify correct task toggling.

author: guweigang
body:
## Summary

Treat a zero-byte read in `parse_frame_header()` as a peer-close condition
instead of continuing the read loop.

## Why

A `read_bytes == 0` result indicates EOF or peer closure. Continuing the loop
can delay close propagation and leave websocket state waiting unnecessarily.

Returning an error here makes connection shutdown behavior more explicit and
better aligned with socket EOF semantics.

author: tcapelle
body:
## Hypothesis

The current TF champion (PR #3140) uses `--residual-prediction` as part of a full physics stack (asinh-pressure, TE coord frame, Cp panel, pressure-prior-addition). No experiment has yet tested `--residual-prediction` **alone** — stripped of all other physics flags. This is the missing noam ablation.

If residual-prediction alone can beat the baseline (val=21.350), it simplifies the stack and confirms it as a standalone driver of improvement. If it requires the compound physics stack, that tells us something important about feature interactions.

In-flight experiments do **not** cover this gap: chopper=#3180 (ANP), fern=#3185 (full noam stack), norman=#3186 (T_max=150), emma=#3189 (asinh+physics). This is a clean single-variable ablation.

## Instructions

**Please run a 3-epoch smoke test of Trial 1 first. Report `val_primary/surface_pressure_mae` before continuing.**

### Trial 1 — Residual-prediction alone (smoke test first, then full run)

**Step 1: 3-epoch smoke test**
```bash
cd target/icml2026 && python train.py --dataset tandemfoil --optimizer lion --lr 1.25e-4 --cosine-t-max 10 --grad-clip 0.3 --weight-decay 1e-2 --enable-fourier --model-layers 3 --model-hidden-dim 192 --model-heads 3 --epochs 3 --ema-decay 0.999 --residual-prediction --wandb_group tf-residual-pred
```

Report `val_primary/surface_pressure_mae` from the smoke test. If the 3-epoch val loss is in a reasonable range (not diverging), proceed to Step 2.

**Step 2: Full Trial 1 run (999 epochs)**
```bash
cd target/icml2026 && python train.py --dataset tandemfoil --optimizer lion --lr 1.25e-4 --cosine-t-max 10 --grad-clip 0.3 --weight-decay 1e-2 --enable-fourier --model-layers 3 --model-hidden-dim 192 --model-heads 3 --epochs 999 --ema-decay 0.999 --residual-prediction --wandb_group tf-residual-pred
```

### Trial 2 — Residual-prediction + asinh compound

Only run after Trial 1 completes. Tests whether pairing residual-prediction with asinh pressure scaling compounds further.

```bash
cd target/icml2026 && python train.py --dataset tandemfoil --optimizer lion --lr 1.25e-4 --cosine-t-max 10 --grad-clip 0.3 --weight-decay 1e-2 --enable-fourier --model-layers 3 --model-hidden-dim 192 --model-heads 3 --epochs 999 --ema-decay 0.999 --residual-prediction --asinh-pressure --asinh-scale 0.75 --wandb_group tf-residual-pred

author: paljort
body:
# What is in this PR
This PR implements four new runtime formulas: `number_format()`, `abs()`, `null()`, `to_duration()`, and `to_datetime()`.

It also adds support for better human-readable error messages by adding a new `getErrorMessage()` method to the `BaserowRuntimeFormulaArgumentType` class, as well as refactoring the `RuntimeFormulaFunction::validateArgs()` to raise the error message if available. The backend has been similarly refactored.

Finally, a new skill `create-update-runtime-formula` AI skill has been added. This will make it easier to use an LLM to add/update a runtime formula with a simple prompt. For instance, to create the `null()` runtime formula, I just prompted:
> I want you to create a runtime formula named null() that should simply return null in the frontend or None in the backend.

Closes https://github.com/baserow/baserow/issues/4974

# How to test this PR
### 1. `abs()`
This simply returns the absolute value of a number, e.g. `abs(-100)` should return `100`.

Create a Builder element, e.g. Heading, and using expert mode type in `abs(-100)`. You should see `100` rendered.

### 2. `null()`
This returns a `null` (or `None` in the backend). This is useful when you need a `null` value to be used, e.g. when upserting a `null` to a row or evaluating it in a Router node, e.g.:
```
if(get('previous_node.40.0.field_2918') = null(), true, false)
```

Create a Date field in your database table and fill the field with a date value. Then in Builder or Automation, create an workflow action or a node that updates that row's field to use `null()` in the service. You should observe that the row's field is correctly set to null.

### 3. `number_format()`
This formats a number with the option to specify:
- Decimal places (defaults to 0)
- Thousand separator (defaults to `,`)
- Decimal separator (default to `.`)

E.g. using `number_format(12345, 2, '.', ',')` should return `12.345,00`.

### 4. `to_duration()`
This returns a timedelta that can be used by the existing `add` or `minus` formulas to operate on a date.

E.g. `now() + date_format('1 day')` should add a day to the current datetime.

### 5. `to_datetime()`
This takes a Moment.js datetime string with an optional date format, and converts it to a datetime objeect.

E.g. `to_datetime('2026-06-04')` returns `datetime(2026, 06, 04, 0, 0, 0)`.

These updates make the requirements interview process more robust, user-friendly, and maintainable.

**Socratic Interview Process Redesign:**

* Updated the `/omg:interview` command to support subcommands (`status`, `help`, `resume`, `done`, `cancel`, `restart`) for better session management and clarity, and restructured the main interview loop for improved usability.

author: xiaonanln
body:
## Summary

Before the PR, the stress test retried calls that had already cleanly returned, so it only hit the dedup cache-hit branch. Now each real call is preceded (with 20% prob) by the **same** call sent with a random 2–20 ms timeout — bracketing local RPC latency, so the client gets a mix of three outcomes it can't distinguish:
- tiny-timeout never reaches the server (pure client abort);
- tiny-timeout races server execution (server applied it, client has no idea);
- tiny-timeout happens to complete normally.

The real retry that follows uses the same \`call_id\` and must still yield a consistent outcome in every case — which is the exactly-once guarantee reliable calls are meant to provide. Invariants (retry-match, per-wallet conservation) are unchanged; the fault attempt's outcome is ignored so only the real call's response contributes to the ledger.

Logs now include \`fault_injects=<N>\` in the periodic stats line.

author: lejamon
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #10 (M2b). Adds two new oracle layers on top of the ledger-hash (layer 1) and per-tx result (layer 2) checks that already exist.

**Layer 3: per-tx metadata diff across nodes.**
- `rpcclient.Client.Tx` now returns the raw \`AffectedNodes\` JSON along with \`TransactionResult\` / \`Validated\`.
- New \`oracle.CompareTxMetadata(ctx, hash)\` fetches the tx on every node and compares the \`AffectedNodes\` blobs byte-for-byte. rippled emits them in canonical order, so byte-equality is a correct proxy for structural equality.
- Mostly diagnostic: if layer 1 agrees, layer 3 must also agree by construction. When layer 1 reports a divergence, layer 3 gives you *which* state objects each node thinks the tx affected — much more actionable than a bare hash mismatch.
- Runner records \`Kind: "metadata"\` divergences into the corpus on mismatch.

**Layer 4: monotone XRP pool-balance invariant.**
- \`oracle.NewInvariantPoolBalance(addresses).CheckLedger(client)\` sums balances for the tracked addresses (genesis + pool) and asserts the sum never strictly increases across consecutive calls.
- Uses \`math/big.Int\` throughout — no float64 precision loss on drop-denominated values.
- First check always establishes baseline; subsequent strict increases error.
- A strict increase indicates either a rippled bug that mints XRP, stale/inconsistent node data, or a wrong tracked set — all worth surfacing.
- Runner calls it in the periodic layer-1 branch (every 10 tx submissions) and records \`Kind: "invariant"\` divergences with the error detail.

## Status

- 6 packages green (\`go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 90s\`). 10+ oracle tests pass (was 5 before M2d, now covers layers 1–4 + invariant).
- \`go vet\` clean.
- Docker image rebuilds cleanly (\`bash scripts/build-sidecar.sh\`).
- No end-to-end Kurtosis smoke in this PR — the runner unit test exercises the full wiring (both new layers fire on every submit and every periodic tick). Real-env validation comes with the M2a timing-fix work on non-Rosetta hardware.

## Deferred (M2+)

- **Owner-count invariant** — \`OwnerCount\` field vs \`account_objects\` walk; catches reserve-accounting bugs.
- **Escrow/PayChan-aware XRP sum** — once M2 adds those tx families, \`InvariantPoolBalance\` should sum locked amounts too, else legit XRP movement (account→escrow) triggers a false monotone-decrease violation when the escrow releases.
- **Lifetime-fee tracking** — stronger invariant: \`sum(balances) + sum(locked) + lifetime_fees = 100B XRP\`. Cheap once we watch every \`Fee\` field on submit.
- **Canonical-JSON normalization for layer 3** — byte-equality breaks if rippled ever changes AffectedNodes emission order. A stable-sort pass would harden it.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`cd sidecar && go test ./... -count=1\` — 6 packages green
- [ ] \`bash scripts/build-sidecar.sh\` — image rebuilds
- [ ] Review \`docs/plans/2026-04-22-fuzzer-m2d.md\` against the landed commits
- [ ] On clean hardware: verify \`stats.Divergences == 0\` over a full smoke run and confirm no corpus entries with \`Kind: "metadata"\` or \`Kind: "invariant"\` unless there's a genuine bug

Stacked on #10. Merge #8, #9, #10 first, then rebase this on main.

O fluxo atual exigia preenchimento manual do memorial descritivo em Word. Esta PR adiciona um caminho automatizado que lê os confrontantes no PDF e preenche apenas os campos `..........` no `.docx`, preservando a estrutura do documento.

- **CLI para extração + preenchimento**
  - Adiciona `preencher_memorial.py` com três entradas: `--pdf`, `--template`, `--output`.
  - Extrai texto do PDF e identifica confrontantes por rótulos:
    - `NORTE`, `SUL`, `LESTE`/`NASCENTE`, `OESTE`/`POENTE`.
  - Preenche placeholders no DOCX na ordem: norte, sul, leste, oeste.

- **Preservação da estrutura do Word**
  - A substituição é feita sobre runs/parágrafos existentes.
  - O algoritmo troca apenas o primeiro bloco de pontos (`\.{5,}`) encontrado por valor, sem reformatar o documento.

- **Cobertura mínima de comportamento**
  - Inclui testes focados para:
    - parsing de confrontantes com aliases (`NASCENTE`/`POENTE`);
    - substituição de placeholders em parágrafos;
    - preenchimento sequencial de múltiplos campos no DOCX.

- **Documentação e dependências**

author: sebharvey
body:
## Summary
Enhanced the ticket reissuance process to preserve non-exchanged coupons from voided tickets and capture original issue information for audit and display purposes.

## Key Changes

**Backend (ReissueTicketsHandler.cs):**
- Modified coupon status marking: coupons for replaced segments are now marked as `EXCHANGED` before voiding, allowing retained coupons to be identified by exclusion
- Implemented coupon preservation: non-exchanged coupons from the old ticket are extracted and merged with replacement coupons
- Added coupon sorting and renumbering: merged coupons are sorted chronologically by departure date/time and renumbered sequentially
- Captured original issue metadata: ticket number, issue date, issuing location, and original fare amount from the voided ticket are now stored in the new ticket's `originalIssue` field
- Refactored coupon building into separate methods (`BuildReplacementCouponNodes` and `SortAndRenumberCoupons`) for clarity
- Updated change history event type from "Reissued" to "IROPSReissued" and enhanced detail field to include prior ticket reference

**Frontend (order-detail.html & order-detail.ts):**
- Added "Original issue" section to ticket detail modal displaying prior ticket number, issue date, issuing location, and original fare amount
- Updated coupon status label mapping to use new status enum values (OPEN, CHECKED_IN, LIFTED, FLOWN, REFUNDED, VOID, EXCHANGED, PRINT_EXCHANGE)

**Type Definitions (order.service.ts):**
- Extended `TicketData` interface with `originalIssue` object containing ticket number, issue date, issuing location, and fare amount

## Implementation Details
- Coupons are converted to `JsonNode` objects to enable flexible merging and manipulation
- Retained coupons are identified by checking if their status is not "EXCHANGED"
- The original issue data is extracted from the first coupon's origin and the fare construction's base fare
- Chronological sorting ensures coupons appear in logical flight sequence on reissued tickets

author: zarah-s
body:
## Summary

Closes the three remaining Phase 7b items (**M3**, **M5**, **M6**).
With this landed, Phase 7b is complete.

### M5 — Nonce-gap hints

`InvalidNonce` errors now carry the current window bounds
(`[base..base+15]`) and the next-usable nonce (= `base` itself — any
lower nonce would have already slid the window via `advance()`).
Wallets can now show "waiting on nonce N to fill" instead of a vague
out-of-range error. Pure error-message enrichment — no behavior
change.

### M6 — `(sender, nonce)` dedup

One tx per `(sender, nonce)` slot. Duplicates rejected at both RPC
ingress paths (JSON-RPC code `-32010`) and on the gossip ingress
path (drop + debug log).

Without this, different nodes could hold different-hash variants
for the same `(sender, nonce)` — block content would depend on
which proposer wins VRF, unpredictable from the user's view.

Simplified from *fee-bump replacement* because our fee model has
no per-tx priority signal (every tx at a given `base_fee` pays the
same per gas). When the protocol grows a priority-fee field, M6 can
upgrade to real fee-bump.

### M3 — Global mempool size cap

Hard reject at **100K pending txs**, matching the M1 sender cap
budget (128 × 782 senders). Bounds worst-case memory to ~180 MB
(100K × ~1.8 KB for FALCON sig) — safe on server, fine on laptop
before swap pressure.

Applied at both RPC ingress (error `-32011`) and gossip ingress
(silent drop + debug log).

Simplified from *fee-priority eviction* for the same reason as M6.

## Regression

1K TPS × 2 min, 100 senders: **1001 TPS inclusion, 100% efficiency,
0 errors.** No change to the 4K × 10 min sustained ceiling or the
7K × 30s burst ceiling.

## New JSON-RPC error codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-32009` | Per-sender mempool cap reached (M1, already shipped) |
| `-32010` | Duplicate `(sender, nonce)` in mempool (M6) |
| `-32011` | Mempool full — global cap reached (M3) |

author: jalesc
body:
Antes, para emitir uma NFS-e era obrigatório ter o arquivo .pfx salvo em disco e passar o caminho até ele. Isso funcionava bem em muitos cenários, mas criava dificuldade para quem armazena o certificado em banco de dados ou qualquer outra fonte que não seja o sistema de arquivos do servidor.

Com essa mudança, o NfseContext passa a aceitar também o conteúdo do arquivo diretamente, via certificateContent. Quem já usa certificatePath não precisa mudar nada — tudo continua funcionando exatamente como antes.

Como usar:

Antes (continua funcionando)
```
$context = new NfseContext(
    ambiente: TipoAmbiente::Producao,
    certificatePath: '/caminho/para/cert.pfx',
    certificatePassword: 'senha',
);
```

Novo: passando o conteúdo diretamente
```
$context = new NfseContext(
    ambiente: TipoAmbiente::Producao,
    certificatePath: null,
    certificatePassword: 'senha',
    certificateContent: $pfxContent, // bytes vindos de onde quiser
);
```

body:
## Summary

Ships the interim mechanism for ROADMAP item 0.7 — **constant-time comparison enforcement**. The roadmap entry names `dylint` as the long-term target but explicitly sanctions an interim CI-grep + manual-review mechanism: that's what lands here. Dylint remains as a future roadmap item.

- **Policy doc** at `docs/ct-comparison-policy.md` — scope, P1-P5 signatures, escape hatch, failure modes, sanity-break recipe, known limitations, complementary clippy layer.
- **Scoped grep gate** at `scripts/ct-comparison-check.sh` — flags five shapes (byte-literal compare, secret-suffix `.eq`/`.ne`, `.as_bytes()` compare, multi-line `derive(PartialEq/Eq)` on secret-named types, secret-suffix identifier in `==`/`!=`) in `auth*` / `crypto*` / `token*` / `hash_chain*` under `crates/*/src/`. Test paths and `.ct-comparison-ignore` entries excluded.
- **Escape hatch** — `// ct-allow: <reason>` on the match line; new annotations in a PR require the `ct-allow-approved` label. Label check uses git set-difference on `(file, normalized-reason)` so rustfmt reflows don't trigger false readings.
- **18-scenario harness** at `scripts/ct-comparison-scripts-test.sh` — positive + negative cases for every signature, label-gate flow, reformatted-annotation pass-through (the key RISK), `.ct-comparison-ignore` validation, test-path exemption. All 18 PASS.
- **Dedicated workflow** `ct-comparison.yml` mirrors `geiger.yml` (pull_request + push:main + merge_group; SHA-pinned checkout; step-level `env:` for every `github.event.*` value).
- **Complementary clippy layer** — `clippy::disallowed_methods` at workspace `warn` level; paired config added to `clippy.toml` for byte-slice `PartialEq::eq/ne` and `Vec<u8>::eq`. Advisory, not blocking — the grep gate is the hard enforcement.
- **`subtle` forward-declared** in `[workspace.dependencies]` with `default-features = false, features = ["const-generics"]` so the first crate that needs it just writes `subtle.workspace = true`.

Roadmap item: [ROADMAP.md:797](../blob/main/ROADMAP.md#L797).

## Classification

Plumbing — this PR adds a CI gate and policy doc. No runtime code changes, no north-star axis moved directly. Operationalizes the "Security side-channel" bar by establishing PR-time enforcement ahead of the dylint follow-up.

## Verification strategy

All commands green at every commit on this branch:

- [x] `bash scripts/ct-comparison-scripts-test.sh` — 18/18 PASS
- [x] `bash scripts/ct-comparison-check.sh` — PASS (0 scoped files currently under `crates/*/src/`)
- [x] `bash scripts/ct-comparison-check.sh --list-scope` — exit 2 (empty scope), as expected
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] Workflow YAML parses (python yaml.safe_load)

## Test plan

- [ ] CI ct-comparison workflow runs green on this PR
- [ ] CI ct-comparison workflow runs `scripts/ct-comparison-scripts-test.sh` as a self-test step
- [ ] `fetch-depth: 0` on checkout so the label set-difference can read `origin/$base_ref:<file>`
- [ ] Clippy CI green with `disallowed_methods = warn` active

## Rollback

Revert the PR. No crate code depends on the new `subtle` workspace-dependency entry yet; the gate scripts are self-contained; removing `.github/workflows/ct-comparison.yml` disables the gate. No schema, no on-disk state, no API surface.

author: apostate0
body:
Fix: Preserve WS_CAPTION, WS_MINIMIZEBOX, WS_MAXIMIZEBOX for BorderOnly decorations with extended client area to restore native Windows animations.

## Problem
When using `WindowDecorations="BorderOnly"` with `ExtendClientAreaToDecorationsHint="True"`, the caption-style bits (WS_CAPTION, WS_MINIMIZEBOX, WS_MAXIMIZEBOX) that DWM uses to trigger minimize/maximize/close animations were being stripped, causing instant transitions instead of native Windows animations.

## Solution
Added a WM_STYLECHANGING handler that preserves these styles when they're being removed, while skipping FullScreen mode to avoid breaking FullScreen behavior.

## Changes
- Added `GWLP` enum and [STYLESTRUCT](cci:2://file:///d:/Projects/Avalonia/Avalonia/src/Windows/Avalonia.Win32/Interop/UnmanagedMethods.cs:942:8-947:9) struct to [UnmanagedMethods.cs](cci:7://file:///d:/Projects/Avalonia/Avalonia/src/Windows/Avalonia.Win32/Interop/UnmanagedMethods.cs:0:0-0:0)
- Added WM_STYLECHANGING handler in [WindowImpl.AppWndProc.cs](cci:7://file:///d:/Projects/Avalonia/Avalonia/src/Windows/Avalonia.Win32/WindowImpl.AppWndProc.cs:0:0-0:0) that preserves:
  - WS_CAPTION (always)
  - WS_MINIMIZEBOX (when window is minimizable)
  - WS_MAXIMIZEBOX (when window is maximizable)

## Testing
All 120 Win32 integration tests pass, including window sizing tests for BorderOnly decorations.

Fixes https://github.com/AvaloniaUI/Avalonia/issues/21160 , Fixes https://github.com/AvaloniaUI/Avalonia/issues/21212

body:
### Motivation
- Remove multiple layers of aggressive keyword-based staged-generation and forced skill planning so ordinary requests complete directly by default. 
- Provide a single policy source-of-truth to decide when to plan, stage, or ASK_USER using explicit user intent, skill metadata, and real complexity/budget checks. 
- Preserve safe recovery paths for true max-output truncation and keep output bounding behavior intact. 

### Description
- Added a small pure-policy helper `src/runtime/response_flow_policy.py` that implements runtime defaults, conservative explicit-intent detectors (plan/stage phrases), true-complexity budget checks, skill metadata awareness, and returns a compact `ResponseFlowDecision` (`plan_required`, `staging_required`, `execution_style`, `ask_user_policy`, `reasons`).
- Wired the shared policy into the three affected layers: 
  - `src/runtime/output_controller.py`: replaced keyword classifier with policy-driven decisioning, inject staged guard only when required, and preserved max-output recovery and output-bounding logic.
  - `src/agents/core.py`: replaced the large-generation guard to call the shared policy (no longer relies on generic marker words), update budget-state fields to reflect policy reasons, and changed over-budget suffix wording so manifest/ask-to-continue is not forced unless staging is active/required.
  - `src/agents/skill_mode.py`: stop unconditional initial plan generation; generate an initial plan only when policy requires it and otherwise initialize a single execute-step fallback; refactored skill-mode system prompt to vary by `execution_style` (`direct` vs `stepwise`) and lowered default ASK_USER aggressiveness for direct skills.
- Extended skill model and runtime config to carry new frontmatter/metadata and propagate it: 
  - `src/skills/registry.py`: added `planning_mode`, `staging_mode`, `execution_style`, `ask_user_policy` (with safe defaults) and `from_dict()` support. 
  - `src/skills/runtime.py`: extended `SkillRuntimeConfig` with the new fields, copied them into runtime config in `build_skill_runtime_config()`, and emit a short runtime behavior line in prompt blocks when explicit. 
  - `src/skills/active_contract.py`: persist the new runtime behavior fields in active contract records.
- Config and docs: added `llm.response_flow` to `Config.PORTAL_MANAGED_FIELD_TREE` and example `config.yaml.example` block; updated `src/skills/README.md` to document new frontmatter.
- Annotated explicit skills that are stepwise/staged in `skills/*.md` frontmatter (kept `create-pull-request` direct). 
- Tests and test updates: added a focused pure-policy test `tests/test_response_flow_policy.py`, updated `tests/test_core_runtime_boundary.py` and `tests/test_skill_mode_termination.py` to reflect non-eager staging and direct-skill startup, and extended `tests/test_config_runtime_profile_automation_removed.py` to allow `llm.response_flow` passthrough.

### Testing

author: exafyltd
body:
Step 4 of the Vitana Index plan.

- New admin-callable RPC `health_compute_vitana_index_for_user(p_user_id, p_date, p_model_version)` (service_role only) — sibling of the main v3 compute RPC that takes user_id as a parameter instead of reading auth.uid(). Lets server-side code trigger recompute without a user JWT.

- New SQL helper `vitana_contribution_vector_from_source_ref(source_ref)` + BEFORE INSERT trigger on `autopilot_recommendations` that auto-populates `contribution_vector` from the signal_type. Backfills existing NULL rows.

- New AFTER UPDATE trigger on `calendar_events.completion_status` — when a row transitions to 'completed', fires `health_compute_vitana_index_for_user()` for today. Works for any completion path (gateway, direct Supabase from the UI, background jobs).

- Gateway POST /api/v1/calendar/events/:id/complete: after marking completed, invokes the admin recompute, diffs against the prior row, emits an `index.recomputed` OASIS event with `per_pillar_delta`, and returns `vitana_index` in the response. Best-effort — recompute failures don't block the completion.

author: shushuzn
body:
## Fix: Windows GBK encoding error in browser tool

**Problem:** On Windows, `subprocess.Popen` defaults to system encoding (GBK).
When reading browser command output from GitHub pages (UTF-8 content), Python
fails with:

```
'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xa6 in position 1068: illegal multibyte sequence
```

**Solution:** Add `encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'` as kwargs to
`subprocess.Popen` in `_run_browser_command`.

**Files changed:** Only `tools/browser_tool.py` — adds two lines:
```python
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ...,
    encoding='utf-8',   # NEW
    errors='replace',  # NEW
)
```

**Testing:** Verified on Windows — `browser_navigate` + `browser_console`
correctly return UTF-8 Chinese content from GitHub pages.

## Summary

Eight rcs of work on `feat/occtkit` (`v0.5.0-rc.1` … `v0.5.0-rc.8`). Net effect:

- **New `occtkit` umbrella binary** (busybox-style multi-call). Single install (`make install`) puts `occtkit` + per-verb symlinks into `$PREFIX/bin`. Replaces the old per-target standalone CLIs (which remain on disk with deprecation notices for downstream compatibility).
- **`--serve` mode** on every verb — JSONL request envelope in / structured `{ok, exit, stdout, stderr, error?}` envelope out, with per-request stdout/stderr capture so child processes (e.g. `swift build` invoked by `run`) don't leak to occtkit's own stdout.
- **`drawing-export` verb** + **`DrawingComposer` library product** — multi-view ISO 128-30 technical drawings as DXF R12 with full ISO scaffolding (5457 sheet, 7200 title block, 5456-2 projection symbol, 128-50 hatching, 128-40 cutting-plane lines, 6410 cosmetic threads, 1302 surface finish, 1101 GD&T, detail views, 5455 standard-scale snapping). Library exposes `DrawingSpec` + `Composer.render(spec:shape:)` for in-process consumers (iOS, OCCTSwiftPartsAgent).
- **`reconstruct` verb** — JSON `[FeatureSpec]` → BREP via OCCTSwift's `FeatureReconstructor.buildJSON` (closes #3).
- **OCCTSwift dep**: `0.135.0` → `0.147.0`. The drawing-export refactor in rc.6 deleted ~600 lines of DIY (Sheet, ViewPlacer, SectionExtraction, PaperSize) once their upstream equivalents landed in v0.144-v0.147.
- **Open-source boundary** (rc.8): swiftGCS dependency and the `solve-sketch` verb removed; the project now depends only on OCCTSwift.

## Verb set

`run` `graph-validate` `graph-compact` `graph-dedup` `graph-query` `graph-ml` `feature-recognize` `dxf-export` `drawing-export` `reconstruct`

## Issues closed by this PR

- **#2** BRepGraph scripting support (Phase 1, commit `c10bca9`)
- **#3** Reconstruct script (rc.6, commit `8eafb53`)
- **#5** `--serve` envelope framing (rc.3, commit `fd2a1cf`)
- **#6** drawing-export verb (rc.4, commit `acfdb88`)
- **#7** DrawingComposer library product (rc.7, commit `e5f4c5d`)

(All five were already manually closed on the issue tracker as the work landed on the branch — the merge formally ties the commit history to the closures.)

## Out of scope

- 2D constraint solving (was `solve-sketch` via swiftGCS) — withdrawn in rc.8 to keep this project to its open-source boundary. Downstream consumers wire their own solver.
- Standalone target removal — kept with deprecation notices; will be deleted in a follow-up release.

### Motivation
- The runtime will begin honoring a sparse managed subtree `llm.response_flow`, and Portal must preserve, validate, expose, and sync that subtree without densifying persisted runtime-profile JSON.

body:
## What changed
- added dedicated `Conversation/Actor Policy` marker support in `document-processor`, including schema/model registration and default registry wiring
- preserved parsed `operations` data in marker loading instead of falling back to the generic marker shape
- enforced actor/source policy checks in `Conversation/Sequential Workflow Operation` matching using raw timeline entry actor/source nodes
- added validation and regression coverage for policy parsing, duplicate policy detection, invalid literals, and operation matching behavior

## Why it changed
`Conversation/Actor Policy` existed in repository types, but `document-processor` did not execute the contract semantics. The processor needed to understand the marker shape and apply policy constraints during operation workflow matching.

## Impact
Documents can now declare per-operation actor/source constraints with `Conversation/Actor Policy`, and unsupported operation invocations are skipped consistently during processing.

## Root cause
The processor previously treated this contract as an untyped/generic marker at best and had no operation-level enforcement logic for actor/source policy rules.

body:
## Description

Using `VkDebugUtilsMessengerCreateInfoEXT` needs special consideration, depending on where it is used.
- `VkDebugUtilsMessengerCreateInfoEXT` is specified to extend `VkInstanceCreateInfo`, and multiple instances of it in that extension chain are allowed. That is, with multiple `VkDebugUtilsMessengerCreateInfoEXT`s in that chain, multiple callbacks are created on instance creation, but just for a very short period of time.
- `VkDebugUtilsMessengerCreateInfoEXT` is not specified to extend itself! That is, with multiple instances of it in the pNext-chain for vkCreateDebugUtilsMessengerEXT, just the very first `VkDebugUtilsMessengerCreateInfoEXT` in that chain is used to create a callback. Actually, I would have expected that the validation layers would fire a warning with such a usage.

The sample `shader_debugprintf` used an additional `VkDebugUtilsMessengerCreateInfoEXT` for both, Instance and DebugUtilsMessenger creation. Now, a separate local DebugUtilsMessenger is created to have both callbacks, the one from the sample and the one from the framework, alive.

Build tested on Win11 with VS2022. Run tested on Win11 with NVidia GPU.

body:
### Description
This PR resolves an issue where Eloquent models using PHP attributes like #[Table] or #[Connection] would ignore those attributes if a parent model explicitly defined the corresponding $table or $connection property.

### Solution
Implemented a ReflectionClass check (using a new `classOwnsDeclaredProperty` helper) to distinguish between properties declared directly on the model versus those inherited from a parent. This ensures child attributes correctly override inherited parent properties.

### Tests
Added comprehensive test cases in DatabaseEloquentModelTest.php covering Table, Connection, primaryKey, and keyType inheritance overrides. Verified that all tests pass.

body:
## Summary

- Keep stdout/stderr data listeners active after the 15s startup check — previously `removeAllListeners('data')` was called, making the stall detector blind to stdout/stderr activity and causing false-positive stall kills
- Persist `progress_file` and `stdout_tail` in demo-runs.json (no longer stripped); add `stderr_tail` capture; stall detector calls `persistDemoRuns()` before SIGTERM so diagnostic data survives the kill
- Reorder runDemo/runDemoBatch/preflightCheck steps: `checkAndSyncWorktree()` and `verifyDistArtifacts()` now run BEFORE `executePrerequisites()`, eliminating a 45-second window where dev servers could die between prerequisite execution and demo launch
- Add `stall_timeout_ms` parameter to `RunDemoArgsSchema` (0 to disable, 10000–300000ms) for demos with slow fixture setup (bridge server, extension rebuild)
- Add `stderr_tail` to `DemoRunState` and `CheckDemoResultResult`; `check_demo_result` uses stderr as fallback `failure_summary` when status is `unknown`

## Test plan

- [ ] All 561 tests pass (verified before submission)
- [ ] Build succeeds (`packages/mcp-servers`)
- [ ] Headed demo with slow fixture setup no longer gets false-positive stall kill
- [ ] `check_demo_result` returns `stderr_tail` when a demo process exits without producing a failure summary

author: copilot
body:
Builds the full MVP for a UK Home Office–compliant rifle club management portal from an empty repository. Covers auth, digital sign-in book (QR-based), club/member management, firearm tracking, and audit trail logging.

## Architecture
- **Monorepo** (npm workspaces): `server/` (Express + TypeScript strict) + `client/` (React + Vite)
- **ORM**: Prisma against PostgreSQL with 6 models (`User`, `Club`, `ClubMembership`, `Firearm`, `VisitLog`, `SignInLink`)
- **Production**: Express serves the Vite `dist` as static files; multi-stage Dockerfile + `docker-compose.yml`

## Backend (`server/`)
- JWT auth (24h, HS256) with bcrypt password hashing (10 rounds)
- Security middleware: Helmet, CORS, rate limiting (15 req/15 min on `/api/auth`), Zod input validation
- Routes: `auth`, `users`, `clubs`, `firearms`, `visits`, `sign-in-links`
- Crypto-random sign-in token generation with expiry; active visit detection (TimeIn set, TimeOut null)

## Frontend (`client/`)
- `AuthContext` with localStorage JWT storage
- Pages: Login, Register (GDPR consent checkbox), Dashboard, Club Dashboard, Profile, Sign-In (`/sign-in/:token`)
- Dashboard surfaces active sign-in state with prominent Sign Out CTA
- Sign-In page validates token, pre-fills user name, groups firearms dropdown (personal first, then club)
- QR code rendered via `qrcode.react` for generated sign-in links
- Plain CSS, semantic HTML5, no Tailwind

## Data model highlights
```prisma
model VisitLog {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId        String
  clubId        String
  purpose       String
  firearmUsedId String?
  timeIn        DateTime  @default(now())
  timeOut       DateTime?   // null = active session
}

model SignInLink {
  cryptoToken String   @unique   // crypto-random, time-limited
  expiresAt   DateTime
}
```

|---|---|---|
| `owner@test.com` | `Password123!` | Club Owner |
| `member@test.com` | `Password123!` | Member |

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> # Project Overview: shootingmatch.app
> You are an expert full-stack developer and security architect. Your goal is to build an MVP for "shootingmatch.app", a compliance and management portal for UK Home Office approved rifle clubs. 
> 
> You must write the code, create the files, and set up the architecture following the exact specifications below. 
> 
> ## Tech Stack
> * **Runtime:** Node.js 24
> * **Language:** TypeScript (Strict mode enabled)
> * **Backend:** Express.js (REST API)
> * **Frontend:** React with Vite
> * **Architecture:** Monorepo style. The Express server should serve the React app's static `dist` build in production, and act as the API backend.
> * **Database:** PostgreSQL (latest)
> * **ORM:** Prisma (Schema-first/State-first ORM)
> * **Deployment:** Dockerized (multi-stage Dockerfile that builds the Vite app, compiles the Express server, and serves them together).
> 
> ## Core Requirements & Compliance
> * **UK Home Office Legal:** The system must maintain strict audit trails for firearm usage, club attendance, and user identity.
> * **GDPR & Security:** All passwords must be securely hashed (e.g., bcrypt/argon2). Personal Data (PII) must be handled securely. Implement standard security practices (Helmet, CORS, Rate Limiting, JWT or secure session cookies for auth).
> * **UI/UX:** Modern, clean, and fully accessible (WCAG compliant) using standard HTML5 semantic tags and a lightweight styling solution (avoid TailwindCSS).
> 
> ## Data Model (Prisma Schema Guidelines)
> Please design the Prisma schema with the following core entities:
> 1.  **User:** ID, Name, Email, PasswordHash, Role, GDPRConsentDate, Address, PlaceOfBirth, DateOfBirth.
> 2.  **Club:** ID, Name, OwnerID (relation to User).
> 3.  **ClubMembership:** UserID, ClubID, Status (Pending, Approved, Rejected), Role (Member, Admin), Expiry.
> 4.  **Firearm:** ID, Make, Model, Caliber, SerialNumber, OwnerType (USER or CLUB), OwnerID.
> 5.  **VisitLog (The Sign-in Book):** ID, UserID, ClubID, Purpose, FirearmUsedID, TimeIn (DateTime), TimeOut (DateTime nullable).
> 6.  **SignInLink:** ID, ClubID, CryptoToken (unique string), ExpiresAt (DateTime).
> 
> ## Feature Specifications
> 
> ### 1. Authentication & Profiles
> * Users can register, log in, and manage their profile.
> * Users can register their personal firearms to their profile.
> 
> ### 2. User Dashboard
> * Display aggregate stats: Average visits per month, Total lifetime visits.
> * Display a list of their approved Club Memberships.
> * Provide UI to request to join an existing club or register a brand new club.
> * **Active Sign-In State:** If the user currently has an active `VisitLog` (TimeIn exists, but TimeOut is null), display a prominent "Sign Out" prompt on their dashboard.
> 
> ### 3. Club Dashboard (For Owners/Admins)
> * View all members and their roles.
> * Approve or reject pending membership requests.
> * Manually invite/setup accounts for new members.
> * Manage the club's armory (Club Firearms).
> 
> ### 4. The Digital Sign-in Book (QR / Crypto Link)
> * The Club Admin can generate a temporary, time-based "Sign-In Session".
> * This generates a crypto-random URL (e.g., `/sign-in/:cryptoToken`).
> * The UI must render a QR code for this URL.
> * When a logged-in user scans the QR/visits the link, they see a form pre-filling their Name. They must select: Club Represented, Purpose of Visit, and Firearm Used (dropdown of their personal firearms + club firearms with their personal ones at the top in a group).
> * Submitting the form creates a `VisitLog` with `TimeIn` set to now.
> 
> ## Execution Plan for Agent
> Please execute this project in the following phases. Wait for my approval after each phase before moving to the next.
> 
> * **Phase 1: Project Scaffolding:** Initialize Node project, setup Vite React frontend and Express backend structure. Setup ESLint, Prettier, and TypeScript configs.
> * **Phase 2: Database & ORM:** Setup Prisma schema with the entities listed above. Generate the client and create a seed file for testing.
> * **Phase 3: Backend API:** Build the Express routes for Auth, Users, Clubs, Firearms, and Visits. Implement middleware for auth and error handling.
> * **Phase 4: Frontend Development:** Build the React UI, hooking it up to the Express API. Implement the dashboards, forms, and QR code generator (using a library like `qrcode.react`).
> * **Phase 5: Dockerization:** Create the `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` to spin up the Postgres DB and the Node application.
> * **Phase 6: Documentation:** Create detailed project contributing

body:
# test(ci): multi-replica smoke subset gated by ci-gate

Promotes a subset of `tests/integration/` to a required check via `ci-gate`.

## Why

PR #413 shipped the docker-compose multi-replica harness as an **advisory** CI
workflow. Advisory means a regression could ride into prod because the check
didn't block merge. The user's autonomous-session directive was explicit:
*"tests are the most important thing we can do … a simple healthz check isn't
sufficient."* This PR puts real cross-replica teeth on every merge.

## What

### New test file: `tests/integration/test_multireplica_smoke.py`

- **`test_both_replicas_serve_authenticated_request`** — GET `/api/devices` on
  both replicas, assert 200 + JSON content-type. Catches "replica boots and
  answers `/healthz` but crashes on first real request" — we shipped that once
  before (Alembic migration race). The MVP tests wouldn't have caught it
  because they only exercise their own seeded state.
- **`test_exactly_one_scheduler_and_offline_sweep_leader`** — polls
  `leader_leases` up to 90 s for **3 consecutive clean samples** with exactly
  one live leader per `{scheduler, offline_sweep}`. Strong enough to catch
  split-brain + flapping election, not just "saw it clean once." Window
  allows for `offline_sweep`'s 30 s startup-delay in `cms/main.py`.
  `offline_sweep` is the alert path the user flagged as *"high temperature
  alerts are very important, I do not want to miss them ever"* — if that loop
  double-runs we generate duplicate alerts; if it doesn't run we miss them.

### Wiring

- `pytest.ini` registers the `smoke` marker.
- Existing 2 MVP tests now carry `@pytest.mark.smoke`.
- New `multireplica-smoke` job in `tests.yml` brings up the compose stack and
  runs `pytest tests/integration/ --run-integration -m smoke`. Added to
  `ci-gate.needs` so it's required.
- Deleted the old advisory `integration.yml` and replaced it with a
  `workflow_dispatch` + nightly variant so future non-smoke heavier tests
  (chaos, fake-device fleet) don't silently lose a home.
- Added `Dockerfile` to the `code` path filter.

### Version

`cms/__init__.py` 1.37.75 → 1.37.76.

## Validation

Local run against real compose stack (2 CMS replicas + shared Postgres +
shared asset volume):

```
tests/integration/test_multireplica_mvp.py::test_skip_on_b_visible_via_a PASSED
tests/integration/test_multireplica_mvp.py::test_concurrent_upgrade_exactly_one_409 PASSED
tests/integration/test_multireplica_smoke.py::test_both_replicas_serve_authenticated_request PASSED
tests/integration/test_multireplica_smoke.py::test_exactly_one_scheduler_and_offline_sweep_leader PASSED
4 passed in 48.05s
```

## Rubber-duck findings addressed

- **Original**: "returns on first clean sample — transient split-brain slips
  through." **Fix**: require 3 consecutive clean polls spaced 1 s apart.
- **Original**: "30 s poll window is tight given `offline_sweep` sleeps 30 s
  before even acquiring its lease." **Fix**: widened to 90 s total.
- **Original**: "deleting `integration.yml` silently drops future non-smoke
  coverage." **Fix**: replaced with `workflow_dispatch` + nightly variant.

## Follow-ups (not this PR)

After merge, the **branch-protection required-check list doesn't need to
change** — `ci-gate` is already required, and this PR extends its `needs:`
array. No manual toggle in GitHub UI is needed.

### Motivation
- Provide a persistent schema for core domain entities (users, profiles, collections, collection items, memberships, marketplace listings, and valuation history) so the API operates against a real datastore instead of static mocks.
- Capture domain invariants (membership roles, item conditions, listing lifecycle, unique membership constraint, and ownership checks) and enable local developer workflows with migrations and seed data.

### Description
- Added a Prisma schema at `apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma` defining `User`, `Profile`, `Collection`, `CollectionMembership`, `CollectionItem`, `MarketplaceListing`, `ValuationSnapshot` plus enums for roles/conditions/statuses and soft-delete timestamps.
- Added an initial SQL migration under `apps/api/prisma/migrations/202604230001_init/migration.sql` with indexes, unique constraints (including `@@unique([collectionId, userId])`) and FKs that enforce listing/collection relationships.

### Motivation

This PR merges `ScaffoldWalkModule` and `ScaffoldRecodeModule` into a single, unified `ScaffoldModule`.

### Key Changes:
- **Consolidated Utilities**: Merged `ScaffoldWalkUtil` into `ScaffoldUtil`, unifying the logic to use `BlockCache` consistently.
- **RotationMode Enum**: Implemented a new `RotationMode` property with support for `BASIC`, `EDGE`, `MODERN_WATCHDOG`, `GOD_BRIDGE`, `INTAVE`, `SNAP`, `BRUTE_FORCE`, and `OFF`.
- **Dual-Mode Rotation Speed**: Added `rotationSpeedMode` ("Manual" vs. "Dynamic"). Manual mode uses the configurable min/max speed range, while Dynamic mode uses advanced speed curves based on `offGroundTicks`.
- **Merged Logic**: Combined advanced slot selection, raycast logic, and tower/sprint support from both original modules.
- **Refactoring**: Updated all external references in sprints, towers, speed modules, and other utilities to point to the new `ScaffoldModule`.
- **Cleanup**: Deleted the redundant `ScaffoldWalkModule.java`, `ScaffoldRecodeModule.java`, and `ScaffoldWalkUtil.java` files.

This change streamlines the scaffold implementation and provides a more robust and configurable feature set for the users.

## Problem

This repo was managing Sentry logging directly using the archived `zerolog-sentry` package, unlike all other repos in the org which delegate to `logger.InitZerolog` from `insights-operator-utils`.

`sentry-go v0.46.0` removed the `Extra` field from `sentry.Event`, which `zerolog-sentry v1.8.5` still references — blocking MintMaker PR #582.

## Fix

Replace the custom `logging.go` Sentry setup with `logger.InitZerolog` from `insights-operator-utils v1.28.0`, which already uses the maintained `sentry-go/zerolog` integration.

The `InitLogging` function signature is unchanged so no callers are affected. `logging.go` goes from ~90 lines to ~50, removing all direct Sentry wiring.

## Related

- Closes / supersedes #590
- Unblocks #582
- `insights-operator-utils` fix: https://github.com/RedHatInsights/insights-operator-utils/pull/842

## Summary
- Precompile `<Foundation/Foundation.h>` once and preload it via `-include-pch` in the syntax-check and build-and-run steps, so Foundation is parsed once instead of per fixture (~10× faster locally on the syntax check).
- Parallelise the `Run Objective-C files` step with `xargs -P` and a per-invocation tmpdir, replacing the serial `while` loop (~5× faster locally; 140s → 27s on 240 fixtures).
- Leaves clang-tidy unchanged — the repo's `.clang-tidy` uses `Checks: *`, which the existing `lint-cpp-tidy` note documents as being slowed down by PCH preloading.

> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: CI-only workflow changes that adjust how Objective-C fixtures are compiled/run; main risk is macOS toolchain/PCH compatibility causing false failures or missed issues.
