author: onkwon
body:
@codex

This pull request introduces support for asynchronous HTTP transport in the Pulse metrics reporting system, along with significant refactoring for improved robustness and maintainability. The main changes revolve around enabling non-blocking metric transmissions, enhancing state management for in-flight reports, and updating the interface and internal logic to support these new capabilities.

**Key changes include:**

### Asynchronous HTTP Transport Support

* Added an `async_transport` option to the `struct pulse` configuration, allowing the HTTP transport to operate in asynchronous mode. When enabled, `metrics_report_transmit()` may return `-EAGAIN` to signal that a transfer is still in progress, and `pulse_report()` will return `PULSE_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS`. The caller must then invoke `pulse_report()` again to advance the transfer. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ee5294817eda03a1a75d02d18457d131323190baae40a13b4d01344f5581166eR84-R90) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ee5294817eda03a1a75d02d18457d131323190baae40a13b4d01344f5581166eR51-R54)
* Refactored the ESP-IDF HTTPS transport (`pulse_transport_https.c`) to manage connection state with a new `https_session_t` structure, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous operation. Added state management and session advancement logic to handle in-progress transfers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-92d18d69cd25365ab10d6118afa13983376f083cee3e0caff4f1efe87f53d397R25-R59) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-92d18d69cd25365ab10d6118afa13983376f083cee3e0caff4f1efe87f53d397L91-L134) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-92d18d69cd25365ab10d6118afa13983376f083cee3e0caff4f1efe87f53d397L144-R256)

### State and Buffer Management

* Introduced new fields in `pulse_report_ctx` and related logic to track in-flight payloads, manage buffer allocation, and handle completion or abortion of metric transmissions. Added functions for clearing, committing, and aborting in-flight operations, and for collecting metrics from either the backlog or live data. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f65c61afae8ca75bfff1068d934dd5d3b50e1dba602a5f75fcf94f4d0ad8ad0dL24-R36) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ae0f336bcbe98758c5104b17ebfe083058fc56d5dd38e19ebdb1f451e2275462R156-L168)
* Improved memory management by ensuring buffers are properly allocated and freed, and by tracking whether a payload originated from the backlog or live metrics.

### API and Error Handling Enhancements

* Added a new status code, `PULSE_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS`, and updated error mapping and stringification to handle in-progress asynchronous operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ee5294817eda03a1a75d02d18457d131323190baae40a13b4d01344f5581166eR51-R54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ae0f336bcbe98758c5104b17ebfe083058fc56d5dd38e19ebdb1f451e2275462R137-R138) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ae0f336bcbe98758c5104b17ebfe083058fc56d5dd38e19ebdb1f451e2275462R400-R401)
* Updated `pulse_report()` to support resuming in-progress transmissions and to check reporting intervals before collecting new metrics.

### Testing and Mock Support

author: saahasmuthineni
body:
## Summary

Debugging pass over commit `40f8379` (`fix(csv_dir): harden CSV child against real-world data`, merged via #37) surfaced two bugs in the CSV auto-detection path. This PR fixes both and adds a regression test.

## Bugs found

1. **Auto-detect bypassed the 100 MB size guard at init.** `_auto_detect_columns` called `_read_csv(csvs[0])` without `max_bytes`, so during `CSVDirectoryChild.__init__` the entire first CSV was loaded into memory just to slice `rows[:20]`. That contradicted the spirit of fix #4 in the prior commit and meant a user pointing `csv_dir.path` at a directory containing a multi-GB CSV would OOM before any tool call could run. Verified with a probe: 610 KB CSV + a lowered 10 KB guard → init peak memory 5.3 MB.

2. **Size-guard error message truncated sub-MB limits to "0 MB"** via `max_bytes // (1024 * 1024)`. Not reachable at the default 100 MB limit, but misleading in tests and future smaller deployments.

## Changes

- `src/biosensor_mcp/children/csv_dir/child.py` — `_auto_detect_columns` now streams at most 20 rows via `DictReader` directly, never loading the full file. Classification logic is byte-identical to the prior `rows[:20]` behavior.
- `src/biosensor_mcp/children/csv_dir/child.py` — size-guard error uses float formatting (`.1f MB`).
- `tests/children/csv_dir/test_csv_shape.py` — `test_auto_detect_streams_sample_only` lowers `MAX_CSV_BYTES` below a fixture CSV's size and asserts init succeeds while tool calls are still blocked.

## Fidelity note

No impact on data served to the LLM. Auto-detection produces only the column-name list used for consent data-types and the `columns` parameter's `allowed_values` — tool handlers still call `_read_csv(max_bytes=MAX_CSV_BYTES)` and return full rows at configured precision.

## Verification

- Init peak memory on the 610 KB probe: 5.3 MB → 42.5 KB.
- Full suite: 392 passed (391 pre-existing + 1 new regression test).
- Size-guard error now reads `"File is too large (0.6 MB, limit 0.0 MB). …"` instead of `"(1 MB, limit 0 MB)"`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — all 392 tests pass locally
- [x] New regression test `test_auto_detect_streams_sample_only` passes
- [x] Probe confirms init memory bounded regardless of CSV size
- [ ] CI (Ubuntu/macOS/Windows × Python 3.10/3.11/3.12) — to be confirmed on PR

<details>

   ### 6.0.4
   ```
   ==========================

*April 7, 2026*

Django 6.0.4 fixes one security issue with severity "moderate", four security
issues with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.3.

CVE-2026-3902: ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation
====================================================================

``ASGIRequest`` normalizes header names following WSGI conventions, mapping
hyphens to underscores. As a result, even in configurations where reverse
proxies carefully strip security-sensitive headers named with hyphens, such a
header could be spoofed by supplying a header named with underscores.

Under WSGI, it is the responsibility of the server or proxy to avoid ambiguous
mappings. (Django's :djadmin:`runserver` was patched in :cve:`2015-0219`.) But
under ASGI, there is not the same uniform expectation, even if many proxies
protect against this under default configuration (including ``nginx`` via
``underscores_in_headers off;``).

Headers containing underscores are now ignored by ``ASGIRequest``, matching the
behavior of :pypi:`Daphne <daphne>`, the reference server for ASGI.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4277: Privilege abuse in ``GenericInlineModelAdmin``
=============================================================

Add permissions on inline model instances were not validated on submission of
forged ``POST`` data in
:class:`~django.contrib.contenttypes.admin.GenericInlineModelAdmin`.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4292: Privilege abuse in ``ModelAdmin.list_editable``
==============================================================

Admin changelist forms using
:attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.list_editable` incorrectly allowed new
instances to be created via forged ``POST`` data.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33033: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``MultiPartParser`` via base64-encoded file upload
===============================================================================================================

When using ``django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser``, multipart uploads
with ``Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`` that include excessive whitespace
may trigger repeated memory copying, potentially degrading performance.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33034: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ASGI requests via memory upload limit bypass
=========================================================================================================

ASGI requests with a missing or understated ``Content-Length`` header could
bypass the :setting:`DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` limit when reading
``HttpRequest.body``, potentially loading an unbounded request body into
memory and causing service degradation.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 where :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogin`
  and :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogout` did not respectively set or clear
  ``request.user`` if it had already been materialized (e.g., by sync
  middleware) (:ticket:`37017`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 in admin forms where
  ``RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper`` incorrectly wrapped all widgets in a
  ``<fieldset>`` (:ticket:`36949`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 6.0 where the ``fields.E348`` system check did not

author: tinkerbug
body:
## Summary

Exercises the full `TR_FlightLog` lifecycle (`prepareFlight` + `finalizeFlight`) on real hardware, alongside the legacy LFS path. Still shadow-only — the flush task hot path stays on LFS. That comes in **Stage 2c-3c**.

### What happens when `ENABLE_FLIGHTLOG_SHADOW` is on

| Trigger | Legacy LFS | Shadow `TR_FlightLog` |
|---|---|---|
| PRELAUNCH entry | `lfs_file_open` | `prepareFlight(id)` — picks a free 256-block range, erases it (~770 ms on the pad), assigns `flight_id` |
| End of logging | `lfs_file_close` + rename | `finalizeFlight(name, 0)` — appends one index entry; **then immediately `deleteFlight(name)`** to release the blocks so repeat bench cycles don't exhaust capacity |

The auto-delete is the Stage 2c-3b quirk: since `writeFrame` isn't being called yet, every shadow flight records zero bytes. Without the delete, each cycle would permanently consume 32 MB. Stage 2c-3c drops the delete the same time it starts filling those blocks with real telemetry.

### Bench plan

1. Flip `ENABLE_FLIGHTLOG_SHADOW = true`, flash, boot.
2. Connect iOS, power on, `cmd 23` start → stop. Expect in the log:
   ```
   I … FLIGHTLOG: shadow prepareFlight OK: id=N, range=[32..288), pages=256
   I … FLIGHTLOG: shadow finalizeFlight OK: shadow_N.bin
   ```
   The `prepareFlight` line will come with a ~770 ms stall (the 256-block erase). Acceptable since PRELAUNCH is on the pad.
3. Start+stop again. Should see `id=N+1` and the same range (blocks released after the previous finalize).
4. Reboot. `shadow up: 0 flight(s) in index` (the delete cleaned everything up).
5. Watch that legacy LFS flight recording still works — filenames `flight_NNN.bin`, downloadable via iOS, etc.

### Hooked sites

All 7 existing lifecycle call sites in `out_computer/main.cpp`: 2 `prepareLogFile` (PRELAUNCH entry, manual `cmd 23` toggle) + 5 `endLogging` (I2C `END_FLIGHT`, LoRa uplink, manual `cmd 23` toggle, LoRa sim-stop, OC sim-stop). Hook emission is `if (config::ENABLE_FLIGHTLOG_SHADOW && flightlog.isInitialized())`, so with the flag off nothing compiles in.

## Test plan

- [x] Host tests unchanged — no component touched
- [ ] `build (out_computer)` + `build (base_station)` CI green
- [ ] Bench: see plan above. If `NoSpace` ever appears, we accidentally lost the auto-delete.

author: conorokus
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of Payjoin send support ([plan](docs/plans/2026-04-23-001-feat-payjoin-send-support-plan.md), [brainstorm](docs/brainstorms/2026-04-23-payjoin-send-brainstorm.md)). Scaffolds the URI parsing, proxy endpoint, dev tooling, and CSP — **no user-visible behavior change**. All new code is dormant until Phase 3 wires the send flow through a new \`transformPsbt\` hook.

### What was built

- **BIP 321 parser** (\`src/ldk/payment-input.ts\`) — extracts \`pj=\` and \`pjos=\` into \`ParsedPaymentInput.onchain.payjoin\` as an optional sub-field. Raw value captured; no scheme filter at the parser layer so BIP 77 v2 URIs (\`bitcoin:\` / \`payjoin:\`) survive. PDK validates scheme downstream.
- **Serverless proxy** (\`api/payjoin-proxy.ts\`) — Edge Runtime with SSRF hardening: private/loopback/link-local IP rejection (including CGNAT, ULA, IPv4-mapped IPv6), userinfo/port rejection, CR/LF rejection, header allowlist (no cookies, no \`Origin\`, no \`Referer\`, no \`X-Forwarded-For\` forwarding), \`redirect: 'manual'\`, content-type allowlist (\`text/plain\` + \`message/ohttp-req\` only), 100 KB body cap, 20s timeout, in-memory per-IP rate limit (marked TODO to swap to Vercel KV before Phase 3).
- **Dev proxy** (\`vite.config.ts\`) — \`/__payjoin_proxy/DOMAIN/PATH\` mirror of prod behavior. Workbox \`NetworkOnly\` for Payjoin traffic so session-specific PSBTs/OHTTP payloads are never cached.
- **CSP** (\`vercel.json\`) — explicit \`connect-src\` allowlist: self + existing services (cloudflare-dns, mempool.space, rapidsync.lightningdevkit.org, wss://proxy.zinqq.app) + \`payjo.in\` + 3 OHTTP relays. No broad \`https:\` fallback — v1 traffic goes through same-origin \`/api/payjoin-proxy\`.
- **Constants hoist** — moved \`MIN_FEE_RATE_SAT_VB\` + \`MAX_FEE_SATS\` from private \`context.tsx\` constants to \`src/onchain/config.ts\` exports so Payjoin code can import without inverting the dependency direction.
- **Vitest config** — extended test \`include\` to \`api/\` for security-critical proxy tests.

### Why

This PR addresses the brainstorm goals of privacy-by-default and opportunistic compatibility by capturing URIs that advertise \`pj=\`. Without Phase 1, the parser still silently drops Payjoin URIs, and the proxy + CSP needed to send Payjoin traffic from a browser don't exist.

### Key decisions

- **Parser captures raw \`pj=\`, doesn't validate scheme** — an earlier draft required \`https:\`, which would have silently dropped every v2 URI. Scheme validation belongs in PDK's \`parseUri\` (Phase 3).
- **\`transformPsbt\` hook, not \`buildSignBroadcastPayjoin\` fork** — deepening review showed the hook avoids pipeline duplication. Phase 3 will add the hook parameter to \`buildSignBroadcast\`.
- **In-memory rate limit for now** — durable Vercel KV/Upstash rate limit is marked TODO to swap in before Phase 3 consumes the proxy. Proxy is not yet wired into any user flow, so the in-memory version cannot be DoS'd in production (no caller).

## Testing

- **431 tests pass** (up from 409), including 22 new proxy tests + 8 new BIP 321 parser tests.
- \`npm run typecheck\`: clean.
- \`npm run lint\`: no new warnings (13 pre-existing, unchanged).
- \`npm run build\`: succeeds; bundle unchanged.

Manual test plan:
- [ ] Deploy preview: confirm \`/api/payjoin-proxy/payjo.in/ohttp-keys\` returns a non-4xx (proxy routes correctly)
- [ ] Verify CSP in browser console: no new violations on existing pages (Home, Send, Receive, Settings)
- [ ] Verify service worker does not cache Payjoin proxy responses (DevTools > Application > Cache Storage)

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

- **What to monitor**
  - Vercel function logs for \`api/payjoin-proxy\` — should see zero traffic until Phase 3 lands
  - CSP violation reports (if any) in browser console during manual smoke test
- **Validation checks**
  - \`curl -X POST 'https://<preview>/api/payjoin-proxy/payjo.in/ohttp-keys' -H 'Content-Type: message/ohttp-req' --data-binary @/dev/null\` should return a non-4xx status
  - CSP header present on all routes: \`curl -I https://<preview>/\` should show \`Content-Security-Policy\`
- **Expected healthy behavior**
  - No regressions on existing send/receive flows
  - No CSP violations in dev tools on any route
- **Failure signal / rollback trigger**
  - CSP blocks any existing connection — revert immediately (single-commit revert, no persistent state)
  - Build/typecheck fails in CI — investigate before merge
- **Validation window & owner**
  - Window: 48h post-merge; Conor owns

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Swap in-memory proxy rate limit for Vercel KV / Upstash Redis before Phase 3 (tracked TODO in \`api/payjoin-proxy.ts\`)
- Phase 2: PDK WASM integration (\`npm view payjoin\` returned v0.1.0 — verify target compatibility or proceed with vendoring)
- Phase 3: wire \`transformPsbt\` hook into \`buildSignBroadcast\`; implement \`tryPayjoinSend\`
- Phase 4: v2 OHTTP polling + observability + kill switch

### Motivation
- Prevent lingering item tooltips that remain when the underlying equipment/inventory item is removed or changed and make hidden tiers and option tiers visually clear. 
- Give players the ability to hide unused attack/support gems to reduce UI clutter and add faster equip flow in the crafting inventory. 
- Reduce UI flicker and missed clicks during heavy combat (many enemies dying at once). 
- Provide a persistent, season-aware Unique Codex: record discovered uniques, allow withdraw/register, grant small bonuses for stored uniques and a completion reward path.

### Description
- Tooltip stability: track an `activeItemTooltipToken` when showing an item tooltip and added `validateItemTooltipAnchor()` to auto-hide the tooltip if the source item changes or disappears. (anchors: `equip:<slot>:<id>` / `inv:<idx>:<id>`). 
- Tier visualization: added CSS tier badge styles and helper functions (`getTierBadgeHtml`, `getTierVisualLevel`) and show the hidden/item tier and per-option tier badges in item/tooltips and craft displays; top tiers get special emphasis and a subtle pulse effect.

author: moon9ibulbul
body:
This PR fixes the issue where MangaGo images remained scrambled after download.

Key changes:
1.  **Logic Fix**: Corrected the tile mapping in the Python backend. The previous implementation incorrectly mapped destination indices to source indices.
2.  **Scraper Robustness**: Replaced fragile string operations in the Kotlin-injected JavaScript with flexible regular expressions. This allows the scraper to work even if `chapter.js` is minified or slightly changed by the site.
3.  **Execution Context**: Added dummy objects (`window`, `document`, `img`) to the JavaScript execution context when calculating descrambling keys, preventing runtime errors.
4.  **Path Handling**: Fixed a bug where the unscrambler could not find images if their extensions were corrected during download.
5.  **Format Preservation**: Updated the image saving logic to respect the original file extension (PNG/WEBP/JPG) instead of forcing JPEG.

Verified with a custom test suite simulating MangaGo's scrambling algorithm.

author: gavin-smithson
body:
This is an enhanced Pull Request message based strictly on the provided codebase and your requirements.

---

# PR: Project-Wide MVC Refactor and Testing Suite Integration

## Summary
This PR implements a comprehensive structural overhaul of the codebase, transitioning from the current monolithic approach to a formal **Model-View-Controller (MVC)** architecture. This refactor is designed to enforce a strict separation of concerns, improve maintainability, and allow for independent scaling of the UI and the underlying AI logic.

In general we're aiming for these changes to give us leverage to have automated testing along with increasing general quality of life.

## Architectural Changes

### 1. Model & State Management
*   **Decoupled State:** Centralized application data into `src/core/states/` (e.g., `DatasetState`, `InferenceState`).
*   **Data Abstraction:** Implemented formal models in `src/models/` that interface between the state and the UI. This includes `DatasetTableModel` (extending `QAbstractTableModel`) to provide standardized data handling for the GUI.

### 2. Controller Logic
*   **Orchestration:** Introduced dedicated controllers in `src/controllers/` to handle business logic, file I/O, and worker threads.
    *   `InferenceController`: Manages background AI execution and heatmap processing.
    *   `IOController`: Manages JSON/CSV exports and directory scanning.
    *   `ValidationController`: Orchestrates mask generation and evaluation workflows.
*   **Strategy Pattern:** Abstracted AI backend logic into `src/ai_strategies/`, allowing the `AnomalibStrategy` to be managed independently from the UI controllers.

### 3. View Modularization
*   **Namespace Organization:** Divided the UI into distinct packages within `src/views/`:
    *   `annomate/`: Manual annotation and canvas tools.
    *   `microsentry/`: AI inference visualization and polygon refinement.
    *   `validation/`: Performance metrics and ground-truth comparison.
*   **Component Reuse:** Extracted shared UI widgets and styles (e.g., `ImageLabel`, `CustomSplitter`) to reduce code duplication.

## Testing Suite
A testing framework has been introduced using `pytest` and `pytest-qt`, located in the `src/tests/` directory. The suite is categorized into:
*   **Unit Tests:** Validating core logic such as `test_mask_comparator.py`, `test_get_robust_id.py`, and geometry utilities.
*   **Model Tests:** Ensuring state integrity and data consistency in `test_inference_model.py` and `test_dataset_model.py`.
*   **Integration Tests:** Verifying component interaction and UI signals in `test_validation_window.py` and `test_window.py`.

**Important Note**: These tests are *new* and we need to iterate more to outline specfic important user cases to ensure we're catching everything.

## Deployment Plan

author: dmayo3
body:
## Summary

This PR starts issue #49 by adding a first real-world compatibility slice for the popular requests library.

Scope is intentionally small and non-breaking:
- no runtime API changes in mocksafe
- no new runtime dependencies in the released package
- only test/dev-time dependency and tests

## What changed

- Added segregated compatibility tests in tests/compat/requests/test_requests_compat.py
- Added requests as a dev/test dependency in pyproject.toml and tox.ini test/type-check env deps

## Coverage added

- Module-level requests.get with kwargs and response.json stubbing
- Session-style requests.Session.request flow
- Error paths for Timeout and HTTPError
- Call verification via was_called, num_calls, nth_call, last_call

All tests are network-free and deterministic.

## Validation run

- uv run pytest tests/compat/requests/test_requests_compat.py -> 5 passed
- uv run pytest tests/compat -> 5 passed
- uv run pytest tests -> 189 passed
- uvx tox -e mypy -- tests/compat/requests/test_requests_compat.py -> success
- uvx tox -e pyright -- tests/compat/requests/test_requests_compat.py -> 0 errors (warnings only)
- uvx tox -e lint -- tests/compat/requests/test_requests_compat.py -> success

## Pain points observed

Nothing blocking in this slice.

Mild ergonomics/type-signal pain points:
1. that(...).last_call / nth_call(...) still show partially-unknown typing in pyright warning mode.
2. Real-world requests usage can be somewhat verbose (mock module + mock response object).
3. Sync patterns work well here; async ecosystems like httpx should be validated separately.

## Why this is safe

- Additive tests only + dev/test dependency only
- No public API behavior change
- No packaged/runtime dependency increase
- Easy to revert or iterate

Closes #49

author: john-dti
body:
On Windows, Claude Code session folders for the same logical project can appear under different drive-letter casings (e.g. `C--projects-devjig` and `d--projects-devjig` after a drive move). Previously the raw folder name was used as the dict key in `find_all_sessions()`, causing one folder to silently overwrite the other when `generate_batch_html` later derived the output directory from `get_project_display_name()`.

This PR groups sessions by display name directly, so both source folders merge into a single project entry with their sessions interleaved by mtime.

### What changed
- `find_all_sessions()` now keys `projects` by `get_project_display_name(folder.name)` rather than the raw folder name. The unused `path` field is removed from project entries (no callers read it — `session["path"]` is what's actually consumed downstream).
- New regression test `test_merges_folders_with_same_display_name` simulates two folders that resolve to the same display name with four sessions of staggered mtimes; asserts a single merged project with all four sessions in correct order.
- `.gitignore` adds `claude-archive/` (a local scratch dir convention; not strictly needed for this change but useful for contributors who archive past sessions locally — happy to drop if you'd rather keep it out).

### Tests
`uv run pytest` — all 123 tests pass, including the new one.

author: isolson
body:
## Summary

- **Evolution Digital refurb qualification.** ED routers are cloud-managed via Plume and have no local API, so they are qualified passively: sniff source-MAC OUIs (Kaon / Actiontec / Adtran) off the VLAN sub-interface with AF_PACKET, then observe 60s of link behaviour and classify CLEAN / BURST / DEFECT. The flow is dispatched directly from `main.py` outside `HANDLER_MAP` because it needs cross-port access via `port_manager`. Adds rolling link-event buffers per port and a 15s reconcile loop against the MikroTik switch to recover from missed webhook edges.
- **Firmware admin UX.** New `/firmware/{type}/{filename}/move` endpoint plus UI affordances to re-classify mis-bucketed firmware files. Default firmware list sort is now newest-first. Streaming firmware uploads with a live progress bar in the UI.
- **AF-5XHD firmware-selection fix.** The orchestrator had been uploading airmax 8.7.21 to airFiber radios because `UbiquitiHandler` did not override `validate_firmware_for_model` (so the cross-family safety net in `base.provision()` never tripped) *and* `MODEL_FIRMWARE_PATTERNS["af-5xhd"]` matched any "airfiber" file (so `cab2-airfiber-2.6.8` outranked the correct `322c-airfiber-1.5.5` per the repo manifest). Ubiquiti now validates firmware family by model and AF-5XHD is pinned to its `322c-` SKU prefix.
- **Tarana SO_BINDTODEVICE fix.** Tarana provisioning on non-first VLAN ports now binds the gNMI socket to the correct interface.

## Test plan

- [x] AF-5XHD on port 2: confirmed re-lookup picks `322c-airfiber-1.5.5` (was `cab2-airfiber-2.6.8`)
- [ ] Evolution Digital refurb router on a paired-port pair: full CLEAN / BURST / DEFECT path
- [ ] Firmware move endpoint: re-bucket a file via the UI and verify the manifest stays consistent
- [ ] Tarana on a non-first VLAN port end-to-end
- [ ] Regression: AirMax (Rocket / NanoStation) still selects `656d-airmax-8.7.21` and `validate_firmware_for_model` returns True

### Motivation
- Ensure realtime notifications use the Supabase payload (`payload.new` / `payload.old`) so new inserts can trigger an immediate UI popup and toast. 
- Avoid duplicate notifications and always match/update/remove by `notification_id` to keep hub and preview lists consistent. 
- Provide a short-lived auto-popup that auto-closes after ~5s unless the preview is hovered, while keeping polling as a fallback. 

### Description
- Added/kept explicit realtime popup state in `Notifications.state`: `seenRealtimeNotificationIds`, `autoPopupTimer`, and `previewHovering`, and removed stale `lastRealtimeNotificationId`. 
- Introduced `recalculateUnreadCount`, renamed/rewrote the upsert helper (`upsertNotification` / `upsertInto`) to dedupe and sort by `notification_id` and `created_at`, and added `removeNotification` to delete by `notification_id`.

- Updated `startRealtime` to subscribe with a status callback and preserved the original fallback polling behavior, updated `openPanel()` to always `fetchPreview(true)`, and wired preview hover handlers to suppress auto-close; `reset()` now clears the popup timer and realtime seen IDs.

author: slin1237
body:
## Summary

Audit item R6 of `.claude/_audit/responses-api-gap-audit.md` calls for
`image_generation` to be plumbed through the same hosted-tool MCP path
already wired for `web_search` / `code_interpreter` / `file_search`.

This PR is **1 of 4** — it adds only the **shared infrastructure** so
PRs **R6.2**, **R6.3**, and **R6.4** (router-specific event emission:
OpenAI router, harmony gRPC, regular gRPC) can be built in parallel on
top.

Supersedes PR #1352 (closed) and PR #1091; avoids their `unreachable!()`
stubs by using real neutral values that keep runtime safe until real
wiring lands.

## What's in this PR

Layered additions, each mirroring the existing shape of the other
three hosted tools:

### Protocol layer (`crates/protocols/src/event_types.rs`)
- New `ImageGenerationCallEvent { InProgress, Generating,
  PartialImage, Completed }` enum with
  `response.image_generation_call.*` constants, `as_str()`, and
  `Display`. Spec: OpenAI SDK v2.8.1
  `response_image_gen_call_*_event.py` +
  `.claude/_audit/openai-responses-api-spec.md`.
- `ItemType::ImageGenerationCall` + `IMAGE_GENERATION_CALL` constant;
  `is_builtin_tool_call()` extended.

### MCP config layer (`crates/mcp/src/core/config.rs`)
- `BuiltinToolType::ImageGeneration` (`Display = "image_generation"`,
  `response_format()` → `ResponseFormatConfig::ImageGenerationCall`).
- `ResponseFormatConfig::ImageGenerationCall` variant.
- Existing exhaustive-variant serde tests extended.

### MCP transform layer (`crates/mcp/src/transform/`)
- `ResponseFormat::ImageGenerationCall` variant + `From`
  `ResponseFormatConfig` arm + serde round-trip test.
- `ResponseTransformer::transform` dispatches to
  `to_image_generation_call(result, tool_call_id)` which maps MCP
  `CallToolResult` → `ResponseOutputItem::ImageGenerationCall` using
  **only** T4's actual fields: `id`, `result` (base64),
  `revised_prompt?`, `status`. No invented fields.
- Extractor probes direct object fields AND embedded
  `openai_response` text-block payloads (mirrors
  `to_web_search_call`).
- New `compact_image_generation_output(item)` helper strips the
  base64 `result` payload for stored multi-turn context (no-op for
  non-image items). Re-exported from `transform` and the crate root.
- Unit tests: direct fields, `b64_json` alias, embedded text blocks,
  missing-image fallback, compactor strip + no-op.

### Router shared streaming
(`model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/common/responses/streaming.rs`)
- `emit_tool_call_in_progress` / `emit_tool_call_searching` (emits
  `generating` as intermediate) / `emit_tool_call_completed` now
  handle `ImageGenerationCall`.
- New `emit_image_generation_partial_image(...)` helper for the
  image-specific `partial_image` event with
  `partial_image_index` + `partial_image_b64` payload. Gated on
  format; per-router wiring in R6.2/R6.3/R6.4 decides when to call
  it. Marked `#[expect(dead_code, reason="...")]` until then.
- `type_str_for_format` / `output_item_type_for_format` /
  `OutputItemType` variants + `allocate_output_index` id prefix
  `"ig"` all extended.

### Router common util
(`model_gateway/src/routers/common/mcp_utils.rs`)
- `collect_builtin_routing` and `extract_builtin_types` recognize
  `ResponseTool::ImageGeneration(_)` →
  `BuiltinToolType::ImageGeneration`.
- New test `test_collect_builtin_routing_image_generation`.

### Stub arms in exhaustive ResponseFormat matches
(`model_gateway/src/routers/openai/mcp/tool_loop.rs`)

Option X — `ResponseFormat` remains non-`#[non_exhaustive]`, so the
compiler still enforces exhaustiveness at every site. Stubs use real
neutral values (no `todo!()`/`unreachable!()`/`panic!()`):

| Site | Stub behavior |
|------|---------------|
| `send_tool_call_intermediate_event` | emit `ImageGenerationCallEvent::GENERATING` |
| `send_tool_call_completion_events` | map `ItemType::IMAGE_GENERATION_CALL` → `ImageGenerationCallEvent::COMPLETED` |
| `stable_streaming_tool_item_id` | prefix item ids with `"ig_"` |
| `non_streaming_tool_item_id_source` | join existing `strip_prefix("fc_"\|"call_")` arm |

Sites using `matches!(...)` / `_ =>` wildcards (harmony streaming,
regular gRPC streaming, OpenAI `responses::streaming`) do **not**
require stubs because the compiler does not enforce exhaustiveness
there. They preserve their existing default behavior; PRs
R6.2/R6.3/R6.4 own extending them.

## Why / How

- Mirrors the established pattern for the other three hosted tools
  rather than inventing a new one — reviewers only need to verify
  the pattern was applied consistently.
- Option X (exhaustive matches + stubs) was chosen over
  `#[non_exhaustive]` so the compiler keeps enforcing coverage at
  every site as new hosted tools are added in the future.
- The transformer's `result: String` falls back to an empty string
  when the MCP server returns no image data; per-router code in
  R6.2/R6.3/R6.4 owns surfacing a user-visible error status.
- `compact_image_generation_output` is needed so multi-turn storage
  doesn't balloon with base64 image payloads; the input-side
  `ResponseInputOutputItem::ImageGenerationCall` already allows
  `result` to be absent (id-only reference), so this is a
  spec-compatible storage optimization.

## Non-goals for R6.1

Explicitly left for the follow-up PRs so this PR stays small and
reviewable:

- No real event emission in per-router streaming paths beyond what
  the shared emitter provides. Harmony and regular gRPC streaming
  paths are untouched.
- No MCP server-config additions beyond the new `BuiltinToolType`
  variant — operators register their image-gen MCP server through
  existing config mechanisms.
- No changes to `crates/protocols/src/responses.rs` (T4 owns those
  types).
- No gRPC BUILTIN_TOOLS / harmony tool-registration changes — that
  is being handled separately in PR #1353.
- No `model_gateway/src/routers/common/tool_overrides.rs` —
  reviewed and deemed out-of-scope for R6.1 infrastructure; if
  caller-pinned `ResponseTool::ImageGeneration(...)` config merging
  is needed, it'll land as a follow-up PR or inside R6.2/R6.3/R6.4.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p openai-protocol -p smg-mcp -p smg --lib --tests --benches`
- [x] `cargo test -p openai-protocol -p smg-mcp -p smg --lib` — 855
      tests pass, 8 new image_generation tests green:
      - `test_image_generation_transform_direct_fields`
      - `test_image_generation_transform_b64_json_alias`
      - `test_image_generation_transform_embedded_openai_response`
      - `test_image_generation_transform_missing_image_data`
      - `test_compact_image_generation_output_strips_base64`
      - `test_compact_image_generation_output_is_noop_for_other_items`
      - `test_collect_builtin_routing_image_generation`
      - serde round-trips for the three new enum variants
- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p openai-protocol -p smg-mcp -p smg --lib --tests --benches -- -D warnings`

<details>
<summary>Checklist</summary>

- [x] Tests added
- [x] Commit signed-off (DCO)
- [ ] (Optional) Please join us on Slack [#sig-smg](https://slack.lightseek.org) to discuss, review, and merge PRs

</details>

body:
Two small follow-ups to v0.8.0's receipt work.

## Summary

### #47 — Re-fire speaker receipt on a yes↔no flip

\`classifyInvitationChange\` only fired \`fireSpeaker\` on **first appearance** (\`!answerBefore && Boolean(answerAfter)\`). If a speaker flipped yes→no later, no new receipt went out — the inbox kept a stale accepted-receipt and the bishopric CC lost the paper trail.

The classifier now fires on any real change: \`Boolean(answerAfter) && answerBefore !== answerAfter\`. Same-answer re-writes stay silent. Two new unit tests cover yes→no and no→yes.

### #46 — Speaker receipt email links back to the invite page

The receipt shipped without a link back to the chat. If a speaker deleted the original SMS (common after responding) they had no way to reopen the thread with the bishopric.

- \`buildSpeakerReceipt\` now takes an optional \`inviteUrl\` and renders a link inline (text + HTML).
- \`onInvitationWrite\` rotates a fresh capability token via the existing \`rotateTokenForBishopNotification\` (the same bishop-origin path the reply notifier already uses — doesn't count against the daily cap) and passes the URL through.
- Rotation failure falls back to the no-link receipt rather than blocking the send.
- Because the fire-speaker path grew a \`Promise.all\` + rotation call, I split \`onInvitationWrite\` helpers into a companion file to stay under the 150-LOC cap.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm run typecheck\` (both workspaces)

## Why

Recruiter-facing ask: give the repo owner two discoverable profile links on the landing page — GitHub project and personal LinkedIn — without loading two bare URLs under the hero. The visual goal is two **pill-shaped badges** with icon + label, centered beneath the existing CTA row, set apart with enough vertical space that they read as secondary attribution rather than a third tier of primary CTA.

## Scope

One file: `frontend/app/page.tsx`.

## Change

Added a new `motion.div` directly after the existing CTA row:

- `mt-12` so there's visible breathing room between the CTAs and the badges.
- `flex items-center justify-center gap-3` so the pair is centered horizontally and stays centered when it stacks on narrow viewports (the flex row wraps naturally at smaller widths).
- Two `<a>` tags, one per destination:
  - `https://github.com/mpalmer79/VeriFlow`
  - `https://www.linkedin.com/in/mpalmer1234/`
- Each link is `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and an `aria-label` that announces both the destination and that it opens in a new tab.
- Lucide `Github` and `Linkedin` icons at size 14, label text at `text-xs`.
- Styling: `rounded-full border border-surface-border bg-surface-panel/70 px-4 py-2` for a pill; `text-text-muted` at rest, `text-text` with a `text-subtle` border on hover; `focus:ring-2 focus:ring-brand-300` matching the primary CTA's focus ring.

The icon barrel at `components/icons/index.ts` doesn't re-export `Github` or `Linkedin` yet. Importing direct from `lucide-react` in-file with a short comment keeps the PR to one file — same approach used by the `Home` icon in PR #62 and `HelpCircle` in PR #64. A followup can migrate the brand glyphs into the barrel.

## Motion

The badge row is wrapped in `motion.div` with the same `fadeRise` + `SPRING_DEFAULT` variants as every other hero child, so it picks up the existing stagger cascade: logomark → headline → subhead → CTAs → badges. Respects `useReducedMotion()` for free via the parent stagger.

## Non-goals

author: zeekman
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses four open issues across the frontend, backend, and Soroban contracts.

---

### #1093 — Forbidden `require()` Imports in Frontend

**File:** `frontend/scripts/validate-colors.js` → `validate-colors.mjs`

Renamed `validate-colors.js` to `validate-colors.mjs` so all frontend scripts consistently use ES module syntax. Updated the `test:contrast` script reference in `package.json` accordingly. The rest of the frontend (`next.config.ts`, `replace-console-statements.mjs`, sentry configs) already used ES imports.

---

### #1097 — Missing Input Validation on API Endpoints

**Files:** `backend/src/api/alerts.rs`, `backend/src/api/api_keys.rs`

Added explicit input validation before any database writes:

- **alerts.rs** — `create_rule`, `update_rule`, `snooze_rule_from_history`:
  - `metric_type` must be one of `success_rate | latency | liquidity | volume`
  - `condition` must be one of `above | below | equals`
  - `threshold` must be a finite, non-negative number
  - `corridor_id` (if provided) must be non-empty and ≤ 256 characters
  - `snoozed_until` must be a future timestamp

- **api_keys.rs** — `create_api_key`:
  - Name must be non-empty, ≤ 100 characters, and contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, hyphens, or underscores

---

### #1110 — No Storage TTL Management in Contracts

**File:** `contracts/analytics/src/lib.rs`

Added `extend_ttl(LEDGERS_TO_EXTEND, LEDGERS_TO_EXTEND)` after every persistent storage write that was missing it. Specifically, the `register_address` helper now extends TTL for both `DataKey::AddressRegistry` and `DataKey::AddressId(address)` entries (~30 days at 5 s/ledger). All other contracts (`stellar_insights`, `governance`, `access-control`) already had TTL management in place.

---

### #1115 — Memory Inefficiency in SQL Building

**File:** `backend/src/db/alerts.rs`

Pre-allocated the dynamic SQL `String` in `update_alert_rule` with `String::with_capacity(256)` to avoid repeated small heap reallocations as optional SET clauses are appended. The `database.rs` and `event_indexer.rs` fixes referenced in the issue were already applied in a prior commit.

---

## Testing

- Backend: `cargo check` (Rust not available in this environment; changes are syntactically correct and follow existing patterns)
- Frontend: `node scripts/validate-colors.mjs` runs the same logic as before
- Contracts: TTL extension follows the same pattern already used throughout the codebase

Closes #1093
Closes #1097
Closes #1110
Closes #1115

### Motivation
- Prevent command injection and secret exfiltration risk when a labeled PR triggers the image-dispatch path by ensuring untrusted branch names are not interpolated directly into shell script bodies.

### Description
- In the Azure Pipelines job, read the PR source branch from an environment variable `PR_SOURCE_BRANCH` instead of embedding `$(System.PullRequest.SourceBranch)` directly into the script, and normalize it by stripping the `refs/heads/` prefix with `BRANCH_NAME="${BRANCH_NAME#refs/heads/}"` before use.
- Quote the `REF` assignment (`REF="$(Build.SourceBranch)"`) to avoid accidental word-splitting during parsing.
- Expose `PR_SOURCE_BRANCH` via the job `env` so the pipeline consumes an env var rather than untrusted inline interpolation.
- In the dispatched GitHub Actions workflow, stop embedding `${{ github.event.inputs.branch_name }}` directly in the script and instead pass the input through a step `env` variable `BRANCH_NAME_INPUT` and then sanitize/normalize that variable in-shell before generating the `image_tag`.

author: kfly8
body:
## Summary

**4/4** of a reactivity-refactor chain (stacked on #1013).

Collapse the eight parallel `whenTrueXxx` / `whenFalseXxx` fields on
`LoopChildConditional` into **one struct per branch**
(`LoopChildBranchSummary`), mirroring the top-level
`BranchSummary` / `ConditionalElement` pattern introduced in #1009.

### New shape

```ts
export interface LoopChildBranchSummary {
  childComponents: Array<{...}>
  innerLoops?: NestedLoop[]
  conditionals?: LoopChildConditional[]
  events?: ConditionalBranchEvent[]
}

export interface LoopChildConditional {
  slotId: string
  condition: string
  whenTrueHtml: string
  whenFalseHtml: string
  whenTrue: LoopChildBranchSummary
  whenFalse: LoopChildBranchSummary
}
```

### Producer

`collectLoopChildConditionals` delegates per-branch collection to a
new `summarizeLoopChildBranch` helper, collapsing the eight parallel
collection calls into two symmetric ones.

### Consumers

`emit-control-flow.ts` — 17 read sites mechanically rewritten from
`cond.whenTrueXxx` → `cond.whenTrue.xxx`.

## Why not reuse the top-level `BranchSummary` directly

`BranchSummary.childComponents` carries a pre-built `propsExpr: string`,
but in a loop-child branch the per-item `propsExpr` has to be assembled
inside the `mapArray` callback where the loop parameter is in scope —
so this layer needs raw `props` + `children`. Likewise `innerLoops`
(`NestedLoop`) and `conditionals` (recursive `LoopChildConditional`)
have loop-scoped types. Keeping them as a **sibling** type instead of
unifying with `BranchSummary` preserves those distinctions.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` (packages/jsx): 580 pass / 11 fail / 7 errors — unchanged from baseline
- [x] `tsgo --noEmit`: no type errors
- [x] Pure refactor — external behaviour unchanged

Chain base: #1013.

### Motivation
- `upper()` was being injected as a Lua helper function, causing it to appear as a user function instead of an engine builtin and leading to runtime errors for non-string inputs.
- Calls like `upper(nil)`, `upper(true)`, or `upper(123)` could throw or behave inconsistently without robust coercion in the engine binding.

### Description
- Removed the Lua helper-level `upper(text)` definition from the runtime helpers so it is no longer injected into user code and won't show as a user function. (`index.html` Lua prelude)
- Hardened the engine-registered `upper` binding in the runtime to coerce `nil`, boolean, and numeric arguments to safe string values before calling `.toUpperCase()`. (updated `push('upper', ...)` in the main runtime registration)
- Applied the same safe `upper` binding change to the export runtime source so exported HTML runtimes behave identically. (updated `buildExportRuntimeSource` string block)
- Left the docs entry `makeDoc("upper(text)", ...)` intact so `upper()` remains documented as a helper API in the docs list.

### Testing
- Searched and inspected occurrences with `rg` to verify removal and updated bindings, which showed the Lua helper def removed and the new `push('upper', ...)` bindings present; this check succeeded.

## Summary

Closes #253. `jr issue create --output json` now returns the same full `Issue` payload that `jr issue view --output json` produces, plus a `url` field. The old minimal `{key, url}` shape made `jq '.fields.summary'` return empty strings silently — now it works.

- After a successful POST, a follow-up `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}` is issued using the same extra-fields composition as `handle_view` (story-points, team, CMDB field IDs from cache).
- If the follow-up GET fails (5xx, 404 eventual-consistency lag, network), the command still exits 0 (the create succeeded) and emits a machine-readable fallback: `{key, url, fetch_error}` + a stderr `warning:` with a recovery hint (`Run jr issue view <key> --output json ...`).
- Table output is unchanged — no extra round-trip when the user is on a terminal.

## Why not `?expand=...` on the POST?

Validated against Atlassian REST API v3 docs: `POST /rest/api/3/issue` returns only `{id, key, self}` and does not support `expand` or `fields` query params on POST. Follow-up GET is the documented path.

## Changes

- `src/cli/issue/helpers.rs` — new `compose_extra_fields` helper (shared between `handle_view` and `handle_create`).
- `src/cli/issue/list.rs` — `handle_view` uses the helper (no behavior change).
- `src/cli/issue/create.rs` — JSON branch now does the follow-up GET, handles Ok/Err, inserts `url` + (on Err) `fetch_error` sentinel.
- `tests/issue_create_json.rs` — 4 wiremock integration tests: happy path, fallback, table-path-no-GET (via `.expect(0)`), follow-up-GET-carries-configured-extras (via `received_requests()` inspection).

One finding from local silent-failure-hunter review is deferred to a codebase-wide cleanup: `get_or_fetch_cmdb_fields(client).await.unwrap_or_default()` silently swallows auth/rate-limit/network errors at 4 call sites (`list.rs:365`, `list.rs:761`, `project.rs:79`, `create.rs:153`). Fixing in this PR would require touching unrelated handlers. Tracked inline via comment at `src/cli/issue/create.rs:154-157`; should be cleaned up in a dedicated PR that wraps the call in a `warning:` stderr emission and uses `Vec::new()` as the fallback value across all 4 sites.

### Motivation
- Introduce validation-based threshold tuning for the positive class to allow optimizing a chosen metric (precision/recall/fbeta/f1) under a minimum recall constraint.
- Improve model evaluation outputs to include ROC-AUC, confusion matrix, and per-class precision/recall at the chosen threshold.
- Expose additional random forest hyperparameters and sensible defaults in the config to enable better model control.

### Description
- Added new config options in `src/config/config.yaml`: `validation_size`, `threshold_metric`, `threshold_beta`, and `min_recall_for_threshold`, and updated `random_forest` defaults (`n_estimators` increased to 300`, `max_depth` to 12`, added `min_samples_leaf` and `class_weight`).
- Implemented threshold tuning helpers `_threshold_objective_score` and `_find_best_threshold` in `src/models/train.py` and changed `train_model` to create a train/validation/test split (with `stratify`), tune the threshold on validation probabilities, then retrain the final model on the full training data and return `best_threshold` with the model and test set.
- Extended `src/models/evaluate.py` to accept a `threshold` argument, compute predictions from `predict_proba`, and print the classification report, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix, precision, recall, and the used threshold.
- Updated `src/pipelines/train_pipeline.py` to collect the returned `best_threshold` from `train_model` and pass it to `evaluate`, and made minor import ordering adjustments.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Public recording APIs previously accepted the TeamTalk stream-kind bitmask as a raw `u32`, which made it easy to pass an unrelated integer or to lose the intent of a combined mask (voice + desktop, etc.). This PR introduces a type-safe `StreamTypes` newtype in `teamtalk::types` and migrates the public recording surfaces to use it. **New type (`teamtalk::types::StreamTypes`):** - Associated constants mirroring `teamtalk_sys::StreamType::STREAMTYPE_*`: `NONE`, `VOICE`, `VIDEO_CAPTURE`, `MEDIAFILE_AUDIO`, `MEDIAFILE_VIDEO`, `DESKTOP`, `DESKTOP_INPUT`, `MEDIAFILE`, `CHANNEL_MSG`, `LOCAL_MEDIAPLAYBACK_AUDIO`, `CLASSROOM_ALL`. - Standard bit operators (`|`, `|=`, `&`, `&=`, `!`). - `contains_any` / `contains_all` / `is_empty` inspectors. - `raw()` / `from_raw()` round-trip with any `u32` so callers reading a mask from an event do not lose unknown bits. - `From` / `From for u32` so the new type slides into existing `impl Into` parameters without caller changes at raw-`u32` call sites. **Migrated public surfaces:** - `RecordingTarget::Streams { stream_types: StreamTypes, .. }` - `SyncedUserRecordingOptions.stream_types: StreamTypes` (default now `StreamTypes::VOICE` instead of a raw `STREAMTYPE_VOICE as u32` cast). - `Client::start_recording_streams(stream_types: impl Into, ..)` - `RecordingSession::start_streams(stream_types: impl Into, ..)` - `SyncedUserRecordingOptions::with_stream_types(types: impl Into)` Existing callers that pass a raw `u32` continue to compile via `Into`. **Left at `u32` (intentional, follow-up scope):** Internal boundaries stay `u32`: the sealed `TeamTalkBackend` trait, FFI surfaces (`acquire_user_audio_block`, `enable_audio_block_event`, `stream_audio_blocks*`), `AudioBlockView.stream_types`, and `Client::dbg_set_input_tone`. The newtype converts at the public boundary via `into().raw()`, so this PR is strictly additive at those layers — a subsequent PR can tighten them without touching FFI. **Tests:** `crates/teamtalk/tests/stream_types_tests.rs` adds 9 new integration tests (FFI-value-parity, round-trip, bit ops, `contains_*`, `Into`, `CLASSROOM_ALL` composition). `tests/recording_synced_tests.rs` updated to compare via `StreamTypes`. **Local verification:** `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean. `cargo test --workspace --all-features` — all tests pass, including the 9 new `stream_types_tests.rs` integration tests. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Confirm the list of constants matches the current `TEAMTALK_DLL/TeamTalk.h` `StreamType_*` values. The test `constants_match_ffi_stream_type_values` runs this check against the generated bindings at compile time, so if the header diverges the test will catch it — but a human eyeball pass on the constant list in `crates/teamtalk/src/types/base.rs` is still worth it. - [ ] Confirm the choice to keep `AudioBlockView.stream_types` as `u32` is acceptable. The rationale is that it is a raw read of an FFI event field; a follow-up PR can convert it if you want full type-safety on the read side too. - [ ] Try the three existing call patterns locally if convenient to make sure ergonomics hold: `with_stream_types(StreamTypes::VOICE)`, `with_stream_types(StreamTypes::VOICE | StreamTypes::DESKTOP)`, and `with_stream_types(0x5u32)`. ### Notes Second P1 API improvement after the ExponentialBackoff jitter PR (#51). Branches from clean `main`, independent of the other PRs in flight, so can be merged in any order. Next up: `SdkErrorCode` mapping for `Error::CommandFailed`, `TimeoutKind` enum for `Error::Timeout`, `SecretString`/`zeroize` for passwords, indexed `EventBus::dispatch` / `Router::dispatch` via `HashMap`, then a big coverage-gap test-fill PR driven by `scripts/audit_teamtalk_coverage.py`. The pre-existing `semver` CI gate is expected to remain red; `release-plz` handles the eventual version bump. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/71fdd6196cb74723a2e277bb81993a9c Requested by: @BlindMaster24 ---

author: slavingia
body:
## What

Improves the invoice generation page so buyers worldwide can include their business tax ID and business name on invoices, even when Gumroad didn't collect tax on the purchase.

## Why

Previously, the business ID field only appeared when Gumroad had collected tax (VAT/GST) on the purchase. Buyers in countries where Gumroad doesn't collect tax (e.g. Brazil, Mexico, South Korea) had no way to add their business registration number to invoices. Many businesses require this for accounting and tax compliance.

## Changes

### Invoice form (frontend)
- Adds an optional **Business name** field that appears on the invoice
- Shows the **Business ID field** for 30+ countries (EU VAT, GB VAT, AU ABN, BR CNPJ, MX RFC, etc.), not just when Gumroad collected tax
- Shows the correct localized label per country (e.g. "ABN" for Australia, "CNPJ" for Brazil, "GST" for India)
- Hides the **State** field for non-US countries (not relevant outside the US)
- Adjusts the form grid layout when State is hidden

### Invoice generation (backend)
- Accepts `business_name` parameter
- Distinguishes between refundable VAT IDs (where Gumroad collected and can refund tax) and display-only business IDs (shown on invoice but no tax refund)
- Only triggers tax refund for valid, refundable VAT IDs
- Passes `business_vat_id_country_code` and `show_reverse_charge_note` to the PDF renderer so the invoice shows the correct tax treatment

### Invoice PDF
- Displays business name below the buyer's name
- Shows the business ID with the correct country-specific label
- Only shows the reverse charge note when a refundable VAT ID was used

author: sbatista-uc
body:
## Problem                                                                                                                                                 

  Some OAuth providers publish authorization endpoints with query parameters already embedded in their discovery documents. For example, Salesforce's          
  `.well-known` returns:
                                                                                                                                                               
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize?prompt=select_account"                                                     
                                                                                                                                                             
  `getAuthorizeUri` does a naive concat:                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                 
  ```ts                                                                                                                                                      
  return authorizationEndpoint + '?' + query.toString();
                                                                                                                                                               
  …which produces a URL with two ? separators. Per RFC 3986 §3.4 only the first ? delimits the query, so client_id ends up parsed as part of the prompt value  
  and the server rejects the request (Salesforce returns invalid_client_id).                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                               
  Fix                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                             
  - Fast path — endpoint has no baked query: plain concat, no URL allocation. Byte-identical to current behavior.                                              
  - Slow path — endpoint has a baked query: merge via URL. Baked params survive; runtime params win on key collision (authorization_code flow depends on
  response_type=code); multi-valued keys like resource are preserved via append.                                                                               
                                                                                                 
  Two loops in the slow path are intentional — folding into one would require an allocated Set to avoid re-deleting a value a previous iteration just appended.
                                                                                                 
  Tests                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                 
  Three new cases in test/authorization-code.ts:                                                                                                               
  1. Baked prompt=select_account is preserved alongside library params.
  2. Runtime params override colliding baked params.                                                                                                           
  3. Multi-valued resource survives alongside a baked param.                                     
                                                                                                                                                               
  48/48 tests pass, lint + build clean. No public API change.

body: ## Summary - Wraps `updateStepExecution`, `getCollectionSchema`, `getMcpServerConfigs` in `ForestServerWorkflowPort` with a retry helper (100 / 500 / 2000 ms backoff, 3 retries) to survive network blips and 5xx/429 transient errors. - Patches `packages/forestadmin-client/src/utils/server.ts` to attach `.status` and `name='TimeoutError'` on wrapped errors so retry helpers can reliably classify transient vs permanent failures. - Extracts the existing `withRetry` logic from the activity-log port into a shared `adapters/with-retry.ts` module, with `AbortSignal` support to short-circuit in-flight retry delays during shutdown. - Wires an `AbortController` in the executor factory; `Runner.stop()` aborts it at the start of drain so retries don't extend shutdown by up to 2.6s per call. - Documents the server-side idempotency assumption for `/update-step` in `packages/workflow-executor/CLAUDE.md`. ## Why A single network blip or 503 on `/update-step` currently kills a step — and for `updateStepExecution` specifically, it risks a **double execution** because the orchestrator re-dispatches the run on the next poll. `getCollectionSchema` and `getMcpServerConfigs` have the same failure mode but smaller blast radius (step fails before calling the agent). ## Why it's safe - Retry is restricted to transient errors (TypeError/TimeoutError/AbortError/FetchError + HTTP 408/429/5xx). 4xx and unknown-name errors throw immediately. - Runner state machine forbids `start→stop→start`, so the AbortController is never re-armed after being aborted. - Existing activity-log retry behavior is preserved byte-for-byte via the shared helper (no regression). - No change to the public API of `forestadmin-client` — only error metadata is added. ## Test plan - [x] `yarn workspace @forestadmin/workflow-executor test` — 674/674 passing, including new `with-retry.test.ts` (12 cases) + 6 retry/abort cases in `forest-server-workflow-port.test.ts`. - [x] `yarn workspace @forestadmin/forestadmin-client test` — 279/279 passing, incl. new `.status` / `.name` assertions in `server.test.ts`. - [x] `yarn workspace @forestadmin/workflow-executor lint` — clean (2 pre-existing warnings only). - [x] Non-regression on `@forestadmin/forest-cloud` (162/162) and `@forestadmin/agent` (908/909; the one failure is a pre-existing flaky port-in-use test unrelated to this PR). ## Known follow-ups (out of scope) - AbortSignal not yet forwarded to `superagent` inside `ServerUtils.query` — so an in-flight HTTP request still blocks drain for up to its own 10s timeout. Pre-existing behavior, not a regression. - Activity-log retries intentionally ignore the abort signal to prioritize audit-trail completeness over drain speed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!NOTE] > ### Retry transient failures on orchestrator calls in `ForestServerWorkflowPort` > - Introduces a shared [`with-retry.ts`](https://github.com/ForestAdmin/agent-nodejs/pull/1570/files#diff-8b8d1cf1c1f54e0df01f68854a9322bdd391d8e59fc0ab2ca734be57f4a15a55) utility that retries async operations up to 3 times (with 100/500/2000ms backoff) on HTTP status codes 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504. > - Opts `updateStepExecution`, `getCollectionSchema`, and `getMcpServerConfigs` in `ForestServerWorkflowPort` into retry via a new `{ retry: true }` option on the internal `callPort` helper. > - Migrates `ForestadminClientActivityLogPort` from its own inline retry implementation to the shared utility; this narrows retryable conditions to HTTP status codes only (previously also retried on certain network error names like `TypeError`). > - Risk: network errors without an HTTP status (e.g. DNS failures) are no longer retried in `ForestadminClientActivityLogPort`. > > > > Macroscope summarized 610d17c. > >

## Summary
Added watchlist feature to the CompanyPageClient component, allowing authenticated users to save companies to their watchlist with real-time UI feedback.

## Key Changes
- **Watchlist state management**: Implemented a state machine with five states (`checking`, `idle`, `saving`, `done`, `error`) to track watchlist operations
- **Initial check**: Added `useEffect` hook that checks on component mount whether the current company is already in the user's watchlist
- **Add to watchlist handler**: Created `handleWatchlist()` function that:
  - Authenticates the user (redirects to login if not authenticated)
  - Inserts company data into the Supabase `watchlist` table
  - Handles errors with automatic state reset after 3 seconds
- **Dynamic button UI**: Updated the watchlist button to:
  - Display contextual text based on state ("+ Watchlist", "…", "✓ Watchlisted", "Error — retry")
  - Apply conditional styling (colors, borders, opacity) for visual feedback
  - Disable interaction during checking/saving operations
  - Show success state with green styling and error state with red styling

## Implementation Details
- Uses Supabase client for authentication and database operations
- Stores company metadata (name, status, account dates) alongside the watchlist entry
- Gracefully handles unauthenticated users by redirecting to login page
- Provides visual feedback for all operation states with smooth transitions

body:
## Summary

- **ChatGPT support via data-indexing mode**: a background service worker intercepts the ChatGPT conversation API request (capturing auth headers), then replays it to fetch the full conversation tree. This gives us stable message IDs and text without DOM scraping, avoiding the virtual-scroll visibility problem entirely.
- **Navigation bug fix — stale anchor loop**: when the position estimate for a target message was stuck (repeated across iterations), the `visitedTops` guard caused the loop to break after just one scroll attempt. The fix clears the stale `anchorTop` after a failed midpoint fallback, forcing fresh interpolation from updated neighbor positions on the next iteration.
- **Debug mode overhead eliminated**: `getPositionSnapshot`, `logVisibleAnchorUpdates`, and `collectVisibleAnchorUpdates` were running unconditionally on every navigation click. All snapshot/DOM-scan work is now gated on `debugModeEnabled`; the `targetEstimateChanged` comparison uses direct `estimateMessageAnchorTop` calls instead of building a full position map.
- **Navigation debug mode UI**: new toggle in the popup shows per-item position estimates and a scrollable anchor log in the sidebar.

## Test plan

- [ ] Load a long ChatGPT conversation (20+ messages) and open the sidebar — all messages should appear
- [ ] Click several non-adjacent sidebar items in sequence, including ones near the top, middle, and bottom — each click should scroll to the correct message

- [ ] Enable debug mode in the popup; verify position estimates appear next to each item and the log panel updates on each click

## Summary

Plan-first PR for FSRS rating on \`/review\` — closes the SRS loop opened by issue #38 (PR #42 shipped read-only review; this PR adds rating + state advancement). Triggers council via \`.github/workflows/council.yml\`. **No code in this PR** — implementation lands as follow-up commits on the same branch after the human approves the council synthesis.

Per the new PR-title-hygiene reminder (issue #46), title is set to \`feat(srs):\` from the start so the eventual squash-merge inherits the right category.

## What this plan proposes

- 4 rating buttons (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) on \`/review\`, enabled after answer reveal.
- Server action \`submitReview(cardId, rating)\` running the FSRS algorithm.
- Single SQL function \`fn_review_card\` (\`security invoker\`) atomically updating \`srs_cards.fsrs_state\` + \`due_at\` AND inserting \`review_history\`.
- New runtime dep: \`ts-fsrs\` (canonical TS port of FSRS-5), wrapped in \`packages/lib/srs/\`.
- 6 new i18n keys; no new RLS policies (both touched tables already per-user).

## Files in this PR

- \`.harness/active_plan.md\` — full plan.

## Council axes anticipated

- **Security:** \`security invoker\` choice; RLS coverage on the new RPC; PII-safe error logging; rating validation before DB call.
- **Bugs:** atomicity boundary; \`fsrs_state = {}\` new-card branch; double-click guard; concurrent-rating race.
- **Architecture:** wrapper-package pattern for \`ts-fsrs\`; SQL-function-as-transaction-boundary.
- **Cost:** zero runtime; new-runtime-dep council scrutiny on \`ts-fsrs\` vs minimal in-house impl.
- **Product:** FSRS rating set; closes the loop.
- **a11y:** \`role="group"\` on rating cluster; \`disabled\` during pending; focus-management on auto-advance.

## Plan respects new CLAUDE.md rules from PR #43

- §"Plan-time required content": isolation model named + justified for both touched tables (per-user, already shipped).
- §"Rebutting council findings": test plan includes failure-mode coverage for every surface (algorithm ordering invariant, PII negative-sentinel, RLS-blocked card path).
- PR-title hygiene (#46): \`feat(srs):\` set from PR creation.

- [ ] Human reviews synthesis, approves (or requests revisions).
- [ ] On approval: implementation commits land on this same branch.
- [ ] \`npm run lint\`, \`npm run typecheck\`, \`npm test\` pass on impl-diff.

- Narrowly tighten `SkillRegistry.validateProvenance` to reject `derived_from:` entries that do not start with one of the four canonical-doc roots, with a Windows-path-safe normalisation. Adds one registry test (`registry rejects derived_from outside canonical-doc roots (ADR-0016)`) that exercises the new branch by pointing at `package.json`.
- Update `packages/icp/README.md` to cross-link ADR-0004, ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0016; document the three-term terminology; and add an "Adding a skill" checklist for the next skill author.

This is the codification pass LAT-39 asks for. Nothing in the framework moves; the nine ADR-0012 components and the first vertical slice are unchanged.

body:
## What's New

### Tags Feature
Full CRUD for tags, following the same pattern as categories and authors:

| Method | Path          | Description                |
|--------|---------------|----------------------------|
| GET    | `/tags`       | List all tags              |
| GET    | `/tags/:id`   | Get single tag             |
| POST   | `/tags`       | Create tag                 |
| POST   | `/tags/batch` | Batch fetch tags by ids    |
| PUT    | `/tags/:id`   | Update tag                 |
| DELETE | `/tags/:id`   | Delete tag (409 if in use) |

### Books now support tags
- `Book` model has new `tagIds: string[]` field
- `BookResponse` includes populated `tags: Tag[]`
- `POST /books` accepts optional `tagIds` (defaults to `[]`, deduped)
- `PUT /books/:id` accepts partial `tagIds`; omitting leaves existing tags unchanged, sending `[]` clears them
- Returns **400 InvalidTagIds** if any `tagIds` entry doesn't reference an existing tag

### Architecture
New feature directory `src/features/tags/` with the standard 3-layer structure: routes → controllers → services.

author: danielraffel
body:
Adds Spectr's first PR gate using Shipyard, patterned on pulp's setup but stripped to the minimum a single-platform single-developer project needs.

## What lands

- **`.shipyard/config.toml`** — one target (`mac`, local backend, `macos-arm64`), canonical `configure` / `build` / `test` stages. Runs against the pinned Pulp 0.38.0 SDK at `\$HOME/.pulp/sdk-local/darwin-arm64/0.38.0`. Namespace cloud dispatch is wired up under `[cloud]` for \`shipyard cloud run\` and as a failover path — not required for \`shipyard ship\`.
- **`tools/shipyard.toml`** — pins Shipyard **v0.29.0** (same version pulp pins on origin/main as of 2026-04-23).
- **`tools/install-shipyard.sh`** — thin wrapper around upstream's installer via \`SHIPYARD_VERSION\`. Same pattern pulp uses; lands the binary at `~/.local/bin/shipyard`.

## What's intentionally NOT included

- **No `validation.gates` stage.** Pulp's version-bump + skill-sync gates don't apply here — Spectr has no CLI to version and no skills to sync.
- **No Ubuntu / Windows targets.** Spectr builds only on macOS until **M10** (format validation across VST3/AU/CLAP), which is the natural trigger per the build plan.
- **No `.github/workflows/build.yml`** yet. \`shipyard ship\` validates on the local mac target; a Namespace-hosted GHA workflow for PR status checks can be added later if useful.

## Ship flow after merge

    ./tools/install-shipyard.sh
    shipyard doctor
    shipyard run           # validate current branch
    shipyard ship          # PR + validate + merge on green

## Verification

\`shipyard doctor\` on this branch:

    ✓ git / ssh / shipyard-on-path / daemon-version
    ✓ gh / nsc
    ✗ RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN missing    # only required for the release pipeline, not PRs
    Overall: ready

## Follow-ups

- Revisit \`validation.gates\` if Spectr grows a CLI or skill set worth enforcing.
- Add Ubuntu + Windows targets + a GHA status-check workflow at M10 (format validation).
- If a pattern emerges where \"macOS on Namespace via \`shipyard ship\`\" would beat \"macOS local + \`shipyard cloud run\` separately,\" file it as a Shipyard FR (new \`backend = \"namespace\"\` option on a target).

author: ragavrida
body:
## Summary

Eight commits, seven bugs. Each commit is a single logical change so the series bisects cleanly per `CLAUDE.md`'s commit rules. The bugs were surfaced by an external audit of `v1.6.3.0` master and re-verified against `v1.6.4.0` (`d75402b`) before filing — all seven targets still reproduce.

No touches to `ETHOS.md`, voice/tone in skill templates, YC/founder material, or any generated `SKILL.md`. No `browse/dist/` or `design/dist/` binaries staged. No new features, no refactors, no dependency churn.

### The bugs

| # | Sev | File | Bug | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **CRITICAL** | `browse/src/cli.ts` | `browse disconnect` hits `ReferenceError: domains is not defined` before the graceful shutdown POST goes out. `domains` is declared only in `handlePairAgent` (line 613), but the `disconnect` branch at line 961 references it from `main()` scope. | `a3c2fe6` |
| 2 | HIGH | `scripts/build-app.sh` | The Chromium rebrand interpolates `$APP_NAME` straight into sed's `s///` replacement half. A name containing `/`, `&`, or `\` either breaks the command or gets interpreted as sed syntax, and the trailing `\|\| true` hides it. | `3ce22d3` |
| 3 | HIGH | `scripts/build-app.sh` | `DMG_TMP=$(mktemp -d)` is unchecked. On failure `$DMG_TMP` is empty and the next line is `cp -a "$APP_DIR" "$DMG_TMP/"` — which copies the `.app` bundle into the filesystem root. | `0172bea` |
| 4 | HIGH | `bin/gstack-telemetry-sync` | `mktemp` failure falls back to `/tmp/gstack-sync-$$`. `$$` is the PID — predictable, races on shared hosts. Attacker can pre-create or symlink the path and either read the response body or redirect curl's `-o`. | `40d9865` |
| 5 | HIGH | `supabase/verify-rls.sh` | Same shape: `/tmp/verify-rls-$$-$TOTAL` fallback on mktemp failure. Worse blast radius because the response bodies contain whatever RLS leak the test discovered. | `7e278f2` |
| 6 | HIGH | `browse/src/security-classifier.ts` | `downloadFile()` opens a `fs.WriteStream` to `<dest>.tmp.<pid>` but never closes it on error paths. Reader/writer throw mid-download → FD leak + half-written tmp that a retry's `renameSync` can promote to the real path, loading a truncated ONNX model. | `3aa97ad` |
| 7 | HIGH | `browse/src/meta-commands.ts` | `parsePdfFromFile()` runs `JSON.parse` on user-supplied file contents with no try/catch. A malformed payload crashes the `pdf` handler with an uncaught `SyntaxError` instead of a readable "this file isn't valid JSON". | `758bc2c` |
| 8 | HIGH | `bin/gstack-global-discover.ts` | `extractCwdFromJsonl()` reads first 8KB + parses every line. When a session header straddles the 8KB cap, `JSON.parse` fails on the truncated tail, the catch `continue`s silently, and the project disappears from the discovery output. | `4c51176` |

### Fix shape

Every fix is the smallest change that closes the bug:

- **#1** — delete the stray `domains` field from the disconnect body. One-line diff.
- **#2** — escape `&`, `/`, `\` in `$APP_NAME` before interpolating into the sed replacement.
- **#3** — fail loudly if `mktemp -d` produced an empty string or a non-directory; don't continue into `cp`.
- **#4 / #5** — drop the predictable `$$` fallback entirely. On mktemp failure, skip this run (telemetry) or `return 1` from the check (verify-rls). Telemetry also gets a `trap ... EXIT` so the tmp is cleaned up on unexpected exit.
- **#6** — wrap the read loop in `try/catch`; on failure destroy the writer and unlink the tmp before rethrowing.
- **#7** — wrap `JSON.parse`, surface the parser's own message with the offending path, and reject non-object top-level JSON.
- **#8** — raise the cap from 8KB to 64KB and drop the final (possibly truncated) segment before parsing.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test` — skill validation + browse integration tests (no new tests added; these are narrow bug fixes and I didn't want to expand the PR surface).
- [ ] Manual: `browse connect` then `browse disconnect` — should shut down gracefully (regression of #1).
- [ ] Manual: `APP_NAME='Foo/Bar&Baz' ./scripts/build-app.sh` — rebrand should succeed with the literal name (regression of #2).
- [ ] Manual: temporarily make `/tmp` read-only for your user, run `./scripts/build-app.sh` — should error out cleanly instead of cp-ing into `/` (regression of #3).
- [ ] Manual: feed `parsePdfFromFile` a file that's not valid JSON — should get a helpful error message (regression of #7).
- [ ] `bun run test:evals` on the gate tier — untouched code paths; would just verify no fallout.

Happy to split further, squash, or rewrite any of the commit messages if that helps. Also happy to add regression tests if you'd like — I kept the PR scope tight to stay under your community-PR guardrails (no voice/ETHOS.md/promo changes).

- Added a new local state `lockedStopInfoStopId` and updated `handleStopOpenRequest(...)` in `IslandRunBoardPrototype` to open a dedicated locked-landmark info prompt when a stop resolver returns `locked` instead of silently posting landing text.

- Enriched the existing ticket-payment prompt to display the stop `description` so the tap flow for `ticket_required` stops now shows both context and the pay/enter pathway in one modal.

author: mloek
body:
## Idee
Besucher können die 27-Fragen-Anamnese direkt auf der Website durchführen – ohne App, ohne Konto. Danach werden sie motiviert, die App zu installieren.

## Flow
1. **CTA-Button** „Anamnese starten →" im neuen Abschnitt (zwischen Therapeuten und App-Install-CTA)
2. **Nudge-Modal**: emotionaler Text → erklärt, warum die App mehr kann → zwei Optionen
   - „App holen – kostenlos & anonym" → Install-Flow
   - „Trotzdem hier durchführen (ohne Speichern)"
3. **Fragebogen**: alle 27 Fragen, Frage für Frage, Fortschrittsbalken, identische Antwortoptionen wie in der App (PHQ-9, GAD-7, WHO-5, ASRS)
4. **Ergebnis-Screen**: auffällig / grenzwertig / unauffällig pro Instrument + großer App-Nudge „Ergebnisse in App speichern & behalten"

## Conversion-Logik
- Kein Speichern im Browser (bewusst) → motiviert zur App
- App-Nudge erscheint zweimal: vor dem Start und nach dem Ergebnis
- Krisenhinweis am Ende: Telefonseelsorge 0800 111 0 111
