author: turdjali
body:
### Motivation
- Improve portrait (phone) presentation so parked weapons sit higher, more outward, and shifted toward the top/edges of the screen for better readability and visual balance.
- Make reserve player tokens for top and bottom seats appear closer to the top player on portrait screens for clearer turn context.
- Reduce dice visual crowding and ensure the camera better follows token motion (especially when tokens move along the top-side lanes) while allowing a small manual lift gesture for the user.

### Description
- Reduced on-screen dice by adjusting `DICE_SIZE` (from a 1.3 multiplier to 1.16) so dice render slightly smaller while existing roll/handoff logic is preserved.
- Moved weapon parking outward and upward by increasing `WEAPON_PARKING_OUTWARD_OFFSET`, per-seat outward offsets, and raising portrait screen shift Y values in `WEAPON_PORTRAIT_SCREEN_SHIFT_BY_SEAT`, and adjusted parked weapon Y offsets in `WEAPON_PARKED_Y_DROP_BY_KIND` for improved visual height.
- Pushed reserve tokens for bottom/top seats further upward by increasing radial offsets in `TOKEN_PORTRAIT_SCREEN_SHIFT_BY_SEAT` so top/bottom reserve tokens sit closer to the top player area.
- Tuned camera distances and portrait camera tuning by lowering `PORTRAIT_INITIAL_CAMERA_DISTANCE_FACTOR` and reducing `backOffset`/`heightOffset` in `PORTRAIT_CAMERA_TUNING`, and expanded top-down framing by increasing `CAMERA_TOPDOWN_RADIUS_FACTOR` and `CAMERA_TOPDOWN_MAX_RADIUS_FACTOR` and centering the 2D top-down target on the table surface.
- Improved token-follow framing in `computeTokenFollowCameraState` by raising the camera target Y and, for tokens moving on top-side lanes, lifting the camera position and nudging it slightly forward so tokens are more visible.
- Added small drag-based lift behavior in the camera `onPointerMove` handler for 3D mode which lets the user lift the fixed camera a bit (with forward nudge) by dragging downwards, constrained to reasonable limits.
- All code edits are contained in `webapp/src/components/SnakeBoard3D.jsx` and keep existing camera-animation durations and dice-handling flows unchanged.

### Testing
- Ran `npx eslint webapp/src/components/SnakeBoard3D.jsx` which reported the file was matched by ignore patterns, and no lint errors were emitted for the edited code path.
- Verified local file diff contains only updates to `webapp/src/components/SnakeBoard3D.jsx` and no unrelated files were modified.
- No automated render snapshot or UI integration tests were run in this environment, and a screenshot/visual validation could not be captured here.

author: mortenoh
body:
## Summary

`uv lock --upgrade` picked 16 packages forward within the existing pyproject.toml `>=` bounds. No majors, no constraint changes. Main driver: silence the `pyright 1.1.409` CI warning that's been nagging every workflow run.

### Package bumps

| package | from | to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pyright | 1.1.408 | 1.1.409 |
| pydantic | 2.13.2 | 2.13.3 |
| pydantic-core | 2.46.2 | 2.46.3 |
| pydantic-settings | 2.13.1 | 2.14.0 |
| mypy | 1.20.1 | 1.20.2 |
| fastapi | 0.136.0 | 0.136.1 |
| typer | 0.24.1 | 0.24.2 |
| uvicorn | 0.44.0 | 0.46.0 |
| authlib | 1.6.11 | 1.7.0 (+ new `joserfc` transitive) |
| idna | 3.11 | 3.13 |
| certifi | 2026.2.25 | 2026.4.22 |
| cachetools | 7.0.5 | 7.0.6 |
| click | 8.3.2 | 8.3.3 |
| cyclopts | 4.10.2 | 4.11.0 |
| pathspec | 1.0.4 | 1.1.0 |

### What's still behind upstream

- `certifi 2026.4.22` and `wheel 0.47.0` sit above what the lock picks, but they're transitive pins from other deps that haven't bumped yet. Next round of the upstream chain will clear them.

### Why this PR is a lock-only change

Every package was already declared as `>=`; no pyproject.toml edit is needed to receive these versions. A PR that only bumps pyproject lower bounds would force the same upgrade without giving us anything new, so the `>=` floors stay where they are.

## Test plan

- [x] `make lint` — pyright 1.1.409 reports clean on 2141 files, no more "new version available" warning
- [x] `make test` — 673 passed / 0 failed
- [x] `verify_examples.py` against the live Sierra Leone stack — 119 pass / 0 fail / 11 skip

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Refactor the frontend to build with Vite and move away from the single 2149-line `src/main.js`, 959-line `src/index.html` and `window.*` globals. No feature changes — behaviour is preserved.

What changed:

- **Vite**: added `vite.config.js` (root `src/`, output `dist/`, dev port `1420`) and `npm` scripts `dev` / `build` / `preview`. `npm run build` produces a static `dist/` that Tauri now reads.
- **tauri.conf.json**: `frontendDist` → `../dist`, added `devUrl` + `beforeDevCommand` (`npm run dev`) + `beforeBuildCommand` (`npm run build`), so `tauri dev` and `tauri build` run Vite transparently (including in CI).
- **`src/main.js`**: replaced with a thin entry that imports modules and orchestrates init. The old monolith is gone.
- **`src/lib/`**: Tauri IPC wrappers (`core.js`), i18n engine with change-listeners (`i18n.js`), DOM helpers (`dom.js`), shared app state (`state.js`), and restart banner/modal logic (`restart.js`).
- **`src/features/`**: one file per UI domain — `strategies`, `status`, `filters`, `connect`, `navigation`, `user-lists`, `info-modals`, `titlebar`, `admin-check`, `binaries`, `versions`, `status-check`, `updates`, `diagnostics`, `wizard`, `firstrun`.
- **`src/i18n/{en,ru}.js`**: converted from `window.i18n_*` globals to `export default` and imported by `lib/i18n.js`.
- **`src/index.html`**: now just the app shell (titlebar, sidebar, header, `<main id="sections-host">`, `<div id="modals-host">`). Section and modal markup extracted into `src/components/{sections,modals}/*.html` and mounted synchronously via `?raw` imports in `src/components/index.js` — no runtime fetches, fragments are inlined at build time.
- Tailwind is still loaded from its CDN (PostCSS migration out of scope).

Build/CI:

- `npm run build` → clean output (~104 kB JS / ~25 kB gz, 43 modules).
- `npm run check-versions` → passes.
- Tauri CI (`tauri build --no-bundle`) will now invoke Vite automatically through `beforeBuildCommand`.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] `tauri dev` brings up the app (the dev server on `127.0.0.1:1420` is now Vite, not a static file server).
- [ ] Start/stop service, game/ipset toggles, strategy dropdown with search + favourites, and cached test badges all work — these were the most state-heavy parts of the original `main.js`.
- [ ] Navigation between Home / Sites / IPs / Diagnostics, including the "Restart required" guard and the bottom banner.
- [ ] Titlebar: minimize/maximize icon swap, close behaviour (ask / tray / exit) from the settings popover, autostart toggle.
- [ ] Wizard: preflight blockers, live progress events, best-result apply as service/temporary.
- [ ] Updates flow: "Check Updates" dual modal (UI + core), and the legacy "Update now" path that stops/starts the service around a core update.
- [ ] Diagnostics: run, show-all toggle, copy report, Discord cache clear.
- [ ] First-run and binaries-missing download flows (fresh install / empty `bin/`).
- [ ] Language toggle refreshes hero/header status, strategy dropdown labels, and the open info modal.
- [ ] `tauri build` produces the expected installer and the bundled app runs.

### Notes

- HTML fragments are imported with Vite `?raw` and inlined into the bundle, so there are no extra network requests at startup and fragments ship with the installer as they did before.
- `@tauri-apps/api` is intentionally *not* imported — `withGlobalTauri: true` stays, and `lib/core.js` wraps `window.__TAURI__` so the bundle stays small and runtime behaviour identical.
- Tailwind CDN kept for now; a PostCSS/`@tailwindcss/cli` migration can be a separate PR.
- `admin-check-modal` isn't present in `index.html` (wasn't in the pre-refactor HTML either); `ensureAdminPrivileges` uses optional chaining so the absence is a no-op, matching prior behaviour.
- Framework migration (SolidJS/React/Svelte) is deliberately **not** in this PR — this refactor is the setup that makes that next step much smaller and safer.

author: st1tcher86
body:
## Summary

Самый крупный PR эпика (14h). Фоновый обработчик массовых операций: дренит Redis pending-queue, применяет изменения с AsyncLocalStorage-контекстом (audit автоматически помечается `bulkOperationId`), восстанавливается после рестарта, чистит старые данные.

### Scope (11 файлов, 1300+ строк)

- **`shared/bulk-operation-context.ts`** — AsyncLocalStorage для `bulkOperationId`. Audit-записи в `executeTransition` автоматически подтягивают id без изменения сигнатур (§5.4). Вне bulk — null.
- **`executors/transition.executor.ts`** — первый реальный `BulkExecutor<TransitionPayload>`. 7 preflight-состояний: NO_ACCESS, NO_TRANSITION, ALREADY_IN_TARGET_STATE, WORKFLOW_REQUIRED_FIELDS (CONFLICT), ELIGIBLE + preview diff.
- **`executors/index.ts`** — registry с `getExecutor(type)`. PR-4 только TRANSITION; PR-5 добавит ещё 6.
- **`bulk-operations.processor.ts`** — 3 cron-задачи:
  - **tick** (lock 'bulk-ops:tick' TTL 90s, batch 25): LPOP + per-item preflight/execute, heartbeat, finalize SUCCEEDED/PARTIAL/FAILED/CANCELLED.
  - **recovery** (~1 мин): stale RUNNING (heartbeat < now-300s) → QUEUED.
  - **retention** (nightly): items > 30d + ops > 90d терминальных.
- **`shared/redis.ts`** — `lpopListBatch` (node-redis v5 `lPopCount`).
- **`server.ts`** — start/stopBulkOperationsScheduler в жизненном цикле + drain SIGTERM.
- **`workflow-engine.service.ts`** — +1 строка: `bulkOperationId: getCurrentBulkOperationId() ?? null` в audit-create (обратно совместимо, null вне bulk).

## Pre-push review (Opus 4.7) — 2 🟠 + 4 🟡 + 1 🔵 + 2 ⚪

Все применены в follow-up коммите (`b16c47d`):

**🟠 Критичные race/correctness bugs:**
1. **TICK_LOCK_TTL 30→90s** — при BATCH_SIZE=25 × `executeTransition` ~1s worst-case 25s ≈ TTL. Lock expiry мид-batch → второй инстанс подхватывал тот же op → double-processing. 90s = 3× headroom + env-override.
2. **actor.systemRoles=[]→ getEffectiveUserSystemRoles(createdById)**. Пустой слайс молча ломал SUPER_ADMIN bulk: NO_ACCESS на каждом item → finalize SUCCEEDED all-skipped. Processor теперь делает 1 pre-batch fetch эффективных ролей (PR-2).

**🟡 UX/correctness:**
3. **finalize: all-skipped (succeeded=0 && failed=0) → PARTIAL, не SUCCEEDED** — не обманываем зелёной галкой если ничего не изменилось.
4. **finalizeCancelled drain heartbeat каждые 10s** — закрывает double-finalize race (drain до 20k items может занять > RECOVERY_STALE_SECONDS без heartbeat'а, recovery бы ресетил RUNNING в QUEUED посреди дренажа).
5. **INVALID_TRANSITION → SKIPPED STALE_STATUS, не FAILED** — race между preflight (T1) и execute (T2): другой юзер изменил статус. Не execution failure, не раздуваем failed-счётчик.
6. **Comment linking RECOVERY_STALE_SECONDS + TICK_LOCK_TTL_S** — инвариант «recovery >> lock-ttl × batches-in-flight» задокументирован.

**🔵 Hygiene:**
7. **Test assert heartbeatAt в $transaction update** — регрессия, дроппающая heartbeat, проходила бы молча.

**⚪ Added:**
- Test all-skipped → PARTIAL.
- Test INVALID_TRANSITION → SKIPPED STALE_STATUS.

**⚪ Skipped:**
- SCAN cursor bug в `delCacheByPrefix` — pre-existing, не мой код.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors
- [x] `npm run lint` → 0 errors, 0 new warnings
- [x] `npm run test:parser` → 548/548 passed (+21 новых в PR-4)
- [ ] CI: backend integration — full Postgres+Redis flow
- [ ] Staging smoke: preview → submit 5 TRANSITIONs → все applied + audit_logs.bulk_operation_id = op.id
- [ ] Staging smoke: kill instance mid-batch → recovery через 5 мин переводит в QUEUED → новый tick завершает
- [ ] Staging smoke: cancel во время RUNNING → `cancel_requested=true` → processor финализирует CANCELLED + дренит queue

## Зависимости

- **Base:** `main` (branch от `ttbulk-1/service-core` = PR-3 #145). После merge #145 сделаю rebase (drop PR-3 commits через `--skip`).
- **Downstream:** PR-5 (6 остальных executor'ов) подключает их в registry + расширяет preflight-матрицы.

## Плановая дельта

§13.9 строка 4 → 🟢 Merged после actual merge (сейчас ✅ Done).

См. [docs/tz/TTBULK-1.md §5.4, §6.3, §6.4, §13.5 PR-4](docs/tz/TTBULK-1.md#135-pr-%D1%8B-%D1%84%D0%B0%D0%B7%D1%8B-2--processor--executors-28%D1%87).

body:
Add opt-in PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) support to the Kiali operator, mirroring the existing HorizontalPodAutoscaler pattern. Users can configure a PDB via the new `deployment.pod_disruption_budget` CR field, which accepts an `api_version` (defaults to "policy/v1" when left empty) and a `spec` passthrough. When `spec` is empty no PDB is created; when populated the operator creates, updates, and removes the PDB resource as part of the normal deploy and remove lifecycle.

Fixes: https://github.com/kiali/kiali/issues/9590

author: yito88
body:
## Summary
- New public types `RunConfig`, `RunSuite`, `NamedRunSummary` in `src/sweep.rs`. TOML `[[runs]]` loader pulls each entry's optional `name` aside and treats remaining flat keys as its `Params` (via a new `Params::from_flat_map`).
- Strict suite parsing: missing/non-array/empty `runs`, nested tables inside a run, and non-string `name` all error clearly at load time.
- `Scenario::run_suite(self, suite) -> Result<Vec<NamedRunSummary>>` executes every run sequentially in the order written in the TOML. Internal refactor: factored `execute_once(&self, params)` so `run_with_params` and `run_suite` share one execution path without needing `Clone` on the closure-carrying `Step` / `Hook` types.
- **Continue-on-failure for step errors**: a run whose step body returns `Err` is recorded with `success=false` / `error_count > 0` and the suite moves on. **Framework errors halt the suite** (hook failure, policy violation) and surface as `Err`, per the spec's "TOML/config/setup errors => return Err".

body:
Obiettivo
Questa Pull Request unisce una serie di major update che trasformano NullifyPDF da uno script funzionale a un'applicazione forense di livello professionale. Introduce un'interfaccia utente completamente riprogettata, un motore di sanificazione dei PDF più profondo e un sistema di build automatizzato compatibile al 100% con Windows, macOS e Linux.

✨ Nuove Funzionalità (UI & UX)
Architettura Widescreen: Implementata una nuova Sidebar laterale per massimizzare lo spazio verticale dedicato all'anteprima del documento.

Navigazione Avanzata: Aggiunto il "Jump to Page" (salto rapido tramite input numerico) e controlli di Zoom fluido (bottoni UI e shortcut CTRL + Rotellina Mouse).

Gestione Finestre: Le finestre di popup (Dizionari e About) ora calcolano dinamicamente le coordinate X/Y per centrarsi sempre perfettamente rispetto alla finestra madre.

🛡️ Sicurezza e Motore Forense
Blindfold Mode (Opzione 2): Aggiunto lo switch Oscura Immagini. Il tool ora rileva tutte le immagini/grafiche nel PDF, ne distrugge i byte e le sostituisce visivamente con un segnaposto professionale grigio ([ IMMAGINE RIMOSSA ]).

Deep Scrubbing: L'esportazione ora appiattisce e distrugge fisicamente i moduli interattivi (AcroForms), i metadati e i cataloghi interattivi.

Sistema Anti-Stacking: L'intelligenza artificiale ora mappa le coordinate vettoriali prima di agire, evitando di sovrapporre censure su aree già coperte dall'utente o dalla Blocklist.

Risoluzione "Whitelist Fantasma": Il click manuale per la rimozione di una censura ora esegue una pulizia "profonda" (forando tutti i livelli vettoriali sovrapposti) prima di spostare la parola in Allowlist.

⚙️ Motore e Prestazioni
Fix Memory Leak & File Lock: Il cambio di documento in esecuzione ora forza il close() del file precedente, sbloccandolo dal file system e liberando la RAM.

Ottimizzazione AI (70% più veloce): Le espressioni regolari (Regex) usate per il match della Allowlist sono state estratte e pre-compilate fuori dai cicli iterativi annidati, abbattendo drasticamente l'uso della CPU durante il processo Auto Redact.

Protezione Crash: Inseriti controlli per bloccare PDF protetti da password senza far crashare la GUI e fixato il bug di cancellazione della funzione "Clear Page".

📦 Build System (PyInstaller & DevOps)
Supporto Windows Nativo: Sostituito il comando CLI con un file .spec dinamico che inietta sys.setrecursionlimit(5000), aggirando definitivamente il crash in fase di build causato dalle librerie Cython di SpaCy.

Supporto macOS Nativo: Lo script ora genera veri e propri .app bundle per i sistemi Apple (Darwin).

Gestione Icone Intelligente: Introdotta la conversione automatica on-the-fly dell'icona .png in .ico (per Windows) o .icns (per macOS) tramite Pillow.

📚 Documentazione
Aggiornato il file README.md aggiungendo una sezione critica sui Limiti dello Strumento per informare gli utenti forensi (mancanza di OCR, gestione firme crittografiche invalidabili).

Aggiornato e formattato il CHANGELOG.md.

author: lishunyang12
body:
## Summary

Adds two attention backends to vllm-omni's diffusion path and makes Blackwell (sm_10x / sm_12x) first-class:

- **`CUDNN_ATTN`** — pins `sdpa_kernel([CUDNN_ATTENTION])` to dispatch to cuDNN 9.5+ tuned Blackwell FMHA. Zero new deps. Mask-path safe via `_maybe_reshape_attn_mask` helper.
- **`FLASHINFER_ATTN`** — dense-prefill wrapper around `flashinfer.prefill.single_prefill_with_kv_cache` with `custom_mask` for non-causal masked attention. Falls back to default SDPA only when mask shape doesn't broadcast to `(qo_len, kv_len)`.

Blackwell previously fell through to `TORCH_SDPA` because the FA gate excluded `capability >= 100`. This PR:
- Auto-routes Blackwell (sm_100 / sm_103 / sm_120 / sm_121) to `CUDNN_ATTN` when cuDNN ≥ 9.5 is available
- Falls back to `FLASHINFER_ATTN` on Blackwell when cuDNN < 9.5 but flashinfer is installed
- Relaxes the FA compute-capability gate so source-built FA Blackwell CUTE kernels work via `DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASH_ATTN`
- Documents the new selection logic in `docs/user_guide/diffusion/attention_backends.md`

## End-to-End Benchmark (BF16, sm_120 RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell)

Same prompt and seed across runs. Numbers from `Total generation time` line of the e2e drivers.

| Model | Shape | TORCH_SDPA | CUDNN_ATTN | FLASHINFER_ATTN | Best/Worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HunyuanVideo-1.5 (T2V) | 480p / 33f / 50 steps | 147.05 s | **73.02 s** | 127.84 s | **2.01×** |
| Wan 2.2 14B (T2V) | 480p / 33f / 40 steps | 117.75 s | 117.17 s | **115.07 s** | 1.02× |
| Qwen-Image (T2I) | 1024² / 50 steps | 17.41 s | **15.14 s** | 16.02 s | 1.15× |
| FLUX.2-dev (T2I) | 1024² / 50 steps, TP=2 | 53.62 s | **53.30 s** | 54.94 s | 1.03× |
| Z-Image-Turbo (T2I) | 1024² / 8 steps, CFG=1.0 | ~3.4 s | ~3.4 s | ~3.4 s | ≈1.0× |
| LTX-2.0 (T2V+A) | 480p / 97f / 500 steps, CFG=2 | 324 s | **crashes (#3121) fixed by commit f905756426b3100c93e0fa47dc80a6b260c89191** | 305.21 s | n/a |

Pattern: **mask-heavy DiTs favor `CUDNN_ATTN`** (HV-1.5: 2×, Qwen-Image: 1.15×) because cuDNN's pinned FMHA sidesteps a PyTorch SDPA dispatch quirk where the unpinned dispatcher picks `EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` (~25 ms) for masked calls instead of cuDNN (~11 ms). Models with lighter masks (Wan 2.2), TP-saturated configs (FLUX.2 TP=2), or short total runtime (Z-Image-Turbo at 8 steps) tie within noise.

`CUDNN_ATTN` is the safe Blackwell default: never slow, sometimes 2× faster.

## Kernel-Level Microbench (HV-1.5 shape, BF16, sm_120)

`benchmarks/diffusion/bench_attention_backends.py --preset hv15`

| Backend | No-mask | With mask | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FLASHINFER (default)** | **6.79 ms** | (custom_mask) | wins kernel-only, no-mask |
| FLASHINFER (fa2) | 6.80 ms | | tied — same kernel |
| CUDNN_ATTENTION (pinned) | 7.08 ms | **11.17 ms** | wins kernel-only, with-mask |
| FLASH_ATTENTION (FA2 via SDPA) | 7.80 ms | FAILED | FA2 rejects 2D attn_mask |
| EFFICIENT_ATTENTION | 19.11 ms | 25.10 ms | slow fallback |
| MATH | 183 ms | 215 ms | slowest fallback |
| FA4 (direct) | broken (sm_120 beta) | mask-not-supported | revisit when stable |
| FLASHINFER (cutlass / fa3 / trtllm-gen) | unsupported on sm_120 | | NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#11799 |

The kernel-level winner (FLASHINFER) ≠ the e2e winner (CUDNN_ATTN) on mask-heavy models because FlashInfer's `_sdpa_fallback` originally dispatched to the slow EFFICIENT path for shape-mismatched masks. Fixed by [@frauttauteffasu's review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/3079#issuecomment-...) — FlashInfer now uses `custom_mask` with `broadcast_to`, closing 13% of the HV-1.5 gap.

## Relation to upstream vLLM

Upstream vLLM exposes FlashInfer and cuDNN for **LLM serving**, not diffusion. The design differs by workload:

| | Upstream vLLM (LLM) | This PR (vllm-omni diffusion) |
|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer | First-class `backends/flashinfer.py` using `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` + explicit `plan()` step for paged KV, ragged batches, cascade, FP8 KV | Dense `single_prefill_with_kv_cache` with `custom_mask`, static shapes, no plan step |
| cuDNN | No dedicated backend; reachable only via `TORCH_SDPA` dispatch | First-class `CUDNN_ATTN` with explicit `sdpa_kernel([CUDNN_ATTENTION])` pin |
| Code size | ~800+ lines per backend | ~80 lines per backend |

Why the delta: LLM serving has ragged batches, paged KV, and prefill/decode mixing, all of which require upstream's `plan()` + metadata-builder pattern. Diffusion has static shapes per resolution, so each backend reduces to a direct kernel call.

## Known Limitations

### LTX-2.0 + `CUDNN_ATTN` crashes under torch.compile, fixed by commit f905756426b3100c93e0fa47dc80a6b260c89191

LTX-2's audio attention has a symbolic head_dim under torch.compile tracing. cuDNN's SDPA selector rejects symbolic dims at trace time and Dynamo aborts compilation. Tried two workarounds (runtime try/except — unreachable; `is_compiling()` guard — regressed HV-1.5's 2× win); both reverted.

**Workaround**: `DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_BACKEND=FLASHINFER_ATTN` or `TORCH_SDPA` for LTX-2.0. Tracked in #3121.

### FA4 not yet integrated

FlashAttention-4 (Tri Dao, March 2026) targets Blackwell natively and reportedly beats cuDNN by ~20% on B200. The current `flash-attn-4 4.0.0b10` wheel crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '_trait'` during JIT on sm_120. Not yet wired into vllm-omni; revisit when stable lands.

## What's Tested

- ✅ Five diffusion models across video / image / image-with-LLM-thinker on sm_120 RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell
- ✅ Backend microbench (`bench_attention_backends.py`) — no-mask + with-mask for SDPA / FlashInfer / FA4 paths
- ✅ E2E drivers landed for HV-1.5, Wan 2.2, FLUX.2, Z-Image, LTX-2 (`benchmarks/diffusion/bench_e2e_*.sh`)
- ✅ Mask-shape `broadcast_to` validated against HV-1.5 (B,1,1,S_k) and LTX-2 (S,S) shapes
- ✅ User-facing doc updated (`docs/user_guide/diffusion/attention_backends.md`) with auto-route logic, benchmark table, and known limitations
- ✅ Existing `TORCH_SDPA`, `FLASH_ATTN`, `SAGE_ATTN` paths unchanged

## What's Out of Scope

- Hopper / Ada / Ampere auto-route stays at `FLASH_ATTN` (FA3). Pre-Blackwell GPUs don't get the new auto-route.
- CUDA graph capture — explored under `DIFFUSION_COMPILE_MODE=reduce-overhead`, regressed 8% on diffusion (scheduler reallocates latent each step, breaks graph reuse). Reverted; scheduler-side plumbing is a separate effort.
- FP8 attention (Phase 3): a 1.5× lever, but cuDNN FP8 prefill on sm_120 has known xfails for CUDA ≤ 12.9. Out of scope here; tracked separately on the quant matrix.

## Roadmap

- **Phase 1 (this PR, done)** — BF16 backend plumbing, Blackwell default via `CUDNN_ATTN`, mask-path correctness fix per @frauttauteffasu review, full e2e benchmark coverage, user-facing doc
- **Phase 2 (separate PR)** — Resolve #3121 (LTX-2 symbolic head_dim under torch.compile)
- **Phase 3** — `CUDNN_FP8_ATTN` / `FLASHINFER_FP8_ATTN`; expected ~1.5-1.8× op, ~1.1-1.3× e2e
- **Phase 4** — `CUDNN_NVFP4_ATTN` / `FLASHINFER_NVFP4_ATTN` for Blackwell sm_100+; expected ~2-3× op, ~1.3-1.5× e2e
- **Phase 5** — FA4 integration when `flash-attn-4` stable lands and the sm_120 JIT bug resolves
- **Phase 6** — Fused QKV-RoPE-Attn-O for hot-path DiTs, only if Phases 3-5 benchmarks show a remaining gap

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure bot-authored messages delivered on private surfaces (DMs, group DMs, private channels, or personal chats) are recorded into the existing conversation history as assistant messages without invoking agent processing.
- Keep ingestion/behavior consistent across similar private surfaces (DMs, group chats, private channels) and avoid duplicating agent runs for bot-generated content.

### Description
- Add `append_bot_message_to_existing_conversation` to `WorkspaceMessenger` to persist assistant `ChatMessage` entries and update `conversations` metadata when a bot-authored message targets an existing conversation, and import `ChatMessage` in `_workspace.py`.
- Change Slack event handling in `slack_events.py` to call the new append method for bot messages in direct/group/private channels instead of processing them with the agent, and mirror the same behavior for Teams in `teams_events.py` when the activity is from the bot in personal/group chats.
- Pass `is_private_channel` into Slack context formatting and update `_format_channel_history_context` in `slack.py` to include a short private-channel notice in the assembled context.

author: tmichett
body:
## Summary

**Fix #3b** adjusts how the Remix build runs in Podman on **SELinux-enforcing** Fedora hosts so `livecd-creator` can complete **strict** `setfiles` relabeling inside the chroot. This replaces the interim approach (`--security-opt label=disable` and warning-only `kickstart.py` relabel) with **labeled bind mounts** and **enforcing** in the live kickstart when the container path is healthy.

## What changed

- **`Build_Remix.sh`**: Dropped `--security-opt label=disable`. On **Linux** hosts, bind mounts use the **`:z`** suffix (`:ro,z` / `:rw,z`) for shared container labeling; on **non-Linux** hosts (e.g. macOS + Podman Machine) the suffix is omitted.
- **`Setup/files/Fixes/kickstart.py`**: Restores **strict** relabel: when the kickstart requests **enforcing** SELinux, a non-zero `setfiles` exit **raises** `KickstartError` again.
- **`Setup/Kickstarts/fedora-live-base.ks`** and **`Setup/Kickstarts/Extra/FlatRemix.ks`**: Restored **`selinux --enforcing`** for the product in the image.
- **Docs**: **`LINUX_BUILD_FIX.md`**, **`Quickstart_Container.md`**, **`SELINUX_RELABEL_FIX.md`**, and a log line in **`Setup/Enhanced_Remix_Build_Script.sh`** updated to document Fix #3b and point to `LINUX_BUILD_FIX.md` for AVC troubleshooting.

## Notes

- **`Enhanced_Remix_Build_Script.sh`** still may use **`setenforce 0`** inside the container for the build runtime; that is separate from **`selinux --enforcing`** in the **kickstart** (the tree that becomes the live ISO).
- If the build still fails with **AVC** on the host, inspect `ausearch -m avc -ts recent` and see **`LINUX_BUILD_FIX.md`**.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build the remix on a **Fedora Linux** host with SELinux **enforcing**; confirm the container starts without `label=disable` and the ISO build completes with relabel **not** downgraded to warnings only.
- [ ] (Optional) Confirm **Podman** on a **non-Linux** path still works with **no** `:z` suffix (script logic for `uname -s`).

author: namastex888
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1357 (which removed `release.yml`'s npm publish). The drift observed on 2026-04-23 between GitHub Release `v4.260423.9` and npm `@latest=4.260423.10` proved that on **main context** `version.yml` was deriving its own new version and publishing it — while `release.yml` had already created a Release with a **different** version from main's package.json.

## The bug

When a PR merges dev→main, two things happen in parallel:
1. `release.yml` runs on main push → reads main's `package.json` (let's call it `X`) → creates GitHub Release `v${X}`
2. CI runs on main → CI success → `workflow_run` fires `version.yml` → `version.yml` derives a **fresh** version `Y` from today's tag count, bumps dev to `Y`, and publishes `Y` as `@latest`

Result: GitHub Release says `v${X}`, npm `@latest` points at `Y`. On 2026-04-23 that was `v4.260423.9` vs `4.260423.10`.

## The fix

`version.yml` now distinguishes bump vs no-bump per context:

| Trigger | Context | npm tag | Bump? | Publishes |
|---------|---------|---------|-------|-----------|
| workflow_run on dev | dev | `@next` | yes | derived new version |
| workflow_run on main | main | `@latest` | **no** | current `package.json` version |
| workflow_dispatch | dev | `@next` | yes | derived new version |

## Changes

- `context` step emits `should_bump=false` on main triggers
- `Configure git`, `Derive version`, `Sync version files`, `Format JSON`, and `Commit and tag` steps all gate on `should_bump == 'true'`
- `context.branch` now emits `main` (not `dev`) on main triggers, so checkout uses main's `package.json` — exactly the version `release.yml` just tagged
- New `Resolve publish version` step for logging
- `Publish to npm via OIDC` unchanged in shape — `npm publish` reads the (unbumped) `package.json` and uses `npm_tag`

## Invariant after merge

**`npm @latest` version == GitHub Release `isLatest` tag** — always.

## Does not address

The historical drift (`@latest=4.260423.10`, Release `v4.260423.9`, `.6/.7/.8/.9` git tags never published) — that's manual cleanup, tracking separately.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR to dev
- [ ] Manual dispatch `Version` once on dev to verify `@next` path still works
- [ ] Merge PR #1341 (dev→main) to validate main path: GH Release version == npm `@latest`

## Related
- #1357 (release.yml → no npm publish; merged)
- PR #1341 — dev→main rolling release

author: antimetal[bot]
body:
## Problem
`recommendation` pods in `antimetal/test` entered CrashLoopBackOff because the service process was repeatedly OOMKilled. While this happened in test, the gRPC recommendation dependency became intermittently unavailable during restarts.

## Root Cause
In `src/recommendation/recommendation_server.py`, the `recommendationCacheFailure` branch grows module-global `cached_ids` on each cache miss by appending the full product catalog and then appending 25% of itself again. With the flag enabled at runtime, this list grows without bound and eventually exceeds the container memory limit.

## What This Fix Does
- Introduces a configurable hard cap (`RECOMMENDATION_CACHE_MAX_IDS`, default `5000`) for the fault-injection cache.
- Keeps existing fault-path behavior (cache hit/miss simulation) but truncates `cached_ids` to the most recent bounded window after growth.
- Prevents unbounded memory growth from this code path, so accidental flag enablement no longer drives OOM crash loops.

## Files Changed
| File | Status | Change |
|------|--------|--------|
| /code/opentelemetry-demo/src/recommendation/recommendation_server.py | modified | Added max cache size guard and truncation in recommendationCacheFailure branch |

## Test Plan
1. Build/deploy recommendation service with this patch in test.
2. Enable `recommendationCacheFailure` and generate traffic to `ListRecommendations`.
3. Confirm pod memory usage plateaus instead of growing unbounded; verify no OOMKills/restart spikes.
4. Check logs still emit cache hit/miss paths and service remains responsive.
5. Rollback: revert this commit and redeploy previous image if behavior is unexpected.

## Summary - add a dedicated slash-autocomplete renderer regression suite with requirement-tagged coverage for R001–R007 - add a focused Electron Playwright spec for `/` trigger, navigation, Esc dismissal, and Tab/Enter acceptance - tighten command/skill discovery contracts in `command-registry` and `skill-scanner` tests - publish operator/UAT evidence for S04 in `apps/desktop/docs/uat/M001/s04-slash-autocomplete.md` plus screenshots - update `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md` with slash-autocomplete behavior and focused e2e gate docs ## Validation - `cd apps/desktop && pnpm run test -- src/renderer/components/chat/__tests__/slash-autocomplete.regression.test.tsx` - `cd apps/desktop && pnpm run test -- src/main/__tests__/command-registry.test.ts src/main/__tests__/skill-scanner.test.ts src/renderer/components/chat/__tests__/CommandSuggestionDropdown.test.tsx src/renderer/components/chat/__tests__/MessageInput.slash-acceptance.test.tsx` - `cd apps/desktop && pnpm run test:e2e -- e2e/tests/slash-autocomplete.e2e.ts` - `cd apps/desktop && pnpm run typecheck` - `cd apps/desktop && test -f docs/uat/m001/s04-slash-autocomplete.md && rg "R001" docs/uat/m001/s04-slash-autocomplete.md && rg "slash-autocomplete" AGENTS.md` Closes #344 ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Added comprehensive end-to-end and regression test suites for slash command autocomplete functionality, covering dropdown presentation, keyboard navigation, and user acceptance flows * Enhanced command registry validation tests to verify descriptions and name uniqueness * Updated test coverage for skill directory scanning operations

Greptile Summary

This PR adds verification and documentation coverage for the S04 slash-autocomplete slice: a new unit regression suite (`slash-autocomplete.regression.test.tsx`) tagging R001–R007, a focused Playwright e2e spec, tightened `command-registry` and `skill-scanner` test contracts, UAT evidence screenshots, and updated `AGENTS.md`. - **P1** — The Enter sub-case in the e2e `[R006]` test is missing `await expect(dropdown).toBeVisible()` before `keyboard.press('Enter')`, creating a race condition where Enter may fire before the dropdown renders and submit `/ka` instead of accepting the suggestion. The Tab sub-case in the same test already has the guard; the Enter scenario needs it too.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge after fixing the missing dropdown visibility guard in the e2e Enter sub-case. One P1 finding: the e2e R006 Enter path has no wait for the dropdown before pressing Enter, making that test assertion intermittently unreliable. Everything else is clean — unit tests, traceability docs, and AGENTS.md are solid. apps/desktop/e2e/tests/slash-autocomplete.e2e.ts (lines 75-76)

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/desktop/e2e/tests/slash-autocomplete.e2e.ts | New Playwright e2e spec covering R001–R007; the Enter sub-case in the R006 test is missing a dropdown visibility guard before pressing Enter, introducing a race condition that could cause non-deterministic failures. | | apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/chat/__tests__/slash-autocomplete.regression.test.tsx | New comprehensive unit regression suite for R001–R007 with good mock/cleanup hygiene; the R005 ArrowDown assertion implicitly assumes index-0 auto-selection without documenting that invariant. | | apps/desktop/src/main/__tests__/command-registry.test.ts | Added R002 tags, a description-presence assertion, and a new determinism/uniqueness test; straightforward improvements with no issues. | | apps/desktop/src/main/__tests__/skill-scanner.test.ts | Renamed two tests with R003/R004 tags for traceability; no logic changes, clean. | | apps/desktop/docs/uat/M001/s04-slash-autocomplete.md | New UAT evidence doc with a complete requirement traceability matrix for R001–R007, diagnostics coverage, and verification commands; no issues. | | apps/desktop/AGENTS.md | Added slash-autocomplete contract note and e2e gate entry to the table; accurate and helpful documentation. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD A[User types '/' in chat-input] --> B{Dropdown visible?} B -- Yes --> C[CommandSuggestionDropdown renders options] C --> D{Key pressed} D -- ArrowDown/ArrowUp --> E[Navigate selection index] E --> C D -- Tab / Enter with selection --> F[Insert command + space into input] F --> G[Dropdown dismissed\nSLASH_ACCEPTED emitted] D -- Enter with no selection/loading --> H[Form submitted as-is\nSLASH_ACCEPT_NO_SELECTION warned] D -- Escape --> I[Dropdown dismissed\nInput unchanged] subgraph Main process J[commands:get-all IPC] --> K[listBuiltinCommands\nreturns builtin entries] J --> L[refreshSkillCache\nreturns /skill:* entries] end C --> J ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: apps/desktop/e2e/tests/slash-autocomplete.e2e.ts Line: 75-76 Comment: **Missing dropdown visibility guard before Enter key in R006** After the Tab sub-case resets the input with `await input.fill('/ka')` (line 75), there is no `await expect(…dropdown…).toBeVisible()` before `await readyWindow.keyboard.press('Enter')` (line 76). React's state update is asynchronous, so the dropdown may not have appeared yet when Enter fires — causing the event to fall through as a plain form submission (sending `/ka`) rather than accepting the first suggestion. The Tab scenario on line 67 correctly waits for the dropdown first; the Enter scenario should do the same. ```suggestion await input.fill('/ka') await expect(readyWindow.getByTestId('command-suggestion-dropdown')).toBeVisible() await readyWindow.keyboard.press('Enter') ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: apps/desktop/src/renderer/components/chat/__tests__/slash-autocomplete.regression.test.tsx Line: 160-164 Comment: **ArrowDown selection assumption is implicit and fragile** After one `ArrowDown`, the test immediately asserts that `/kata plan` (the second option) is `aria-selected="true"`. This is only correct if `/kata` (index 0) is already pre-selected by default when the dropdown first opens. If the component initialises with no selection (`selectedIndex = -1`), then a single `ArrowDown` would land on `/kata`, making this assertion a false pass on the wrong item. A short comment or an explicit pre-condition check (e.g. asserting `/kata` is `aria-selected` before the first key press) would make the invariant clear and prevent silent drift. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. --- This is a comment left during a code review. Path: apps/desktop/e2e/tests/slash-autocomplete.e2e.ts Line: 34 Comment: **Thin timing margin over the debounce window** `waitForTimeout(2200)` provides only 200 ms of headroom above the 2-second debounce. On a loaded CI runner or a machine with slower I/O, the debounce may not have fully settled, meaning `seedWorkspaceSkill` writes arrive just before the timeout expires and the first scan after the gap still misses them. Consider bumping to 3 000 ms or, better, using `expect.poll` to wait until the workspace skill name is visible in the dropdown rather than a fixed sleep. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````
Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["docs(S04/T03): publish slash autocomplet..."](https://github.com/gannonh/kata/commit/7192eb10d12924189c8a2fdc964f26c44c5aabc8) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=29509716) > Greptile also left

author: jcbsfilho
body:
This pull request makes small but important improvements to the GitHub Actions workflows for prereleases and releases, focusing on safety and clarity.

Workflow improvements:

* In `.github/workflows/prereleases.yml`, the script that creates a local `main` branch now only force-updates the branch if `main` is not currently checked out, preventing potential worktree errors.
* In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, the changeset publish action now includes a custom commit message (`chore: version packages`) for versioning commits, improving commit history clarity.

author: minsky-ai[bot]
body:
## Summary

- Adds `getUserToken?: () => Promise<string>` to `GitHubContext` so the merge path has access to the user PAT when the bot token lacks merge rights
- Wraps `octokit.rest.pulls.merge(...)` in an inner try/catch; on 403 (and only 403 — 405/422 merge-conflict errors pass through unchanged), retries with the user PAT obtained from `gh.getUserToken()`
- Logs a clear `[merge] Bot token lacked merge permission; retrying with user PAT` warning on fallback; logs success or throws an augmented `MinskyError` with actionable fix instructions if both tokens fail or no fallback is available
- Wires `getUserToken: () => this.tokenProvider.getUserToken()` into `requireGitHubContext()` in `GitHubBackend`
- Adds 8 unit tests covering: success via fallback, no-fallback augmented error, 405/422 bypass, both-tokens-fail, tokenOverride-suppression, and type-contract checks

## Root cause

`requireGitHubContext` wired only `getToken → tokenProvider.getServiceToken()`. The `mergePullRequest` call used that bot token, which lacked `contents: write` on the repo, producing a GitHub 403. No fallback was attempted. Observed on PR #700 (mt#1009) on 2026-04-23.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun test src/domain/repository/github-pr-operations-merge-fallback.test.ts` — all 8 pass
- [ ] `bun test src/domain/repository/` — no regressions
- [ ] TypeScript compiles (pre-commit hook)

Note: had Claude implement this fix based on the pre-dispatch scouting analysis in mt#1127.

author: rachelarteaga
body:
feat(planners): My Planners catalog + first-run new-planner flow## Summary

Ships a `/account/planners` catalog for managing every planner a user owns, a refactored binary per-planner share model, and a first-run UX that drops zero-planner users straight into the new-planner flow.

## Data model

- **Migration 027** — partial unique `(user_id, planner_id)` on `shared_schedules` where `scope='planner'`. Dedupes legacy rows before creating the index.
- **Migration 028** — drops `planners.is_default` + unique-default index; rewrites `handle_new_profile_planner` trigger to seed a starter planner without the flag.

## Catalog UI (`/account/planners`)

- Row per planner: inline rename, dates, kid count, last-edited rollup.
- Split share treatment — off = red-outlined "Share planner" CTA; on = green-outlined pulsing "Sharing on" read-only badge + separate **Copy link / Edit settings / Stop sharing** buttons. Avoids the "clicking the state toggles it" footgun.
- "+ New planner" modal defaults to next Monday + 8 weeks. New planners start empty (no kids).
- Duplicate + Delete row actions with confirm dialogs. Delete cascades via FKs and refuses to remove the last planner.

## Planner routing & smart redirect

- `/planner` accepts `?id=<uuid>`.
- Zero planners → `/account/planners?new=1` (auto-opens the New planner modal).
- One planner → opens it automatically.
- Two or more planners → `/account/planners` catalog.
- This fixes every upstream CTA in one place: landing "Build a planner", nav Planner tab, `/explore` "add camps from your planner" link, `/submit` redirect, and onboarding completion.

## Server actions

- `createPlanner` (no kid auto-seed), `duplicatePlanner` (deep-copies kids, entries, blocks, block_kids — **not** share links), `deletePlanner`.
- `createPlannerShare` refactored to upsert so edits keep the token stable.
- New `revokePlannerShareByPlanner` for the catalog's toggle-off path.
- `submitCamp` / `assignCampToWeek` / `addPlannerBlock` now require `plannerId` explicitly. All call sites updated.

## Cross-planner scoping fixes

- `fetchPlannerBlocks` + `fetchPlannerEntries` now require `plannerId` and filter by it — previously only filtered by `user_id`, causing blocks/entries to leak across planners.
- `/api/planner-entries` and `/api/planner-export` now require a `plannerId` query param.

## Nav + deprecations

- Account menu: "Share preferences" → "My planners".
- `/account/sharing` redirects to `/account/planners`. Old `ActiveSharesClient` + `ActiveSharesList` + their tests deleted.
- Deleted unused `addPlannerEntry` action (was missing `planner_id` on insert — would have failed NOT NULL on first call) and unused `fetchSharedSchedule` + `SharedScheduleRow` type.

## Tests

- 5 new tests for `MyPlannersClient` covering empty state, row rendering, on/off share treatment, delete confirm, and the new planner modal.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh account with zero planners → landing "Build a planner" CTA and nav **Planner** link both drop you into the New planner modal on `/account/planners`
- [ ] Cancel that modal → `?new=1` is stripped from the URL so refresh doesn't re-trigger
- [ ] Create planner → lands on `/planner?id=...`
- [ ] Single-planner user → clicking nav **Planner** opens their planner directly
- [ ] Multi-planner user → clicking nav **Planner** shows the catalog
- [ ] Catalog: rename inline, duplicate, delete (cannot delete the last one), toggle share on/off, edit share settings, copy link
- [ ] Verify blocks/entries do not leak across planners (create two planners, add a block to each, confirm they don't cross-render)
- [ ] Run migrations 027 and 028 against a staging DB with existing share rows — ensure dedupe + `is_default` drop succeed
- [ ] `/account/sharing` redirects to `/account/planners`

author: eltonaguiar
body:
## What changed

This PR keeps NBA and NHL slates alive in `live-monitor/sports-betting.html` when live bookmaker depth disappears.

- adds `live-monitor/nhl_nba_model_fallback.py` to synthesize multiple bookmaker-style moneyline quotes from free ESPN scoreboard data
- augments thin NBA/NHL odds in `live-monitor/api/odds_api_fetch.php` with those fallback model books before the analyzer runs
- allows the fallback bookmaker keys through paper auto-placement in `live-monitor/api/sports_bets.php`
- adds a short note in `live-monitor/sports-betting.html`
- documents the fix in `updates/2026-04-23-nba-nhl-fallback-paper-bets-pr.md`

## Why

NBA/NHL games could still disappear from the betting page even when games existed because the backend ended up with thin quote depth. The value analyzer only emits picks when a market has enough bookmakers, so sparse fallback data never became picks or paper bets.

## Impact

- NBA/NHL markets now have a free-source fallback path when live odds are thin or missing
- the page has a better chance of surfacing NBA/NHL picks instead of showing an empty board
- paper auto-placement can now track those fallback picks too

## Validation

- `python -m py_compile live-monitor/nhl_nba_model_fallback.py`
- `python live-monitor/nhl_nba_model_fallback.py --sport NBA`
- `python live-monitor/nhl_nba_model_fallback.py --sport NHL`

author: blevene
body:
## Motivation
The split-workflow chain hit GitHub's documented 3-level `workflow_run` cascade cap, verified definitively by [the GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run):

> "You can't use `workflow_run` to chain together more than three levels of workflows."

Our chain needs five cascades (Discover → Citation chain → Quality gate → Harvest → Classify → Publish). Today's real run stopped exactly at Harvest — Classify never fired, matching the docs precisely.

## Fix

### New: `pipeline.yml`
Single workflow, two jobs:

1. **`pipeline`** — one runner, six sequential steps (`Discover`/`Citation chain`/`Quality gate`/`Harvest`/`Classify`/`Publish`). Each step runs its CLI command and commits+pushes its own stage output with a stage-specific commit message. Git log still reads as a per-stage audit trail.
2. **`deploy`** — `needs: pipeline`, runs under the `github-pages` environment, stages `index.html` + `data/papers.json` + `data/osint_cyber_papers.csv` into `_site/`, uploads the artifact, deploys via `actions/deploy-pages`.

Triggers: weekly cron `Mon 03:23 UTC` + `workflow_dispatch`. Concurrency group `pipeline` with `cancel-in-progress: false`.

Running as one job (rather than multiple `needs:`-chained jobs) saves ~20–30s of runner startup per stage — ~2–3 minutes total on the full run.

### Individual stage workflows → manual-only
`discover.yml`, `citation_chain.yml`, `quality_gate.yml`, `harvest.yml`, `classify.yml`, `publish.yml` now have **only** `workflow_dispatch`. They remain as ad-hoc debug tools for re-running a single stage without walking the whole chain. The `schedule` + `workflow_run` triggers that drove the old chain are gone.

### Unchanged
- `pages.yml` (push + workflow_dispatch) — still handles non-pipeline pushes (human merges, etc.). The pipeline's own Pages deploy covers the automated path.
- `discover_manual_assist.yml` — Monday reminder for human-curated sources.
- `tag_new_papers.yml`, `rebuild_site.yml` — always were manual.

## Test plan
- [x] YAML validation across all 11 workflows.
- [x] 121 tests pass.
- [ ] After merge: manually dispatch `Pipeline` and confirm all six stages plus Pages deploy complete in one Actions run, with clean per-stage commits on `main`.
- [ ] Confirm the deployed site reflects the latest corpus (no manual intervention needed this time).

## Trade-offs

**Single job vs `needs:`-chained jobs.** I chose single-job to save runner startup time. Downside: if step 3 fails, the job UI shows "job failed at step 3", slightly less discoverable than 6 separate green/red tiles. Steps 1-2's commits are already pushed, so no data loss. Can revisit if the granular UI matters more than the startup time.

**Individual stage workflows kept.** Could also delete them to reduce count. I kept them because they're useful for debugging — `gh workflow run classify.yml` to re-tag without re-running discovery. Can prune later if they go stale.

author: sviyh
body:
## Summary
- Adds a compat patch for `adaptive.storage.framework` (by bbradson) wrapping spawn-time graphic-randomization in `Rand.PushState(thingIDNumber)` / `PopState` so it can't perturb MP's `SeedMapFinalizeLoading` seeded scope during host's `SaveAndReload`.
- `LoadPatch` is deferred via `LongEventHandler.ExecuteWhenFinished` to avoid triggering AS's `ThingExtensions` cctor before `DefDatabase` is populated.

## The bug
Adaptive Storage Framework's item-graphic code reaches `Verse.Graphic_Random.get_MatSingle` during spawn, which consumes `Verse.Rand` to pick a random material variant. Two entry points trigger this chain:

1. **`AdaptiveStorage.ThingClass.InitializeStoredThings`** — bulk re-add when a storage container itself spawns
2. **`AdaptiveStorage.ThingClass.Notify_ItemRegisteredAtCell`** — per-item hook fired by [AS's transpiler on `ThingGrid.RegisterInCell`](https://github.com/bbradson/Adaptive-Storage-Framework/blob/main/Source/AdaptiveStorage/HarmonyPatches/RegisteredAtThingGridEvent.cs) for every item spawn landing in an AS storage cell

Full stack (captured from probe instrumentation on a reproducing session):

```
Verse.Rand.Range
  Verse.Graphic_Random.get_MatSingle
    Verse.Graphic.get_Shader
      Verse.GraphicData.GraphicColoredFor
        Verse.Thing.get_DefaultGraphic
          Verse.Thing.get_Graphic
            RimWorld.MinifiedThing.get_Graphic
              AdaptiveStorage.ItemGraphicWorker.GetGraphicFor
                AdaptiveStorage.StorageRenderer.SetPrintDataDirty
                  AdaptiveStorage.StorageRenderer.AssignThingGraphic
                    AdaptiveStorage.ThingCollection.Add
                      AdaptiveStorage.ThingClass.InitializeStoredThings
                        AdaptiveStorage.ThingClass.OnSpawn
                          → Map.FinalizeLoading → SaveLoad.LoadInMainThread → SaveAndReload
```

During host's in-process `SaveAndReload` the spawn-order of these Rand calls relative to `RoomTempTracker.RegenerateEqualizeCells.Shuffle` differs from the client's fresh-process load (same 8174 things spawned, different ordering). Both pull from the same `SeedMapFinalizeLoading`-pushed seed, but at different iteration counts, producing divergent `equalizeCells` per room. Within ~120 ticks the temperature drift propagates into a `FreezeManager.DoIceMelting` `Rand.Chance` short-circuit and the main RNG stream desyncs.

## The fix
Wrap both entry points with `Rand.PushState(__instance.thingIDNumber)` / `PopState` (MP-only). Same pattern as [MP's own `SeedPawnGraphics`](https://github.com/rwmt/Multiplayer/blob/dev/Source/Client/Patches/Seeds.cs#L189-L210) for `PawnRenderer.SetAllGraphicsDirty`. The seed is stable across save/load and identical across clients, so each container picks the same graphic variant every time it spawns — no functional change.

## Why `LoadPatch` is deferred
AS's [`ThingExtensions`](https://github.com/bbradson/Adaptive-Storage-Framework/blob/main/Source/AdaptiveStorage/Utility/ThingExtensions.cs#L138-L146) has a static initializer that reads `DefDatabase<ThingDef>.AllDefsListForReading` and throws if the list is empty. Calling `MpCompatPatchLoader.LoadPatch(this)` in the mod constructor runs early enough that Harmony's patch installation on AS methods transitively triggers the cctor before `DefDatabase` is populated. The cctor throws once, the failure is cached, and every subsequent AS extension-method call rethrows `TypeInitializationException` — tens of thousands of errors per load. Deferring via `LongEventHandler.ExecuteWhenFinished` guarantees `DefDatabase` is loaded when Harmony touches AS.

## Test plan
- [x] Builds cleanly (`dotnet build Source/Multiplayer_Compat.csproj -c Release`)
- [x] Deploy to `D:\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\294100\1629973374\1.6\Assemblies\Multiplayer_Compat.dll`
- [x] Game loads cleanly (no `ThingExtensions` / `TypeInitializationException` flood)
- [x] Manual MP repro: host loads a save with AS containers + stored items, client joins. Previously reproducing `equalizeCells` shuffle desync no longer fires.
- [x] Visual inspection in SP — storage containers render correctly (deterministic graphic variants per container)

## Notes
- Does not depend on `References/AdaptiveStorageFramework.dll` — uses string-named method resolution throughout, so it stays in `Source/Mods/` rather than `Source_Referenced/`.
- Gate is `[MpCompatFor("adaptive.storage.framework")]` — patch is inert for players without AS installed.
- Companion mod `Reel's Expanded Storage` (`reel.expanded.storage`) depends on AS Framework and shares the same code path; this patch covers it implicitly.

## Summary
- Conflict-check engine no longer self-matches a just-created client against its own `identityNumber` / `name` / `registrationNumber` rows when the request carries an explicit `customerId`.
- The fix filters out `candidate.customerId == subject.customerId` on every customer-match path (ID number exact, registration number exact, name similarity). Adverse-party matching is untouched. Free-text probes (`customerId` absent) behave identically to before.

## Root Cause
`ConflictCheckService.performCheck()` queried customers by `idNumber` / `registrationNumber` / similar `name` without excluding the subject itself. When Bob ran a conflict-check against a freshly-created client (e.g. Sipho Dlamini), the subject's own record returned as an `EXISTING_CLIENT` match at 100% similarity, flipping the result to `CONFLICT_FOUND`.

## Fix
- Added `isSubjectCustomer(UUID candidateId, UUID subjectCustomerId)` helper.
- Skips the subject's own row in the three customer-match paths.
- Helper returns `false` whenever `subjectCustomerId == null`, keeping the free-text probe path identical to prior behavior.

body:
## Summary

PR 4 of Plan 5 (Scout Desktop M1). Implements `@scout/desktop-preload` — the typed `contextBridge` that exposes the `ScoutBridge` surface from `@scout/shared` as `window.scout` to the renderer.

## What's in

- `src/build-bridge.ts` — pure factory mapping `CHANNEL` entries into a `ScoutBridge` implementation backed by `ipcRenderer.invoke` / `ipcRenderer.on`. Extracted so the bridge can be unit-tested without Electron.
- `src/preload.ts` — thin wrapper calling `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('scout', bridge)`. No side effects beyond that single call.
- `src/window.d.ts` — global augmentation declaring `window.scout: ScoutBridge`. PR 5 consumes it from the renderer.
- `package.json` build script emits `dist/preload.cjs` (CJS is required by Electron's sandboxed preload).
- `tsconfig.json` targets CommonJS emit.
- `main/src/main.ts` resolves `preloadPath` at `packages/preload/dist/preload.cjs` — the "preload not found" warning introduced in PR 3 disappears once preload is built.
- 13 new preload tests (28 expects). Total workspace: 60/60 pass (shared 28 + main 19 + preload 13).

## "Not implemented" behaviour

Channels without main-side handlers reject on `invoke` with Electron's native "No handler registered for …" error. This is the expected "not-implemented" state for PR 4. Main handlers (vault, discord, worker, detect, app) land in PRs 6-10 and progressively light up the surface without touching the preload again.

## Deviations

- `module: CommonJS` + `ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` in the preload `tsconfig.json`. Using `Node16` without `"type": "module"` caused TS1479 when importing the ESM `@scout/shared`; Bun bundles ESM → CJS at build time, so TS just needs to accept the import shape.
- `IpcSubset` interface with explicit method signatures instead of `Pick<typeof ipcRenderer, …>`. Electron's `on` returns `IpcRenderer` (for chaining), which makes direct `Pick` awkward to satisfy in hand-rolled test fakes.
- Event handler uses `...args: unknown[]` with a localised cast — necessary to satisfy the generic Electron listener signature while keeping the rest of the bridge strictly typed.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun install` succeeds
- [ ] `bun run lint` — 0 errors / 0 warnings
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` — green across shared, main, preload
- [ ] `bun run test` — 60 pass (28 shared + 19 main + 13 preload)
- [ ] `bun run --cwd packages/preload build` — produces `dist/preload.cjs`, contains `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld`, no ESM `import` statements
- [ ] `bun run --cwd packages/main build` — still green
- [ ] `bun run format` — Prettier clean

## Read-only invariant

Confirmed. No preload method performs network, filesystem, or process operations. The preload is a bridge only — all side effects belong to main. The exposed surface forbids renderer-initiated external writes by design.

author: alliscode
body:
## Summary

When an agent is served by `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry.Hosting`, every outgoing OpenAI Responses-API request now carries a `foundry-hosting/agent-framework-dotnet/{version}` segment in its `User-Agent` header — alongside the existing `Azure.AI.Projects.Agents/...` and `MEAI/...` segments.

## Approach — polyfill at the `ResponsesClient` boundary

When `AgentFrameworkResponseHandler` resolves an agent (the only context where we KNOW we are hosted), it calls a new `TryApplyUserAgent(AIAgent)` helper that mirrors the existing `ApplyOpenTelemetry(AIAgent)` pattern. `TryApplyUserAgent`:

1. Walks `agent.GetService<IChatClient>()` then `chatClient.GetService(meaiResponsesChatClientType)` to find MEAI's internal `OpenAIResponsesChatClient` instance.
2. If found, reflectively swaps the private `_responseClient` field with a `DelegatingResponsesClient` wrapper.

The wrapper subclasses `OpenAI.Responses.ResponsesClient` and overrides every `RequestOptions`-accepting public-virtual protocol method (Create/Get/Delete/Cancel + GetInputTokenCount + CompactResponse + GetResponseInputItemCollectionPage, both sync and async — 14 overrides total). Each override augments the per-call `RequestOptions` with a `HostedAgentUserAgentPolicy` and delegates to the inner `ResponsesClient`.

The OpenAI SDK's `internal CreateResponseStreamingAsync(CreateResponseOptions, RequestOptions)` and `GetResponseStreamingAsync(GetResponseOptions, RequestOptions)` (which MEAI binds via reflection) bottom out in calls to the public-virtual non-streaming overloads via virtual dispatch on `this` — so streaming traffic is covered without overriding any non-virtual member.

The wrapper accepts any `ResponsesClient`-derived inner — both Foundry's `ProjectResponsesClient` and the native OpenAI `ResponsesClient` — and preserves the inner's full pipeline (Transport, RetryPolicy, NetworkTimeout, OrganizationId / ProjectId / UserAgentApplicationId, custom policies) because every override delegates to the inner instance.

Idempotency: `TryApplyUserAgent` is a no-op when the agent has no `IChatClient`, when the chat client is not backed by MEAI's `OpenAIResponsesChatClient`, or when the inner `_responseClient` is already a `DelegatingResponsesClient`.

## What's NOT covered

`FoundryAgent.CreateConversationSessionAsync` makes a direct call to `ProjectConversationsClient.CreateConversation` that does not flow through MEAI's chat client. That single bootstrap call does not carry the supplement; chat invocations on the same agent (which are the dominant traffic) DO.

## Validation

- 16 new unit tests in `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry.UnitTests` cover streaming AND non-streaming paths, retry policy preservation, `OrganizationId` / `ProjectId` / `UserAgentApplicationId` pass-through, idempotency, all 14 protocol-method overrides via a `[Theory]`, native `OpenAI.ResponsesClient` (not just `ProjectResponsesClient`), and reflection guards for MEAI / OpenAI SDK shape drift.
- One end-to-end test (`HostedOutboundUserAgentTests`) spins up a real ASP.NET Core `TestServer` with `AddFoundryResponses(agent)` + `MapFoundryResponses()`, sends an inbound `POST /responses` as the Foundry runtime would, and asserts the OUTBOUND HTTP request from inside the hosted environment carries the supplement. Proves the full pipeline: inbound HTTP → `AgentFrameworkResponseHandler` → `TryApplyUserAgent` → wrapper swap → MEAI invocation → outbound transport.
- All 380 unit tests pass on net10.0.

## Cleanup

Removes earlier-iteration code that did not belong in the final design:

- `FoundryHostingExtensions.AddHostedAgentTelemetry(AIProjectClientOptions)` extension method (was never invoked).
- `HostedUserAgentPolicy` private class (replaced by the polyfill mechanism).
- `AgentFrameworkUserAgentMiddleware` and its `app.UseMiddleware<>()` registration in `MapFoundryResponses` — inbound-side User-Agent decoration was not the intended scope; only outbound matters.
- `HostedAgentContext.cs` (the cross-package static signal is no longer needed; the supplement is a `static readonly` inside the policy that only runs when `TryApplyUserAgent` swaps the wrapper in).
- `RequestOptionsExtensions.ToRequestOptions(this CancellationToken, bool)` extension method (no callers anywhere in `dotnet/src` or `dotnet/samples`).
- Updates two error messages in `AgentFrameworkResponseHandler.cs` that referenced `AddAIAgent(...)` (which lives in `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting`, not `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry.Hosting`) to point users to the correct registration APIs.
- Reverts an unrelated whitespace change in `Agent_Step25_ToolboxServerSideTools/Program.cs`.

The net effect: the PR now does exactly one thing — decorate outgoing Responses-API requests from a hosted agent with the foundry-hosting User-Agent supplement. No inbound header manipulation, no other side effects.

### Contribution Checklist

- [x] The code builds clean without any errors or warnings
- [x] The PR follows the [Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] All unit tests pass, and I have added new tests
- [ ] **Is this a breaking change?** No.

body:
## Summary

- `trigger_sync` was acquiring `_sync_lock`, setting `_sync_running=True`, then **releasing the lock** before the background task started
- Two concurrent requests could both get through during that window, both queue a `_run_sync` task, and both return "Sync started"

## Fix

- `trigger_sync` now only reads `_sync_running` as a fast guard — no lock manipulation
- `_run_sync` is the sole owner of `_sync_lock`: acquires on entry, releases in `finally`
- The lock still prevents any two `_run_sync` executions from overlapping; at worst a second queued task silently exits on the `acquire(blocking=False)` check

author: ddrdushy
body:
## Summary

Fourth promotion from `_gaps.md` (A2). First security-pile entry to ship.

- **Server-side policy validator** — min 10 chars, class-of-3 (Unicode-aware so Sinhala/Tamil passphrases work), OBVIOUSLY_WEAK literal set, not-the-user's-email-local-part, not-the-user's-name. Pure helpers in `apps/api/src/modules/identity/password-policy.ts`.
- **HIBP k-anonymity breach check** — SHA-1 first-5 → `api.pwnedpasswords.com/range/<5>` with `Add-Padding: true`, 1500ms timeout, **fails open** on any error. `PASSWORD_BREACH_CHECK_DISABLED=true` env short-circuits for air-gapped deploys.
- **Wired into `POST /auth/signup`** — policy runs before `hashPassword` so signup can't be used as a free argon2 oracle. Failures return 400 `WEAK_PASSWORD` with `reasons: string[]` for bullet-render.
- **New `POST /auth/change-password`** — session-gated, 5/10min/IP on top of global limiter. Verifies current password, rejects `SAME_PASSWORD` no-op, runs full policy gate on new password. After update: destroys every session for this user (incl. current) + mints a fresh session for this tab — boots an attacker's parallel session without signing the legitimate user out of the tab they just saved from.
- **Web UI** — `PasswordStrengthHint` live tick-list mirroring server checks on signup + new `/app/settings/password` page. `ApiError.reasons` surface as bulleted list under WEAK_PASSWORD error banner. Settings card added with KeyRound icon.
- **Docs** — roadmap row #49, `_status.md` paragraph, `_gaps.md` A2 deleted (parking lot now 42 items).

Deferred: password-reuse prevention (needs `password_history` + retention), forced rotation (NIST argues against), admin-driven reset (belongs to team-admin console).

Zero schema / migration / new DB table. One new route, two pure helpers, three new web files.

## Test plan
- [ ] Sign up with `password` → 400 WEAK_PASSWORD with reasons list rendered as bullets under the banner.
- [ ] Sign up with a 10-char Unicode passphrase (e.g. `සූර්ය123!` if available) → class-of-3 passes.
- [ ] Sign up with email local part as password → identity guard fires.
- [ ] Sign up with a known-breached password (`Password123!`) → HIBP match returns WEAK_PASSWORD with reasons.
- [ ] Sign up with `PASSWORD_BREACH_CHECK_DISABLED=true` → HIBP skipped, only policy checks apply.
- [ ] Sign up with network to HIBP blocked → fails open, signup succeeds if other checks pass.
- [ ] Change password: wrong current → WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD.
- [ ] Change password: same as current → SAME_PASSWORD.
- [ ] Change password: weak new → WEAK_PASSWORD with reasons.
- [ ] Change password successfully → success banner, current tab stays logged in, a second browser session for the same user gets signed out on next request.
- [ ] Hit `/auth/change-password` > 5× in 10min from same IP → RATE_LIMITED.
- [ ] Typecheck baselines held: api 27, web 10, db 1.

author: kitplummer
body:
## Summary

First `v0.9.0-rc.1` tag-triggered release workflow failed at the `cargo publish` verify step on `peat-schema`:

```
clang: error: invalid linker name in argument '-fuse-ld=mold'
error: could not compile `libc` (build script) due to 1 previous error
error: failed to verify package tarball
```

Root cause: `.cargo/config.toml` pins the linker to `-fuse-ld=mold` for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. `ci.yml` installs `mold clang libdbus-1-dev` in every job that compiles, but `release.yml`'s publish job was only installing `protobuf-compiler`. `cargo publish` runs a verify-compile step (between packaging and uploading), which hit the missing linker.

## Fix

Expand the release.yml system-deps apt-get to match ci.yml: `protobuf-compiler mold clang libdbus-1-dev`.

## Impact on the failed tag

The verify step failed *before* the crates.io upload happened, so nothing landed on the index — no yank required. The `v0.9.0-rc.1` tag I pushed earlier has been deleted (both local and origin); once this merges I'll re-tag and exercise the pipeline.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green
- [ ] After merge: push `v0.9.0-rc.1`, workflow completes end-to-end

author: jankepinski
body:
## Summary

Splits each peer-dep-coupled ecosystem group in [.github/dependabot.yml](.github/dependabot.yml) into two variants:

- `<name>-major` — bundles major bumps that must ship together because of strict peer deps (e.g. `vitest` + `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `@typescript-eslint/parser` + `eslint-plugin`, `marked` + `marked-terminal`).
- `<name>-minor` — bundles minor + patch for the same ecosystem (auto-merge friendly).

Follow-up to #28, where a major `vitest` bump broke CI because `@vitest/coverage-v8` was not bumped together. With this config, both packages would have landed in a single `vitest-major` PR from the start.

### Why split instead of one group with all update-types

Keeping majors in their own PR:
- Preserves the breaking-change signal in the changelog (squash commit title still reads `chore(deps): bump X major ...`).
- Keeps review focused — one major ecosystem bump per PR, not mixed with unrelated minors.
- Prevents a stuck major migration from blocking unrelated minor/patch updates in the same ecosystem.

Added a top-of-file comment explaining the rationale so the pattern is not cargo-culted when new ecosystems are added later.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML parses (Dependabot validates it on next scheduled run; GitHub also lints the file on push)
- [ ] Next weekly Dependabot run produces the expected split (major bumps in `<name>-major` PR, minor/patch in `<name>-minor` PR)

body:
Closes #280
Closes #283

## What changed

### #280 — Complete select-winners API
- **Strict per-method schemas** via `zod` discriminated union — each method gets its own validated shape
- **`random`** — Fisher-Yates shuffle, respects `count` param, capped at `maxWinners`
- **`manual`** — accepts only `entryIds` (UUID array); validates all IDs belong to the post; rejects unknown IDs with clear error; deduplicates; caps at `maxWinners`
- **`merit_based`** — ranks eligible entries by burn count desc, entry age asc as tiebreaker
- **`firstcome`** — selects earliest `count` entries (already ordered by `createdAt asc`)
- **Duplicate prevention** — existing winners are excluded from eligible pool before selection
- **Consistent post status + notifications** — single `$transaction` marks entries `isWinner`, upserts `PostWinner` rows, sets post `status: completed`, and creates `giveaway_win` notifications for each winner

### #283 — Align wallet APIs with Stellar sync model
- `GET /api/wallet/balance` — normalized response: `{ balance, assets, transactions, lastSync, simulated }`; `?simulated=false` placeholder for future on-chain Stellar asset fetch
- `POST /api/wallet/fund` — accepts `simulated` flag (default `true`); `simulated=false` returns `501` stub for on-chain path; response includes `lastSync`
- `POST /api/wallet/withdraw` — same `simulated` flag pattern; response includes `lastSync`
- `GET /api/wallet/transactions` — adds `lastSync` field so clients can implement interval/focus refresh without blind polling

body:
### 💡 What
Added missing `aria-label`, descriptive `title` tooltips, and explicit `focus-visible` styling to the Theme Toggle and Mobile Menu Toggle buttons in the main Desktop Navbar. The new strings are fully integrated with the `react-i18next` configuration across all 4 supported languages.

### 🎯 Why
Icon-only interactive elements lack descriptive context for screen readers and can be difficult to discern for users relying on keyboard navigation. This change improves accessibility and discoverability.

### 📸 Before/After
**Before:** The theme and mobile menu toggles were only recognizable visually and lacked a focus ring when navigating via the `Tab` key.
**After:** Both buttons now feature an outline ring on focus (`focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-[#C69320]`) and announce their actions to assistive technologies via translated `aria-label` attributes.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Added `aria-label` to visually hidden/icon-only controls.
- Enhanced keyboard operability with highly visible focus rings.
- Expanded `lib/i18n.ts` translations for the new accessibility labels.

author: ovasylenko
body:
💡 **What:** Replaced a synchronous `.entry().or_insert_with()` call on `DashMap` with a read-lock fast path using `.get().map_or_else(...)` in `orch8-api/src/webhooks.rs`.
🎯 **Why:** The replay-protection cache eagerly acquired a write lock on the underlying `DashMap` shard on every single incoming webhook. This serialized requests mapped to the same shard unnecessarily, as the cache for a given webhook slug usually already exists.
📊 **Impact:** Significantly reduces write-lock contention on the hot path for webhook ingestion, allowing for higher concurrent throughput without blocking.
🔬 **Measurement:** Verify with high-concurrency payload loads against `POST /webhooks/{slug}`; throughput should remain steady without latency spikes caused by contention. Tested using `cargo test -p orch8-api` and clean linting via `cargo clippy`. Added relevant learnings to `.jules/bolt.md`.

author: skialpine
body:
## Summary
Four cleanups to quiet clang-tidy / clazy noise in `src/main.cpp`:

1. **Platform-scope `qtscalebletransport.h`** — moved the include into the same `#if/#else` block that already guards `corebluetoothscalebletransport.h`, so iOS/macOS builds (which use CoreBluetooth at `main.cpp:1360`) no longer pull in a header only referenced inside the `#else` branch at `main.cpp:1363`. Added `// IWYU pragma: keep` on both branches so clangd's include-cleaner doesn't re-flag either side when analysis runs on the "off" platform.
2. **`const auto entries`** at the SAW learning lookup (line 624) — silences `clazy-range-loop-detach`. The subsequent `for (const auto& e : entries)` was iterating a non-const lvalue, hitting `QList::begin()`'s non-const overload and forcing a COW detach.
3. **`engine.rootObjects().constFirst()`** at lines 1620 and 2120 — fixes `clazy-detaching-temporary`. `rootObjects()` returns a fresh `QList` and calling `.first()` on it returns a non-const reference into a temporary; `constFirst()` returns a const reference without triggering detach.

No behavioural change — the `#else`-branch QtScaleBleTransport use at line 1363 and the CoreBluetooth use at line 1360 were already platform-gated; only the include was un-gated.

## Test plan
- [ ] Build Debug + Release on both macOS and Windows, confirm no new warnings.
- [ ] iOS/macOS: QtScaleBleTransport is no longer compiled (already was effectively dead code, just less noisy now).
- [ ] Non-Apple platforms (Linux / Android / Windows): `QtScaleBleTransport` is instantiated at `main.cpp:1363` exactly as before.
- [ ] Shot save flow still records SAW learning entries (the range-loop at line 630 still runs, just without the COW detach).
- [ ] App startup and shutdown still work — `RelayClient::setWindow()` and the `shuttingDown` QML property still get set.

author: jicowan
body:
## Summary

- **Persists per-run / per-suite cost at orchestrator completion**: `benchmark_runs.total_cost_usd`, `loadgen_cost_usd`, and `test_suite_runs.total_cost_usd` are stamped once using the pricing row current at that moment. Freezes historical accuracy and makes aggregates trivial SUMs.
- **Hero rows gain a 5th "Total Cost" metric** on Run Detail and Suite Results. `HeroBlock` auto-scales its grid to 5 columns when 5 metrics are passed.
- **Dashboard stats endpoint** (`GET /api/v1/dashboard/stats`) replaces the client-side tallies that had four preexisting bugs (100-row cap, suites excluded, wrong success-rate denominator). Adds a `TOTAL SPEND` card and a 14-day `cost_per_day` series that feeds a cost overlay on the ActivityPulse hover.
- **ModelCache stats endpoint** (`GET /api/v1/model-cache/stats`) replaces the page's client-side row counts which regressed after PRD-36 paginated the list.

## Design note — suite cost

The initial PRD specced a `SUM(total_cost_usd)` rollup from child `benchmark_runs`. During implementation I discovered `scenario_results` doesn't reference `benchmark_runs` — suites store scenario metrics directly on the scenario row and never create per-scenario `benchmark_runs`. Since all scenarios share a single model deployment, the suite's own `started_at → completed_at` span captures the full billable EC2 lifetime. So suite cost is computed the same way as single-run cost (hourly × span / 3600), which is both simpler and more accurate than the impossible rollup.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` passes (7 new unit tests: DashboardStats, ModelCacheStats, computeRunCost happy path / missing pricing / failed run / in-flight)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` + `vite build` clean
- [x] Deployed to prod. Started a benchmark; DB shows `total_cost_usd=$1.08` and `loadgen_cost_usd=$0.53` on the completed run
- [x] Dashboard `TOTAL SPEND` card + ActivityPulse tooltip reflect new cost; success rate denominator now excludes in-flight runs; suite runs count in totals
- [x] Run Detail hero shows 5-column grid with $X.XX in the `Total Cost` cell
- [x] One-off backfill applied to 293 historical runs + 9 suites; `GET /dashboard/stats` returns `total_cost_usd=$1172.99` (was $0 pre-backfill)

### B1 — `key` + `keyProvider` mutually exclusive (`scheme.rb:85`)
Rails raises `Errors::Configuration` when both are passed. TS previously accepted both silently. Added check to `_validate()`.

### B2 — `compressor` + `encryptor` mutually exclusive (`scheme.rb:87`)
Rails raises `Errors::Configuration` when both are passed. Added check to `_validate()`.

### B3 — `key:` auto-wrapped in `DerivedSecretKeyProvider` (`scheme.rb:90–93`)
Rails lazily resolves `key_provider` via `key_provider_from_key` when `key:` is set. The `keyProvider` getter now returns `new DerivedSecretKeyProvider(key)` when `key` was passed and no explicit `keyProvider` was given.

### B4 — `deterministic:` auto-wired to `DeterministicKeyProvider` (`scheme.rb:96–99`)
Rails creates `DeterministicKeyProvider.new(config.deterministic_key)` when `deterministic:` is set and no explicit provider/key is given. The `keyProvider` getter now returns this when `config.deterministicKey` is configured.

## Test plan

- [x] Validation tests: both new `ConfigError` cases throw
- [x] `keyProvider` getter: resolves to `DerivedSecretKeyProvider` from `key:`, `DeterministicKeyProvider` from `deterministic: true` + config, `undefined` when nothing is set
- [x] `pnpm tsc --noEmit` clean

## Summary

- Adds `UPDATE_PROJECT` lifecycle action with its own switch arm that only blocks `OFFBOARDED` (terminal) — every other lifecycle (PROSPECT / ONBOARDING / ACTIVE / DORMANT / OFFBOARDING) is permitted.
- Routes `ProjectFieldService.validateCustomerLink` (called from `ProjectService.updateProject` when the PUT body carries a `customerId`) to `UPDATE_PROJECT` instead of `CREATE_PROJECT`.
- `CREATE_PROJECT` semantics are **unchanged** — it still blocks PROSPECT / OFFBOARDING / OFFBOARDED at actual matter-creation time (`ProjectFieldService.resolveCustomerName`, `CustomerProjectService.linkCustomerToProject`).

## Root cause

`PUT /api/projects/{id}` (Save Custom Fields on a matter) with the existing `customerId` in the body re-ran the **creation** guard. For Sipho Dlamini (PROSPECT) this threw `"Cannot create project for customer in PROSPECT lifecycle status"` even though the matter was already created. The guard was intended for net-new project creation, not routine updates.

## Fix shape

**Option A-2** (new action) — `CREATE_PROJECT` is used at two layers (actual create + every update carrying `customerId`), so splitting its switch arm would silently permit PROSPECT project creation which is a separate business decision. Instead, introduced a dedicated `UPDATE_PROJECT` action for the update path. Mirrors the L-56 / L-60 "only OFFBOARDED blocks" shape.
